title: Ripken, Hill part O's buy-in team
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Ripken, Hill part O's buy-in team

 January 31, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 718
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Cal Ripken Jr. and Grant Hill are part of the investor group that has agreed to buy the Baltimore Orioles, and so are former New York Mayor Michael Bloomberg and former Baltimore Mayor Kurt Schmoke.The group is headed by Baltimore native David Rubenstein, co-founder of the Carlyle Group. Additional investors were revealed in a news release Wednesday announcing the agreement between Rubenstein and the Angelos family.
"I am excited to once again be a part of the Orioles organization and I thank David for including me in the ownership group," Ripken said in a statement. "The Orioles have been a part of my life since I was a child, and this is a special day."
The Angelos family has run the team for the past three decades and is selling a control stake in the team to Rubenstein for $1.725 billion.
"I am grateful to the Angelos family for the opportunity to join the team I have been a fan of my entire life. I look forward to working with all the Orioles owners, players and staff to build upon the incredible success the team has achieved in recent seasons," Rubenstein said. "Our collective goal will be to bring a World Series trophy back to the city of Baltimore. To the fans I say: We do it for you and can't do it without you."
John Angelos, the club's current chairman, will remain as a senior adviser.
"I am personally committed to helping David and his partners take the franchise to the next level," Angelos said. "We think this transaction is great for Major League Baseball and great for the city of Baltimore and Maryland. We are thankful to the fans and supporters cheering on the O's as we reached this important goal — and who will be with us celebrating more success to come."
Rubenstein's investment team includes Ripken and Hill, who in addition to being Hall of Famers in baseball and basketball have ties to the extended area. Ripken, of course, is an Orioles legend who was born in Havre de Grace, Maryland. Hill is from northern Virginia, not far from Washington.
Other members of the investment group include Bloomberg, Schmoke, Ares Management co-founder Michael Arougheti, Ares Credit Group co-heads Mitchell Goldstein and Michael Smith, and Cognosante founder Michele Kang, who also owns the Washington Spirit of the NWSL.
The sale is subject to a full vote of Major League Baseball ownership and must receive 75% approval.
The Angelos family has been in control of the Orioles since 1993, when Peter Angelos purchased the team for $173 million. Angelos' son John is the team's current chairman, and the Orioles recently reached a deal on a new lease extension at Camden Yards.
"Governor Moore, the Maryland Stadium Authority, and the entire Moore-Miller Administration send their congratulations to Baltimore native David Rubenstein, Michael Bloomberg, Kurt Schmoke, Mike Arougheti, NBA legend Grant Hill, and Maryland native and Orioles legend Cal Ripken Jr. on their deal to purchase the Baltimore Orioles. The governor looks forward to continuing the strong relationship between the State of Maryland and the Baltimore Orioles," said Carter Elliott, a spokesman for Maryland Gov. Wes Moore.
"Governor Moore would like to thank the Angelos family for their contributions to the Orioles community and this storied franchise. Keeping the Orioles in Baltimore for the long term was a key priority for this administration and we are proud that this transaction won't change that."
The Angelos family will keep a significant investment in the team.
"When I took on the role of chair and CEO of the Orioles, we had the objective of restoring the franchise to elite status in major league sports, keeping the team in Baltimore for years to come, and revitalizing our partnership group," John Angelos said. "This relationship with David Rubenstein and his partners validates that we have not only met but exceeded our goals."
The Orioles won 101 games last season, their most since 1979, and their future is bright thanks to young stars Adley Rutschman and Gunnar Henderson — as well as a farm system that has remained loaded even as top prospects moved on to the big leagues.
The team's low payroll has been a sore spot with fans, but this sale offers hope that the Orioles might spend aggressively enough to make the most of the impressive foundation of talent they've built in recent years.

title: Four players charged with sexual assault
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Four players charged with sexual assault

 January 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 796
 Words 

 Read News Document

 NHL players Carter Hart of the Philadelphia Flyers, Michael McLeod and Cal Foote of the New Jersey Devils and Dillon Dube of the Calgary Flames have been charged with sexual assault in connection with an alleged assault by several members of Canada's 2018 world junior team.Attorneys representing Hart, McLeod, Foote and Dube said Tuesday that each player has been charged with sexual assault by police in London, Ontario. They denied any wrongdoing on behalf of their clients.
Hart's lawyers, Megan Savard and Riaz Sayani, said their client is facing one count of sexual assault, adding, "He is innocent and will provide a full response to this false accusation in the proper forum, a court of law."
Legal teams representing McLeod and Dube said the players would be pleading not guilty.
"(We) will vigorously defend the case," McLeod's attorneys, David Humphrey and Seth Weinstein, said in a statement. "We ask that the public respect Mr. McLeod's privacy, and his family's privacy. Because the matter is now before the court, we will not comment further at this time."
Dube's lawyers, Louis Strezos and Kayleigh Davidson, said their client "maintains his innocence (and) will defend the allegations in court."
Foote's lawyer, Julianna Greenspan, said her client was "innocent of the charge and will defend himself against this allegation to clear his name."
"What is most critical at this time is the presumption of innocence, and the right to a fair trial that everyone in Canada is entitled to," Greenspan said in a statement emailed to The Associated Press. "As the matter is before the court, I ask that Cal's and his family's privacy be respected."
A Devils spokesperson said the organization is aware of the reports and have been told to refer all inquiries to the league. A Flyers spokesman echoed a similar sentiment, saying the team "will respond appropriately to this very serious matter when the outcomes of the investigations are made public."
"We have now become aware of the charge of sexual assault that has been laid against Dillon Dube," the Flames said in a statement. "We take this matter very seriously. Because the matter is now pending legal proceedings, we will have no further comment at this time."
The NHL was not expected to address the situation Tuesday. Commissioner Gary Bettman is set to speak at the league's upcoming All-Star Weekend.
The latest developments in the case come two days after former NHL player Alex Formenton surrendered to police to face charges. Attorney Daniel Brown said Formenton is innocent "and asks that people not rush to judgment without hearing all of the evidence."
All five players have taken leave from their current clubs over the past 10 days. Their agents have not spoken publicly since.
London police have scheduled a news conference for Monday to address the situation. A spokesperson for police told the AP by email no updates on the investigation will be provided before the news conference.
London police launched their investigation in 2022 after it was disclosed that Hockey Canada had settled a lawsuit with a woman who said she was sexually assaulted by eight members of that gold medal-winning team after a Hockey Canada Foundation fundraising gala. London is approximately halfway between Toronto and Detroit.
According to court documents, the woman, then 20, alleged that a man, identified only as "John Doe #1," took her from a bar to a hotel room and invited seven other people into the room to perform undisclosed sexual acts, intimidating her and preventing her from leaving. The woman said in the lawsuit the men directed her to take a shower and asked her to say on video that she was sober.
The woman sought $3.55 million in damages and dropped the lawsuit after reaching a settlement with Hockey Canada.
The NHL opened its own investigation in 2022 and has pledged to make those findings public. Deputy Commissioner Bill Daly last week said the league would issue a statement if and when it is appropriate.
The Flyers said Hart requested and was granted a leave of absence for personal reasons. General manager Daniel Briere declined to provide details when asked follow-up questions related to the 25-year-old No. 1 goaltender's departure.
The Devils did not give a reason when announcing McLeod and Foote were granted indefinite leaves of absence. McLeod, who turns 26 on Saturday, is in the middle of his fourth full season with the team, while Foote — son of former NHL player Adam Foote — has spent much of this season in the American Hockey League and appeared in four games for New Jersey.
The Flames said Dube was on indefinite leave to tend to his mental health. As part of their statement Tuesday, they said they "had no knowledge of pending charges at the time Dillon's request for a leave of absence was granted."
The 25-year-old Dube has played for Calgary since 2018.

title: Despite heartbreaks and mistakes, future looks bright for the Lions and Ravens
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Despite heartbreaks and mistakes, future looks bright for the Lions and Ravens

 January 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 938
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The Detroit Lions lost their huge halftime lead and the Baltimore Ravens lost both their composure and the football just inches from advancing to Super Bowl 58 next week on the Las Vegas Strip.Too bad, too, because both teams looked every bit the high-rolling risk-takers that the betting houses love.
It'll be the San Francisco 49ers and the Kansas City Chiefs instead in a rematch of the Super Bowl four years ago after Lions coach Dan Campbell lost two big gambles by going for it on fourth down in field-goal range and the Ravens frittered away their favorable odds with a series of dubious decisions that led to two end-zone turnovers, eight yellow flags and a trio of turnovers to KC's zero.
Those included Lamar Jackson's throw into triple coverage and rookie Zay Flowers' fumble at the goal line that followed a boneheaded taunting call after a big catch.
If recent history is any guide, however, one of these runners-up will heed the lessons from all their mistakes, miscues and miscalculations on championship weekend to make it to Super Bowl 59 at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans a year from now.
The 49ers were walloped 31-7 by the Philadelphia Eagles in the NFC title game last year and reached this year's Super Bowl with Brock Purdy engineering back-to-back second-half comebacks against the Packers and Lions in the playoffs.
After digging themselves a 24 — 7 halftime hole Sunday, the Niners scored on each of their first five possessions of the second half to deny the Lions their first Super Bowl appearance in franchise history.
The Chiefs are in their second straight Super Bowl after losing to the Cincinnati Bengals 27-24 in the AFC championship following the 2021 season.
So yes, there's hope for dispirited Detroit and bummed out Baltimore.
Of course, there are plenty of examples of conference runners-up who didn't parlay their breakdowns on championship weekend into a breakthrough the following season.
The Eagles looked like a team ready to atone for their 38-35 loss to Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs in Super Bowl 57 last year when they raced out to a 10-1 start this season, only to lose six of their final seven games in one of the biggest collapses in Philly sports history.
The Bengals lost to KC 23-20 in last year's AFC championship and didn't even make it back to the playoffs this time around after losing quarterback Joe Burrow to a broken wrist in November.
Neither head coach was hanging his head after his early exit, but both realized how hard it will be to get back here, much less get over that huge hump.
"The message is, 'Eyes straight ahead,'" Ravens coach John Harbaugh said. "(Keep) your chin up, your chest out, and understand what you did accomplish.'" He told Jackson to stand tall and he wasn't about to scapegoat Flowers, who had the best rookie season for a receiver in team history, for his fumble inches from the goal line.
"We coach two hands when you reach for the end zone," Harbaugh said. "He had two hands on the ball."
As for all the times the Ravens lost their composure, like when Flowers followed a long catch with a push, a taunt and a spin of the football on the grass, drawing a 15-yard penalty, Harbaugh declined to comment before he'd had a chance to see the film.
Jackson admired the Chiefs for their paucity of penalties and zero turnovers and suggested that had the Ravens played that way, they might be the ones scrambling to get Super Bowl tickets for family and friends this week.
"We were a game away from the Super Bowl," Jackson said. "We've been waiting all this time, all these moments for an opportunity like this, and we fell short. But I feel like our team is going to build. This offseason, we're going to get right, get better, grind and try to be in this position again but on the other side of victory."
The success-starved Lions appeared poised to make their first Super Bowl in franchise history when they took that 17-point halftime lead Sunday only to allow 27 straight points in a mistake-filled second half.
Detroit has a league-high 62 conversions on fourth down in Campbell's three seasons but came up short when it mattered most.
Nobody knows if kicker Michael Badgley would have made those kicks from 46 and 48 yards, but we do know this: He has converted 85% of his field goal attempts from 40-49 yards over his last three seasons.
"I don't regret those decisions," said Campbell, who has faith they'll convert it the next time.
Detroit remains the only team to play every season of the Super Bowl era without reaching the ultimate game. This looked as though it could be the breakthrough season to end that drought when Detroit won back-to-back playoff games after winning just one in the previous 56 seasons.
But the Lions must wait at least another year to have a chance at their first NFL championship since 1957.
"You've got to get your heart ripped out" sometimes, Campbell said, "which we did. And it's a lesson learned."
Still, he knows there are no guarantees and that sometimes second chances just don't come around.
"I told those guys, this may have been our only shot," Campbell said. "Do I think that? No. Do I believe that? No. But I know how hard it is to get here. I'm well aware, and it's going to be twice as hard to get back to this point next year than it was this year. That's the reality."
Like Harbaugh does, Campbell trusts that if his team does get another chance, it will end up on the winning side next time.

title: Lions ride 1-2 punch past Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions ride 1-2 punch past Easton

 January 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 850
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Queen Anne's County High's Bea Holthaus and Laila Coles are one of the top freshmen combinations to hit the North Bayside hardwood in a long, long time.But Lions girls' head basketball coach Mike Kern knows there are going to be nights when his team isn't at its best.
Tuesday was shaping up to be one of those nights, as Easton went on an 8-0 run to open the second half for one-point lead. But that only seemed to wake up the Lions, who proceeded to go on a 17-3 tear to close the third quarter on the way to a 53-42 victory.
"We're young," said Kern, whose team improved to 14-0 overall, 12-0 North Bayside. "We're playing in a tough environment. We're going to have these games where we don't play our best. But will still overcome. I'm proud of them for overcoming."
Holthaus, who had a game-high 25 points to go with 13 rebounds and five blocked shots, and Coles (16 points) helped Queen Anne's build a 24-17 halftime lead.
But Easton (7-8, 7-5), which lost to the Lions by 32 on Jan. 2 in Centreville, erased that deficit in the opening two minutes of the second half. Addison Chandler (10 points) buried a 3-pointer. Sisi Sama (10 points) scored inside, hit one of two free throws, then drove the lane for a basket and a 25-24 Warriors lead.
"I thought Easton came out a little hungrier than we were tonight," Kern said. "And they out-rebounded us, which is a little disappointing. But they were going hard to the ball. I think Easton deserves a lot of credit. They did a great job on the boards. And they were getting second and third opportunities, and that's what kept them in the game. We've got to do better."
The Lions may not have done better immediately on the glass, but they improved on the scoreboard. After Kern called time with 5:45 remaining in the third, Queen Anne's returned to the floor and took control of the game, outscoring the Warriors 25-5 over the next 7-plus minutes.
Leading the charge was Holthaus, who accounted for 17 points in the surge, which included burying three baseline jumpers and a 5-for-6 effort from the foul line.
"Bea is just a phenomenal athlete," Kern said. "She's sees the court really well. She makes everybody around her better. She's very unselfish. She can go inside. She can go outside. She's an all-around player. We're lucky to have her for four years."
The same can be said of Coles, who in addition to her 16 points, totaled seven steals, five assists and five rebounds.
"Her (Holthaus) and Coles both as freshmen are just going to be amazing kids coming up," Easton head coach Lesley Staehli said.
And while Holthaus and Coles proved a formidable one-two punch, the Warriors hurt themselves with a 10-for-25 performance from the free-throw line.
"We missed 15 free throws," Staehli said. "Had we made some of them, and then stopped the turnovers; taken care of the ball a little bit better (against Coles). And then shutting Bea down a little bit with hands in her face with her shot."
Queen Anne's 17-3 surge to close the third, and an 8-2 burst to open the fourth gave it a 49-30 cushion with 6:21 remaining. Easton made the score more respectable as Chandler's third 3-pointer of the game started a 12-4 Warriors' game-ending run.
"We did well I thought considering we got blown out the last time we played them," said Staehli, who got a team-high 11 points from Kate Adelman and 10 from Serenity Velez. "But we're going to be working on our foul shots."
CAMBRIDGE-SD 58 NORTH DORCHESTER 13CAMBRIDGE — LeAsia Todd had 19 points, 13 rebounds and four blocked shots as the Vikings won their third straight.
Tejanae Ballin scored 11 points and Damiya Henry had 10 for Cambridge-South Dorchester (8-4, 7-4).
NORTH CAROLINE 65 KENT COUNTY 39RIDGELY — Chloe Escoe had a team-high 16 points and Selaya Garrison finished with 12 to lead the Bulldogs (8-5, 6-4). Ashley Kercheval added 10 points for North Caroline.
SSPP 55 SALISBURY SCHOOL 19SALISBURY — Morgan Quade scored 27 points and Avery McCall had 16 to pace the Sabres in an Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference game.
ST. MICHAELS 46 CRISFIELD 45ST. MICHAELS — Brooke Reilly scored 17 points and Madi White delivered a 14-point effort Monday as the Saints notched their first win of the season.
BOYS BASKETBALLEASTON 66, QUEEN ANNE'S 60EASTON — Ja'Kai Brooks finished with 21 points and Marshall Bailey had 15, leading the Warriors past the Lions and forging a second-place tie in the North Bayside.
Kyree Acree had 11 points for Easton (11-4, 10-2) which pulled even with the Lions (11-4, 10-2) in the division.
CAMBRIDGE-SD 68 NORTH DORCHESTER 56SHILOH — Koby Ennals' team-high 16 points led the unbeaten Vikings over their county rival. LaShaun Moody and Thomas Wilson each scored 13 points for Cambridge-SD (13-0, 11-0).
SSPP 76, KEY 61ANNAPOLIS — Garett Hemingway had 18 points and Robbie Cunningham dropped in 17 to fuel the Sabres in an Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association C Conference game Monday night.
Brayden Smith added 15 points for Saints Peter and Paul (7-7, 3-2).

title: STEP BY STEP
author: Bill Haufe
content:
STEP BY STEP

 January 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 763
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — James Gardner's instructions to freshman Matthew Brunner were simple."The last thing I told him before he got out on the mat: Wrestle hard. Stay aggressive. And stay off your back," Easton High's head wrestling coach said.
Brunner checked all those boxes in what was perhaps the biggest match of his young career, pinning St. Michaels' Oliver Cummings midway through the first period of Friday's final bout to seal a 39-30 victory that extended the Warriors' win streak to three.
"That's exactly what we needed," Gardner said of Brunner's fall which helped raise Easton's record to 3-8 overall and in the Bayside Conference. "I'm really happy with his outcome and his progression."
St. Michaels (0-7, 0-7) never trailed until the ninth match, when Easton's Hayden Allen won by forfeit at 157 pounds, nudging the Warriors to a 21-18 lead. The Saints regained the lead at 24-21 in the next match, as Blake Foy built a 4-0 first-period advantage before pinning Kameron Popal in 3:34 of the 165-pound bout.
But the Warriors won the three of the remaining four bouts, starting with senior Matt Svehla's 15-second fall over Andrew Moorehead at 175.
"He's been one of my most consistent wrestlers this year," Gardner said of Svehla, who has yet to lose a conference match this season. "He's still working, still trying to get better on a daily basis.
"Tonight he just knew what he needed to get done," Gardner added of Svehla. "He knew we needed more than a win. We needed a pin because I tell them every point matters. I just appreciate him as a young man and a wrestler. I wish I had him for another year."
Svehla's pin moved Easton into the lead at 27-24. Liam Lewis widened that margin to 33-24 in a swing match, when he pinned Max Reed in 1:23 at 190.
"We definitely needed the match with Liam Lewis," Gardner said. "He's normally at 170, but we pushed him up to 190. That was big."
Will Bridges picked up a forfeit at 215, drawing St. Michaels within 33-30, and giving the Saints a chance to either tie or win heading into the final match at 285.
But Brunner followed Gardner's instructions, getting a takedown of Cummings before turning his opponent to his back for a fall with 1:02 remaining in the first period.
"I knew I just had to go out there and do my job to get the win," Brunner said. "At first I wasn't thinking I was going to get a pin. But I went in there confident and ended up getting the pin.
"It feels amazing," said Brunner, who after having his arm raised in victory received a big smile and handshake from Gardner before getting surrounded by his celebrating teammates. "When it's down to you and you go out there and get a win, it's a big one."
St. Michaels took a 6-0 lead in the opening match, as Will Coale led 4-0 after one period, watched his lead get trimmed to 4-2 by John Seymour 40 seconds into the second before earning a reversal and notching a fall with 3 seconds left in the second period at 106.
Easton cut that deficit in half via Gabe Trise's 14-8 decision over Hudson Jones at 113. St. Michaels' Andrew Sanchez (120) answered with a 6-1 win over Jakob Barnhart, restoring the Saints' six-point cushion.
Then came four consecutive forfeits. Easton's Shawn Arnold won a forfeit at 126 to make it 9-9. St. Michaels' Jacob Jenkins took a forfeit at 132, pushing the Saints back to a 15-9 lead. After a double forfeit at 138, Easton's Adonis Schmitt won by forfeit at 144, leaving the match even at 15-all.
St. Michaels' took its final lead at 150. After a scoreless first, Easton's Teddy Antal hit a reversal for a 2-0 lead. But St. Michaels' Lane Cappa took over from there. Despite two blood stoppages, Cappa rallied for a 4-2 lead, watched Antal escape, then scored three near-fall points for a 7-3 lead. Antal closed with a takedown with 28 seconds remaining in the match, but couldn't get any closer, as Cappa hit a switch for a 9-5 final and an 18-15 Saints lead.
"We're trying to get there," said St. Michaels' first-year head coach Steve Mister, one of the most outstanding wrestlers to ever come through the Saints' program. "We're going through growing pains, but everybody does. We'll get there … sooner than later. But we did what we came to do."
Each team won four matches that were wrestled. Easton had three pinfalls to St. Michaels' two, and also picked up one more forfeit win than its county rival.

title: ROADBLOCK
author: Bill Haufe
content:
ROADBLOCK

 January 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Roadblock 
 
 1002
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs took a different route to face the Baltimore Ravens in the AFC championship game.They're going on the road.
After hosting this game five straight seasons, the No. 3 seed Chiefs had to beat Josh Allen and the Bills at Buffalo and now travel to Baltimore to face Lamar Jackson and the Ravens.
The defending Super Bowl champion Chiefs (13-6) are looking for their third Super Bowl title in five years and are trying to become the first team to repeat since Tom Brady and the New England Patriots did it in the 2003-04 seasons.
They have to get there first.
Standing in their way are the No. 1 seed Ravens, who have played their best against tough opponents. The Ravens (14-4) had 11 wins over winning teams, including nine by at least 14 points.
The Chiefs shut down Tua Tagovailoa and Miami's potent offense in the wild-card round and sneaked past the Bills in Mahomes' first career playoff game on the road.
The Ravens rolled to a 34-10 win over Houston after enjoying a first-round bye. They're 3 1/2-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook.
WHEN THE CHIEFS HAVE THE BALLThe Chiefs had the league's sixth-ranked passing offense behind Mahomes and 19th-ranked rushing attack. The Ravens gave up the fewest points per game (16.5) and were sixth against the pass and 14th against the run.
Mahomes is a magician and what he's been able to do without a legitimate No. 1 wide receiver has been impressive. The two-time NFL and Super Bowl MVP threw for 4,183 yards with 27 touchdowns, a career-high 14 interceptions and career-low 92.6 passer rating. His receivers dropped 44 passes, most in the league.
Mahomes' go-to option still is tight end Travis Kelce. The Ravens have All-Pro safety Kyle Hamilton to match up against Kelce so rookie wideout Rashee Rice, veteran Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Kadarius Toney, if he's healthy, need to step up.
Kelce had 93 catches for 984 yards and five TDs in the regular season and caught two scores last week in Buffalo. Rice had 79 receptions for 938 yards and seven TDs.
The Chiefs will rely on running back Isiah Pacheco to balance the offense. He ran for 935 yards and seven TDs in the regular season, and had 97 yards on 15 carries with one TD against the Bills last week. Baltimore's front seven led by All-Pro linebacker Roquan Smith, LB Patrick Queen and defensive tackle Justin Madubuike held Houston to 38 yards rushing last week and kept nine teams under 100 this season.
Chiefs coach Andy Reid is one of the NFL's all-time great offensive innovators and he's been known to add a few new wrinkles in big games. Injured All-Pro left guard Joe Thuney will force Reid to make some adjustments to the game plan. Ravens defensive coordinator Mike Macdonald has become a hot candidate for head coaching positions after Baltimore's defense became the first in NFL history to lead the league in fewest points allowed, sacks and turnovers.
WHEN THE RAVENS HAVE THE BALLThe Ravens led the NFL in rushing and were 21st in passing behind the dual-threat Jackson. The Chiefs gave up the second-fewest points (17.3), were fourth against the pass and 18th against the run.
Jackson is one of the league's most talented all-around offensive players so defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo's unit will have its hands full. The All-Pro QB and 2019 NFL MVP threw for 3,678 yards and 24 touchdowns and also ran for 821 yards and five scores. Jackson excelled in the biggest games this season, outplaying Brock Purdy in a rout over San Francisco and tossing five TD passes in a win over Miami that determined the AFC's No. 1 seed.
The Chiefs can expect to see a heavy dose of Gus Edwards, Justice Hill and Dalvin Cook running the ball and have to watch out for Jackson's scrambles. The trio of backs ran for 129 yards on 31 carries against Houston last week. Jackson led the way with 100 yards rushing.
Rookie Zay Flowers led Baltimore with 77 catches for 858 yards and five TDs. Jackson also has veterans Nelson Agholor and Odell Beckham Jr. Tight end Mark Andrews is expected to return from an ankle injury, giving Jackson his favorite playmaker.
All-Pro slot cornerback Trent McDuffie against Flowers, who lines up everywhere, will be a key matchup. Blocking All-Pro defensive tackle Chris Jones, who can be a game-changer, is a top priority for Baltimore's offensive line.
Jackson flourished in his first season in offensive coordinator Todd Monken's system. Spagnuolo's defense can perplex the best teams. His unit shut down Brady, Randy Moss and the undefeated Patriots when the Giants pulled off a stunning Super Bowl upset 16 years ago.
SPECIAL TEAMSTwo of the best kickers in the NFL are in this one. Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker made 33 of 35 field goals, including all five from beyond 50 yards. Ravens five-time All-Pro Justin Tucker had a down season by his standards, going 32 of 37 on field goals and missing four of five from 50-plus yards.
Ravens punter Jordan Stout had a 39.1-yard net average while Kansas City's Tommy Townsend had a 41.9-yard net average.
The Chiefs use Mecole Hardman and Richie James for returns. Hardman had the longest punt return at 50 yards and James had the longest kick return at 31. Devin Duvernay is a solid returner for the Ravens. He returned a punt 70 yards.
COACHINGReid is a likely future Hall of Famer. He already has two Super Bowl rings and is the winningest coach in the history of the Chiefs and Eagles.
Ravens coach John Harbaugh, a Reid disciple, also has a Hall of Fame-caliber resume. He's only had two losing seasons in 16 years with Baltimore and led it to one Super Bowl title.
INTANGIBLESReid and Mahomes are chasing Bill Belichick and Brady. They've got to win four more Super Bowls to match them. Jackson and the Ravens are trying to silence the playoff narrative. The Ravens were 1-3 in the postseason with Jackson before last week's dominant win. Losing this one would be a setback.

Warriors struggle, surge past Bucs

 EASTON — Two players forgot their jerseys.Another forget his stick, and still another was short one sock.
Then Easton High's ice hockey team fell behind by two goals in the first period Friday night to Kent Island.
That combination was enough for Warrior head coach Tim Nowak to issue a warning to his team.
"I said, 'You better figure it out because next week when we play Severna Park we'll be down 10-0, it won't be two," Nowak said.
Easton figured it out, and quickly, as Ethan Finlay scored a hat trick and older brother Ty Finlay had three assists and a goal — all in the second period — sparking the Warriors to a 10-4 victory at the Talbot County Community Center.
"I was like, 'Guys, you have to be ready,'" Nowak said. "You can't just show up and say, 'OK, we're playing hockey today.'"
Kent Island, now 1-7 in the Maryland Student Hockey League Eastern Conference, came out with a new look in the first period and it paid dividends. Jacob Keever converted a pass from Jayden Calisto 4:37 into the game for a 1-0 Bucs lead. Kent Island continued to keep the puck in the Easton end for much of the first period, and widened its lead to 2-0 with just over 3 minutes left when Aidan Mahaffey set up Blake Vane's goal.
"We had a different strategy," Bucs head coach Doug Wackowski said. "We were playing defense first and that was very successful through the first period and into the second. Unfortunately, kids get tired and Easton's a good team. They've got a full bench and things started going their way."
But before things started going Easton's way, Kent Island had impressed Nowak.
"I said to our guys, 'Look how they're playing,'" Nowak said. "'They're playing like structured. They're passing. You guys are trying to skate through everybody.' They (Kent Island) totally dominated us. And it wasn't just the fact they were up 2-0. They won every puck battle in the first period. I was like, 'Are we going to start doing something?'"
Blanked by Erick Long for almost 14 minutes, the Warriors finally tucked one past Kent Island's goalie with 1:08 left in the first period as David Rogers scored on Kaleb Fluharty's assist.
Then the Finlays found their groove.
The Ty-to-Ethan connection produced the tying goal 5:06 into the second period. Just 50 seconds later they connected again, putting Easton in front to stay at 3-2. Long stopped everything directed his way over the next 8-plus minutes. But with 21 seconds left in the period Shane Gunshenan and Ty Finlay set up Ethan's third goal. Ty then punctuated Easton's four-goal period with an unassisted goal 7 seconds later for a 5-2 Warrior lead.
Easton fattened its lead to 7-2 in the third as Fluharty took a Ty Finlay pass, steamed down right wing and snapped a wrist shot past Long. Just 26 seconds later Finlay scored his second goal — compliments of a Fluharty feed — against Nicole Seiler, who had taken over in net for Long.
Kent Island got back on the scoreboard with 9:29 remaining when Vane took an Abigail Mahaffey and James Biles passing combination and beat Easton goalie James Shaw (19 saves), starting his first game of the season.
Easton again responded with a quick one-two punch. Paxton Echternach scored off a Ryan LaCorte pass 21 seconds after Vane's goal. Less than a minute later, Echternach set up Nick Walters' score for a 9-3 Easton lead.
The Warriors stretched their lead to 10-3 when Bradyn Speakman and Walters set up Carson Clow's goal. Vane then fed Aidan Mahaffey on a breakaway goal for the 10-4 final with under 3 minutes remaining.
Easton, which has won three four, is 3-3 in conference play and sitting behind South River (6-1, Annapolis/Arundel/Chessie (6-1), Severna Park (7-1) and Broadneck (6-2) in the Eastern Conference. The top two teams in the conference will earn byes into the state tournament, while seeds 3 through 6 will meet in the playoffs in a bid to qualify for states.
"We're close," said Nowak, whose team lost by two goals to Annapolis/Arundel/Chessie and surrendered a goal in the final minute of an eventual 4-3 loss to Broadneck. "We're so close to being a top echelon team. But the little things are keeping us from that."
Notes: Long and Seiler combined for 25 saves.

 EASTON — Easton High boys head basketball coach Dionte Hynson thinks his team is beating the teams it should be defeating right now.More importantly, he thinks the Warriors are playing they way they should as the regular season pushes toward its latter stages.
Senior Ja'Kai Brooks scored a game-high 16 points and classmate James Warren finished with 13 Thursday night, as Easton rolled to its sixth consecutive victory — excluding its Jan. 11 forfeit to Cambridge-South Dorchester — with a 75-40 victory over North Dorchester on senior night.

Batson and Ramirez each scored four points in the paint in the third quarter as Easton began dominating inside. Bailey then converted a steal into a transition basket before Brooks took two more steals to the rim for a 19-point cushion.
"I like where I am," Hynson said. "We're always ready to play whoever wherever. We got (Queen Anne's) on Tuesday so we'll see what happens."

Jackson on list for NFL's top awards

 Lamar Jackson, Christian McCaffrey and Dak Prescott are finalists for The Associated Press 2023 NFL Most Valuable Player and Offensive Player of the Year awards.The winners will be announced at NFL Honors on Feb. 8. A nationwide panel of 50 media members who regularly cover the league completed voting before the playoffs began.
Bills quarterback Josh Allen and 49ers QB Brock Purdy also are finalists for MVP. Dolphins wide receiver Tyreek Hill and Cowboys wideout CeeDee Lamb are the other two finalists for Offensive Player of the Year.
Jackson, the 2019 MVP, threw for 3,678 yards and 24 touchdowns and also ran for 821 yards and five scores. He helped the Baltimore Ravens (14-4) finish with the best record in the league and led them to a playoff win over Houston. Jackson received 45 of 50 votes for AP first-team All-Pro.
The Ravens will host the Kansas City Chiefs (13-6) in the AFC championship game on Sunday.
Prescott had 4,516 yards passing, an NFL-best 36 TD passes and a 105.9 passer rating while leading Dallas to an NFC East title. But the Cowboys were eliminated in the wild-card round by Green Bay.
McCaffrey, a unanimous choices for AP All-Pro, led the NFL with 1,459 yards rushing and had 14 rushing TDs for San Francisco. He also had 564 yards receiving for seven scores.
Purdy, McCaffrey and the 49ers (13-5) will host the Detroit Lions (14-5) in the NFC championship game on Sunday.
The Cleveland Browns have finalists in four categories: Myles Garrett for Defensive Player of the Year; Kevin Stefanski for Coach of the Year; Joe Flacco for Comeback Player of the Year; and Jim Schwartz for Assistant Coach of the Year.
The Houston Texans have finalists for Offensive and Defensive Rookie of the Year. QB C.J. Stroud and edge rusher Will Anderson Jr., selected back-to-back with the second and third picks in the NFL draft, are aiming to make it two straight years the winners are from the same team. New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson and cornerback Sauce Gardner won the awards in 2022.
The Texans routed the Browns in a wild-card playoff before losing at Baltimore in the divisional round.
Cowboys edge Micah Parsons and cornerback DaRon Bland, Raiders edge Maxx Crosby and Steelers edge T.J. Watt join Garrett as finalists for Defensive Player of the Year.
Watt led the NFL with 19 sacks, Crosby had 14 1/2 and Garrett and Parsons each had 14. Bland set an NFL record with five interception returns for a touchdown.
Lions tight end Sam LaPorta and running back Jahmyr Gibbs, Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua and Falcons running back Bijan Robinson are finalists for Offensive Rookie of the Year along with Stroud.
Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter, Rams defensive lineman Kobie Turner, Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon join Anderson as finalists for Defensive Rookie of the Year.
Houston's DeMeco Ryans, Detroit's Dan Campbell, San Francisco's Kyle Shanahan and Baltimore's John Harbaugh are finalists for Coach of the Year along with Stefanski.
Stefanski, the 2020 winner, led the Browns to an 11-6 record despite losing Deshaun Watson and having to use four starting QBs. Ryans took the Texans from the AFC South's worst to first in his rookie season. Campbell helped Detroit capture its first division title in 30 years. Harbaugh and Shanahan led their teams to No. 1 seeds.
Schwartz guided the NFL's No. 1 ranked defense in his first season as Cleveland's defensive coordinator. Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson, Ravens defensive coordinator Mike Macdonald and offensive coordinator Todd Monken and Texans offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik also are finalists for Assistant Coach of the Year.
Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield, Rams QB Matthew Stafford, Dolphins QB Tua Tagovailoa and Bills safety Damar Hamlin join Flacco as finalists for Comeback Player of the Year.
This was the second year for the AP's weighted voting system. Voters chose a top five for MVP and top three for all other awards. For MVP, first-place votes were worth 10 points. Second through fifth-place votes were worth 5, 3, 2 and 1 points.
For all the other awards, first-place votes equaled 5 points, second were 3 and third were 1.

title: James, Embiid in U.S. player pool
author: Bill Haufe

 There are few surprises in USA Basketball's men's player pool for the Paris Olympics that was announced Tuesday, with most of the big names like LeBron James, Joel Embiid, Stephen Curry and Kevin Durant on the list.The surprise may have been who was missing.
Draymond Green, who helped the U.S. win gold at the 2016 Rio de Janeiro Games and then another title at the rescheduled Tokyo Olympics in 2021, was not among the 41 names released by USA Basketball as candidates for the team that will compete in Paris this summer in search of a fifth consecutive gold medal.
The naming of the pool is the first official phase in the process of assembling a 12-player Olympic roster that will be coached by Golden State's Steve Kerr and assisted by Miami's Erik Spoelstra, the Los Angeles Clippers' Tyronn Lue and Gonzaga's Mark Few. Team selection will be finalized this spring, with many of those decisions likely hinging upon player health and how deep their respective teams go in the NBA playoffs.
"The United States boasts unbelievable basketball talent and I am thrilled that many of the game's superstars have expressed interest in representing our country at the 2024 Olympic Summer Games," men's national team managing director Grant Hill said. "It is a privilege to select the team that will help us toward the goal of once again standing atop the Olympic podium. This challenging process will unfold over the next several months as we eagerly anticipate the start of national team activity."
The pool, which is subject to change, includes 13 players who already have Olympic gold medals — Durant has three, James and Chris Paul each have two, while Anthony Davis, Bam Adebayo, Damian Lillard, Devin Booker, James Harden, Jayson Tatum, Jimmy Butler, Jrue Holiday, Kyrie Irving and Paul George each have one.
If he plays and the U.S. wins, Durant would be the first men's player with four basketball golds.
"I will play in the Olympics," Durant adamantly said last fall at Phoenix's media day.
The other 28 players on the list are headlined by a pair who may make their Olympic debuts — Embiid and Curry among them. Both said last year that they would like to play on the Paris-bound U.S. team, though again, nothing will be finalized until their NBA seasons end.
"Definitely want to be there," Curry said last fall. "Definitely want to be on the team."
Embiid — the reigning NBA MVP, two-time scoring champion and Philadelphia star who scored 70 points Monday night — could have decided to play for France (he has dual citizenship) or even Cameroon, his birthplace, if it qualifies. He chose to play for the U.S. last fall instead.
"When he gets motivated … anything can happen," 76ers coach Nick Nurse said.
Also picked for the pool: Jarrett Allen, Paolo Banchero, Desmond Bane, Scottie Barnes, Mikal Bridges, Jaylen Brown, Jalen Brunson, Alex Caruso, Anthony Edwards, De'Aaron Fox, Aaron Gordon, Tyrese Haliburton, Josh Hart, Tyler Herro, Chet Holmgren, Brandon Ingram, Jaren Jackson Jr., Cam Johnson, Walker Kessler, Kawhi Leonard, Donovan Mitchell, Bobby Portis, Austin Reaves, Duncan Robinson, Derrick White and Trae Young.
"We get to go to Paris. We get to go do something special," said Adebayo, who got his first gold in 2021 and is expected to be part of the 2024 team. "I reflect on it and I get excited because I get an opportunity to do something special — twice."
Green had expressed some interest last year in being part of the Paris-bound team.
But the Golden State forward missed 16 games spanning mid-December to mid-January while serving what was originally called an indefinite suspension for striking Phoenix center Jusuf Nurkić in the face. Green said he considered retiring and sought counseling before he was reinstated.
Players not in the pool aren't exactly ineligible to make the Olympic team; while it is a long shot, it has happened before. San Antonio's Keldon Johnson was not one of the 57 players USA Basketball announced in March 2021 as a pool member, but he was eventually selected for the Tokyo Games team and won a gold medal under Spurs coach Gregg Popovich.
That said, it took an extraordinary set of circumstances for Johnson to be in that position.
He was on the U.S. Select Team that practiced against the Olympic team to help it prepare for the Tokyo Games, got promoted to the national team in part because some players were still taking part in the NBA Finals, then got added to the Olympic roster (along with JaVale McGee) when Bradley Beal and Kevin Love — both of whom had been picked for the team — had to drop out late in the process.

title: Noskova adds yet another surprise down under
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Noskova adds yet another surprise down under

 January 20, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 683
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Iga Swiatek's No. 1 ranking, four Grand Slam titles and 18-match winning streak were no help against big-hitting teen Linda Noskova at the Australian Open.After crouching at the baseline and covering her face when she closed out the 3-6, 6-3, 6-4 third-round victory over Swiatek on Saturday, the 50th-ranked Noskova said: "I didn't really think that it would end up like this."
Who possibly could have? Noskova, after all, is making her debut at the year's first Grand Slam tournament and had only two match wins at all majors until a week ago. Plus, it had been a quarter of a century since any teenager eliminated the WTA's No. 1 player at Melbourne Park (Amelie Mauresmo defeated Lindsay Davenport in 1999).
Then again, pedigree and past performance seem to mean little to nothing so far this year, setting up a Week 2 that features a bunch of new players and storylines.
"For sure," Swiatek said, "I wish I could have played a little bit better."
That's been a familiar refrain. Even before Swiatek's exit, only 12 seeded women reached the third round, equaling last year's French Open for the fewest at a Slam since the 32-seed format was introduced in 2001.
"We have, like, a deep pool of players who can beat anybody on the given day. I think that's what makes them more dangerous," said Victoria Azarenka, a two-time champion in Melbourne. "The consistency sometimes can be on and off. You don't know which player you're going to get on which day."
The first three rounds were calmer for the men; Novak Djokovic led nine of the top 10 seeds safely through. (No. 8 Holger Rune lost to Arthur Cazaux, a 21-year-old from France who is the first non-Australian men's wild-card entry in 30 years to get to the fourth round.)
Of the eight women left in the top half of the bracket, only Azarenka has been to a major final, and no one is currently in the Top 10. No. 12 Zheng Qinwen, a 21-year-old from China, is the highest seed there.
Aside from that pair, along with Noskova and three-time major semifinalist Elina Svitolina, others who can make the final are Jasmine Paolini, Dayana Yastremska, Anna Kalinskaya and Oceane Dodin — a quartet who were 23-63 in Grand Slam action before this fortnight.
So what does it all mean? It's hard to make sweeping conclusions based on early-for-them departures by Swiatek, No. 3 Elena Rybakina, No. 5 Jessica Pegula, No. 6 Ons Jabeur and No. 7 Marketa Vondrousova.
But it does offer a contrast to the sort of day-in, day-out excellence displayed by Serena Williams, for one, as she compiled 23 Slam singles titles and, even as the end of her career approached, run after run to the finals at the sport's biggest tournaments.
And, in this post-Serena world, it offers fans a chance to learn unfamiliar names and appreciate unfamiliar games. They won't all be future stars — and, likely, none will be — but it's worth watching to find out.
Noskova is part of the seemingly never-ending reservoir of talent from the Czech Republic. Folks who follow tennis closely know she was the 2021 French Open junior champion. They might also remember she was half of the doubles team that beat Williams and her sister, Venus, in doubles at the 2022 U.S. Open, Serena's last event.
But this? Swiatek was listed by FanDuel Sportsbook as a minus-1,700 favorite, then took the first set, but then couldn't handle Noskova's confidence and booming strokes down the stretch.
Noskova is in a wave of not-yet-20-somethings making noise in Melbourne. Three 16-year-olds won first-round matches — the most at the Australian Open since 2005 — and one, Mirra Andreeva, was scheduled to play in the fourth round Sunday on the bottom half of the bracket.
That's the portion that includes Coco Gauff, the 19-year-old American who won the U.S. Open in September, and No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka, the defending champ in Melbourne. They both reached the fourth round without dropping a set, so not every result has been a stunner.
Still, as Sabalenka cautioned: "Anything can happen." Which is not necessarily a bad thing for those watching.

title: KINGS AND QUEENS
author: Bill Haufe
content:
KINGS AND QUEENS

 January 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1226
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SNOW HILL — It was a first for Cambridge-South Dorchester High's boys track program and head coach Clint Falduto.But it was the last conference indoor title run for Kent Island's girls team, at least under head coach Justin Holland.
Tori Willis Jr., won two individual titles to lead the Vikings to their first boys team crown indoors in school history, and Gabrielle Bernhard struck gold twice and set a new standard Wednesday, pacing the Buccaneers to their fifth girls title in six years during the Bayside Conference indoor track and field championships at the Worcester County Recreation Center.
"I was nervous," said Holland of the girls' competition, which ended with Kent Island totaling 96½ points — 23 ahead of runner-up Parkside.
Holland, who is set to retire from coaching after this season, had reason to be nervous.
Historically a power in the middle- and long-distance events, the Bucs did not score a point in the 1,600 or 3,200 meters Wednesday, had Kaitlyn Stevens place fifth for their only points in the 800, and were an uncharacteristic fifth in the 4x800 relay.
"This is not the stereotypical Kent Island track team," Holland said. "The four-by-eight (relay), I can't remember us not either winning, or you know, (placing) top three in the four-by-eight. I'm not used to this.
"And then when it comes to the (800), that's when we usually win the meet," Holland continued. "It's tight and then we go to the 800 and we triple score in the eight, and we seal the deal, because everybody knows we're going to be in the top four in the four-by-four relay. It was interesting."
Bernhard helped make up for those rare deficiencies, leading a 1-2-4 finish in both the 500 meters and pole vault.
"I'm happy that she switched over from cheerleading to track," Holland said of Bernhard, who did cheer and ran indoors last year, but is running track only this year.
Like many of Wednesday's competitors, Bernhard ran all her events in a fairly tight time frame. She placed second to Cambridge-SD's Enazajah Young (8.76 seconds) in the 55 hurdles, clocking a 9.03. She came right back and took fourth (45.26) in the 300. Two events later, she was back on the track, running the 500.
"Last year she was in the four-by-two (relay), but I had to drop her all the time because the four-by-two and the pole vault were all in the same (time) spot," Holland said. "So this year she's been scoring individually in the three and the five. And she wasn't a 500 runner. But she ran cross country this year so she knew she was in shape. So I said, 'Let's try the 500.' Of course that's the one she won."
But it took some doing, as she rallied past sophomore teammate Reece Heyliger over the final 50 meters to win in 1:24.59. Heyliger, who overcame a false start in the 55 to run strong legs for the second-place 4x200 relay and first-place 4x400 relay, was second in 1:24.78, followed by teammate Siena Koch (1:27.66) in fourth.
Bernhard, who early in the season broke Fiona Mulligan's school indoor pole vault record when she cleared 11 feet, 1 inch, capped her day by winning the pole vault with a new conference record effort of 11-2. The senior was followed by teammates Siena Koch (8 foot) in second and Nora Koch (6-6) in fourth.
Parkside (1:53.95) won the 4x200, but Kent Island's team of Kendra Coffey, Siena Koch, Heyliger and Seryna Stephan was second in 1:57.12. The Bucs punctuated the ninth girls indoor championship of Holland's career in the 4x400 relay, as Heyliger, Coffey, Stephan and Stevens won in 4:31.45.
The defending Class 1A state champion in the girls 55 meters, Cambridge-SD's Young held off Parkside's RaNiya Corbin (7.56) to win the conference crown in 7.45, before coming back to win the 55 hurdles in 8.76.
"Enazajah is a talent that's hard to match," Falduto said. "She's just incredibly athletic. We're trying to build her stamina up for some more different events other than the short ones. This could be a great opportunity for her future after high school. Just excited to see how she continues to control this season."
Falduto was excited to see what his boys team could do this season, and Wednesday the Vikings showed why, rolling to their first Bayside title indoors with 134½ points — 74 points ahead of runner-up Kent Island.
"They're stacked," Holland said of Cambridge-SD.
At the top of that stack is Willis, who started his day by winning the 55 meters in 6.576 — nipping Parkside's Nasir Bolden (6.578) — then leading a 1-2-3 Vikings sweep in the 55 hurdles. Willis took gold in 8.07 seconds followed by teammates Antonio Blueford (second, 8.121) and Jaydene Smith (third, 8.129).
"We've been training Tori to prepare for a day like this, knowing that come the state meet it would not be a similar type (of situation)," Falduto said in reference to the tight time schedule. "We knew coming into the Bayside meet and the competition we had, that he had a great opportunity to be a medalist in all four events."
A junior, Willis placed second in the 300 (37.10) to Snow Hill's Logan Hurney (36.88) before closing his day with a third-place in the 500 (1:13.71), completing a 34-point day.
Competing indoors for the first time, sophomore Majestic Jones gave Cambridge-SD an added boost, winning the high jump with a leap of 5-10.
Then there was Viking junior Tekai Drummond, who logged runner-up finishes in the 1,600 (4:55.50), 3,200 (10:49.39) and 800 (2:09.11), and ran a leg on the third-place 4x400 relay.
"Tekai has been probably the backbone of our team," Falduto said. "He was a sprinter last year, rarely did an 800 here or there, but as he's moved now to the mile, two mile. What he has done has really changed the dynamics of our team.
"We had a goal set on having a championship year," Faldutot said of his boys team. "Starting off the postseason with the indoor Bayside championship is a huge success for our team, and where they're at, and where they're heading. We had a goal set and we accomplished it for the boys. Everybody showed up in my opinion so I was very excited about that."
Queen Anne's County junior Ben Marks looks comfortable and in command en route to winning the boys 1,600 meters (4:51.13) and 800 (2:03.25).
"We didn't want him to run too hard," Queen Anne's head coach Natasha Dawson said of Marks, who's been focusing on the 1,600 this indoor season. "He hasn't run the 800 competitively this season. So we needed to make sure he got a good time so that sets him up for a good heat in regions."
Easton's Jed Smith led from start to finish in the boys 3,200. The senior began widening his lead with six laps remaining and won in 10:41.28. Smith joined Colin Smith, Jacob Camper and William Orndoff to give the Warriors victory in the boys 4x800 relay (8:49.39).
The Warriors got a second individual champion, as senior Sumayah Wilkins won the high jump, clearing the bar at 5 feet. Easton's Marvin Foster was second in the boys shot put (42-10½).
North Caroline junior Morgan Knott outdueled Snow Hill's Allie Suarezapecheche to win the girls 800 in 2:36.43. Knott also teamed with sophomores Seanna Rupp, Reece Bisesi and Linda Ridgell for victory in the 4x800 relay (10:49.95). Ridgell was runner-up in the 3,200 (12:46.96).

title: Warriors assistant Milojević dies
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors assistant Milojević dies

 January 17, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 825
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Golden State Warriors assistant coach Dejan Milojević, a mentor to two-time NBA MVP Nikola Jokic and a former star player in his native Serbia, died Wednesday in Utah after suffering a heart attack, the team announced. Milojević, part of the staff that helped the Warriors win the 2022 NBA championship, was 46.Milojević died in Salt Lake City, where he was hospitalized Tuesday night after the medical emergency happened during a private team dinner. The Warriors had been scheduled to play the Utah Jazz on Wednesday night, a game the NBA postponed.
"We are absolutely devastated by Dejan's sudden passing," coach Steve Kerr said in a statement released by the team. "This is a shocking and tragic blow for everyone associated with the Warriors and an incredibly difficult time for his family, friends, and all of us who had the incredible pleasure to work with him."
Milojević's death elicited a massive and immediate outpouring of sympathy from the basketball community, and moments of silence were held Wednesday before NBA games. Miami Heat coach Erik Spoelstra called the news "horrific." Atlanta forward Bogdan Bogdanovic — a Serbian, like Milojević — politely declined comment Wednesday before the Hawks' game, saying "I'm sorry. I can't talk about it right now. I feel so bad," while tapping his chest. San Antonio coach Gregg Popovich raved about how good a coach Milojević was.
"You changed my life in such a short time," Warriors rookie Brandin Podziemski wrote on social media. "The most important thing you ever told me was to just smile! Your joy and laughs will forever be missed. Shine down on us from heaven."
Milojević was in his third season with the Warriors. He previously coached in Serbia — where he once worked with a young Jokic before the now-Denver Nuggets star came to the United States — along with Montenegro, plus had been an assistant coach for the Serbian national team alongside current Atlanta assistant Igor Koskoskov.
"The NBA mourns the sudden passing of Golden State assistant coach Dejan Milojević, a beloved colleague and dear friend to so many in the global basketball community," NBA Commissioner Adam Silver said.
Milojević worked closely with Jokic, Los Angeles Clippers center Ivica Zubac, Orlando center Goga Bitadze and Houston center Boban Marjanovic, among others, during his time as a coach in Europe. With the Warriors, he worked primarily with the big men like Kevon Looney, who raved about Milojević's attention to detail.
"Rest in peace, Deki," Dallas Mavericks star Luka Doncic wrote on social media.
Kerr said he originally learned of Milojević from Kent Lacob, the son of Golden State owner Joe Lacob. And when the Warriors went through some staffing changes in 2021, Kerr decided to pursue Milojević. It took some convincing, but Milojević finally agreed to take the offer. Kerr was thrilled.
"I immediately saw what Kent was talking about," Kerr said in a video produced by the Warriors last year. "He was so great to be around. At the same time, he had this amazing basketball background both as a player and a coach. It made so much sense for us to bring Deki in."
Milojević won three consecutive MVP awards in the Adriatic League, taking those trophies in 2004, 2005 and 2006 when the 6-foot-7, 240-pound power forward was at the peak of his playing career. Jokic was MVP of that league in 2015, a year after current Golden State forward Dario Saric was MVP.
His potential in the game came early: Shortly after he began playing, Milojević scored 141 points in a game as a 14-year-old in 1991.
"I teach all my players that basketball is not a job, but that they should enjoy the game," Milojević told Bosnian radio-television outlet RTV in a 2018 interview. "Because if you want to do something for the next 20 years, then you have to love it a lot. It's not easy to endure all these efforts if you don't like something. Only those who have a sincere love for the game can handle everything with great success."
Before joining the Warriors, Milojević had NBA experience through Summer League assistant coach stints with Atlanta, San Antonio and Houston.
Toronto coach Darko Rajaković said he had known Milojević since he was a teenager.
"He was a role model as a player, as a man, as a husband, as a coach — somebody that I really admired and have a lot of respect for," Rajaković said. "Unfortunately, last night, his heart stopped working and he left his wife and two kids behind and a big, big legacy."
Added former Golden State assistant and current Sacramento head coach Mike Brown: "Not only was he an extremely talented coach, he was an even better person."
A rescheduled date for the Warriors-Jazz game was not immediately announced. The Jazz said tickets for Wednesday night would be honored at the rescheduled game. Golden State is next scheduled to play at home Friday against Dallas.
Milojević is survived by his wife, Natasa, and their children, Nikola and Masa.
"Their loss is unfathomable," Kerr said.

title: McCarthy will return as Cowboys head coach
author: Bill Haufe
content:
McCarthy will return as Cowboys head coach

 January 17, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 267
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Mike McCarthy will get another chance to end a nearly three-decade stretch without a deep playoff run for the Dallas Cowboys.Owner and general manager Jerry Jones said Wednesday night McCarthy will be back for a fifth season as coach after a stunning 48-32 wild-card loss to Green Bay.
The Cowboys were the first No. 7 seed to lose since the 14-team format was adopted in 2020. Dallas surged to the NFC East title in the final two weeks and had a chance for multiple home playoff games.
Instead, McCarthy's team is the first not to reach a conference title game after three consecutive 12-win playoff seasons.
"There is great benefit to continuing the team's progress under Mike's leadership as our head coach," Jones said in a statement with several references to the disappointment of the playoff loss. "Mike has the highest regular-season winning percentage of any head coach in Cowboys history and we will dedicate ourselves, in partnership with him, to translating that into reaching our postseason goals."
McCarthy was hired to get Dallas past the divisional round for the first time since the 1995 season, the last of the storied franchise's five Super Bowl titles.
The 60-year-old won a Super Bowl with Green Bay 13 years ago and reached the NFC championship game three other times in 12-plus seasons leading the Packers.
McCarthy was fired midway through a second consecutive losing season in 2018 in Green Bay. He was out of football in 2019 before Jones hired him. He is 167-102-2 overall and 42-25 with Dallas.
McCarthy has one year remaining on his contract. Jones' statement made no mention of an extension.

title: ENDING ON A GREAT NOTE
author: Bill Haufe
content:
ENDING ON A GREAT NOTE

 February 29, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1261
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Gary Gould was admittedly a bit baffled as he kept watch on Beth Tfiloh School's boys basketball team heading toward the postseason."They lost a couple games the last week of the (regular) season," said Saints Peter and Paul High's head coach, whose team had lost three straight to the Warriors. "And then some of the games they won, they only won by like four or five points to teams that we were beating by double-digits. I was confused why other teams could play them so well and we couldn't. And then I thought about it and said, it had to be me. I was doing too much. I was trying to be too good in the x's and o's part, instead of just letting us play."
Gould let his team play Saturday night, made a halftime adjustment, then watched the Sabres pull away in the second half for a 68-58 victory over Beth Tfiloh in the Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association C Conference championship game at UMBC's Chesapeake Employers Insurance Arena.
"It feels amazing," said senior forward K'den Spears, named player of the game after Sts. Peter & Paul won its first MIAA C title since 2016. "The only reason why we keep losing games is when we selfishly play. We really played as a group and really helped each other and built each other up."
Though a mid-season injury limited junior star Garett Hemingway's minutes, Sts. Peter & Paul had built a nice hot streak heading into the playoffs, having won nine of its last 10, including its last eight straight.
Beth Tfiloh defeated Sts. Peter & Paul in last year's conference championship, won a two-point nail-biter in Easton on Jan. 11, then rolled to a 72-45 victory at home Jan. 31, dealing the Sabres their most lopsided loss of the season, as well as the only blemish during their hot streak.
But Warriors head coach Ari Braun didn't necessarily put a lot of stock in his team's Jan. 31 romp.
"The first game this year was down to the wire at Saints Peter and Paul. Either team could have won it," Braun said of the Jan. 11 clash in which Hemingway scored 33 points. "The second time, I think that was (Hemingway's) first game back from his ankle and he was not the same player. They weren't all right yet, and we made shots and defended. Obviously we played an awesome game, and it looks worse than maybe it should have."
Then came Saturday night's title bout.
"I think the difference was we were more focused," Gould said. "We realized the game at Beth was something we knew wasn't going to happen again because we didn't shoot the ball well. Plus that second game, I did too much. I was trying to coach too much strategy wise and take away things and add stuff. I think I had my kids playing too slow.
"The kids knew that last year we didn't know what to expect, so we played with a little nerves," Gould said of the Sabres' 65-58 loss in the title game. "But this year we knew going in what to do. So the kids were just focused about getting it done, went out and just played. And we knew it was just our time."
Hemingway (game-high 19 points) canned a pair of 3-pointers early as the Sabres (16-8) carried a 27-24 lead into the locker room after a back-and-forth first half. And while he was guarded against over-coaching again, Gould searched for an edge during the first half.
"I was trying to figure out on the sideline what was happening; what were they doing that was working, and what we could take away to give us the advantage," Gould said.
Gould's key takeaway was switching from the man-to-man and 2-3 zone defenses the Sabres used in the first half to a 1-2-2 zone. The move proved critical, especially when it came to defending Warrior senior guard Michael Cohen, who scored a game-high 35-points in last year's title game.
"Their skip passing wasn't available to them," Gould said. "And then we kept number four, Michael Cohen, in front of us so he wasn't able to penetrate and do all the stuff he did to us last year. He was the guy who hurt us."
Consistently penetrating inside and drawing contact, Cohen went 19 of 28 from the line in last year's final, which included a 12-of-16 effort in the fourth quarter. In Saturday's rematch he finished with 17 points.
"Defense was big for us," Hemingway said. "We came into the game saying, if we can slow them down, hold Cohen. Slow him down, get in front of him, take charges. As long as we get the defense down the offense will just come."
Braun agreed Gould's defensive tweak was big.
"They did an unbelievable job with their defense, Braun said. "They started off in the man, which I didn't think it went great for them, but then they quickly pivoted to the zone. And they were very disciplined in staying back and clogging the paint and not really giving Michael as many opportunities to drive. Last year in the championship game, they were pressing and allowing us to get out in the open court, and that led to a lot of his free throws and baskets. But this year they did a great job of staying at home defensively."
That move produced steals and kick-started the Sabres' transition game. Senior point guard Brayden Smith scored eight of his 13 points in the third quarter, and Robbie Cunningham netted seven of his 11, as Sts. Peter & Paul outscored the Warriors 19-9 for a 46-33 lead heading into the fourth quarter.
Braun, who graduated a number of seniors from last season's title team, acknowledged two other significant factors. Elan Vogelstein, Beth Tfiloh's top rebounder and assist man, suffered a thigh injury in the second Sts. Peter & Paul game, and has been sidelined the remainder of the season.
"I don't know if that changes the outcome of the game, but obviously that would have helped us," Braun said.
And then there was Sts. Peter & Paul's job on the boards, especially the effort delivered by Spears.
"I think what really hurt us even more than the zone was their offensive rebounding," Braun said. "When we can get a stop and end it with a rebound we can then run. That's way different than them getting rebound after rebound and pounding us and then scoring. And then we're just playing against a settled defense. So I thought they just did an awesome job in terms of game plan and execution, just playing with a lot of effort on the court.
"And I think number zero, he was a beast on the glass and our guys really struggled with that," Braun said of Spears.
Spears was a force on the boards in the Sabres' semifinal victory over Cristo Rey. Against the Warriors, he was again tough on the glass, yanking down eight rebounds, and in the score column, finishing with 13 points.
"That's the best I've ever seen K'den play," Hemingway said.
Gould echoed that sentiment.
"He was more consistent and forceful in what he was doing," Gould said of Spears
Spears was also more confident.
"I just felt because this is the second time for us being there, and there was no point in us being nervous because it was the same team we played last year," Spears said.
Beth Tfiloh (25-8) outscored the Sabres, 25-22, in the fourth, but it couldn't rally enough.
"As a team I felt more together," Spears said. "This was our last game and I just wanted to end it off on a really great note."

title: Bailey's hot hand fuels Warriors
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Bailey's hot hand fuels Warriors

 February 29, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 705
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Wicomico High's defensive plan had held Easton's Marshall Bailey without a field goal for almost three quarters Thursday night.Then in a bid to generate some offense, Indians head coach Butch Waller dropped his triangle-and-two scheme and went man to man. Bailey took advantage of the switch, connecting for 25 of his game-high 30 points over the final 11-plus minutes while leading Easton to a 69-56 victory over Wicomico in a Class 2A East Region II semifinal.
The second-seeded Warriors (15-6) travel to top-seeded Queen Anne's (17-4) on Tuesday for the 2A East Region II championship at 5 p.m. The Lions defeated fourth-seeded Parkside, 62-55, in last night's other semifinal.
"Second half they went man and he was hard to stop," Easton head coach Dionte Hynson said of Bailey. "He was hitting his jump shot, getting to the hole. He put us on his back in the second half."
With the Indians' triangle-and-two limiting Bailey and backcourt mate Ja'Kai Brooks, Easton worked the ball inside to Tymier Thomas (12 points) whose seven first-quarter points helped the Warriors take a 16-10 lead heading into the second quarter.
"They really couldn't get open," Hynson said of Bailey and Brooks in the first half. "Thankfully, Tymier was hitting. He kept us in the game in the first half."
Down 18-12, the Indians rallied to draw even at 18-all on Tyson Hayward's bucket with a little over 5 minutes remaining in the half. Brooks then hit a 3-pointer to break a 22-all tie with 2:06 left before intermission. Kyree Acree (12 points) sandwiched a 3-pointer and a layup around a Zymier Ramirez free throw to push the Warriors lead to 31-25 at halftime.
Waller stayed with his triangle-and-two zone until midway through the third when he opted to go man in hopes of kick-starting his offense.
"We ran a little triangle-and-two and we did an OK job, but we couldn't balance it by scoring," Waller said. "The defense was fine in the first half, even halfway through the third quarter. And then I just said, 'We've got to play them man to man, take our chances, pick the tempo up.' We couldn't do it.
"Same problem we've been plagued with all season long; can't score," Waller continued. "Shooting percentage tonight was 32.1. We've had that same problem, which is understandable with some new players. At this level, or any level really, you've got to be able to put the brown thing in the round thing."
Bailey began doing just that.
After consecutive baskets from Kahlil Batson, and a nice low-post bucket from Acree, Bailey made a three-point play with 3:13 left in the third quarter for a 40-29 Warrior lead. Wi-Hi's Tay'Shawn Swann (16 points) scored on a reverse layup. But Bailey answered with a 3-pointer and another three-point play, extending Easton's lead to 46-32 by the end of the third quarter.
"I just knew we had to lock in defensively because that first half we were only up by six and it was a sloppy game," Bailey said. "So once we locked in defensively — I think we held them to like seven points — everything offensively started clicking for us."
Thomas scored on a drive to maintain the Warriors' 14-point cushion at 48-34 early in the fourth quarter. Bailey then hit back-to-back 3-pointers, drove for a layup and buried a pull-up jumper for a commanding 58-41 lead with 5:13 remaining in the game.
"Excellent shooter," Waller said of Easton's sophomore guard. "One of the better shooters I've seen in years."
Bailey converted a Thomas dish for a layup, then assisted on Thomas and Acree baskets that gave Easton a 65-52 lead with just over two minutes remaining.
Takai Hugee led Wi-Hi with 18 points.
1A EAST REGION II PLAYOFFSCambridge-SD 84 Crisfield 32CAMBRIDGE — LaShaun Moody scored a game-high 30 points as the top-seeded Vikings rolled into the 1A East II final.
Koby Ennals had 15 points for the Vikings, who got 11 from Sterling Perkins and 10 from Semaj Pinder.

Manny Wallace finished with 15 points for Colonel Richardson.
