title: Defense fuels Cambridge-SD past Warriors
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Defense fuels Cambridge-SD past Warriors

 February 15, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 739
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Cambridge-South Dorchester High's boys basketball team arrived in Easton Thursday night having already won the North Bayside.The way the Vikings played, you would have thought the division title was still on the line.
Sophomore Semaj Pinder scored a team-high 19 points and four others finished in double figures, as Cambridge-SD, behind an overwhelming defense, rolled to a 79-60 victory over the Warriors.
The Vikings (19-1 overall, 15-1 North Bayside) now prepare to play Stephen Decatur for the Bayside Conference championship next Tuesday at the Wicomico County Civic Center in Salisbury.
"Old fashion butt kicking," Easton head coach Dionte Hynson said after the Warriors' second most lopsided loss of the season. "Congratulations to them. They were the better team tonight. I thought they brought a whole lot of energy. We didn't match their energy tonight. First quarter, came out, played well. And then after that."
Easton (14-6, 13-3) led 12-5 with a little over 3 minutes remaining in the first quarter. Cambridge-SD sophomore Sterling Perkins (17 points) converted a steal into a layup. Darren Belizare turned another steal into a layup. Pinder then buried a 3-pointer to forge a 12-12 tie heading into the second quarter.
Cambridge-SD continued to hound the Warriors defensively and took control of the game, outscoring Easton, 21-11 in the second quarter.
"We got a chip on our shoulder," said Cambridge-SD head coach Shawn Tucker, who was minus starting point guard LaShaun Moody. "We're the underdogs we feel like every game we're going in. There's so much negativity that goes with these C-SD boys. And they just fight and fight. They're resilient. And they represent me. I'm wild. I'm passionate. I'm full of energy."
So were the Vikings.
Easton shaved a seven-point deficit to 25-21 when sophomore guard Marshall Bailey (18 points) hit a pair of free throws with 2:36 left in the second quarter. But Perkins and junior Koby Ennals (12 points) drained back-to-back 3-pointers before a Kamarion Hall's bucket capped an 8-0 run, that helped the Vikings to a 33-23 halftime lead.
"I give all props to my assistant coaches, also my defensive coach, Ryan Waters," Tucker said. "He has those guys locked in on defense. And we've been pressuring teams for the last seven games. We're just relentless on that."
After letting a 17-point third-quarter lead get away in a 58-57 loss to Queen Anne's on Feb. 1, Cambridge-SD has reeled off seven straight wins.
Easton scored the last five points of the third quarter to pull within 50-41 at the end of the third quarter. But the Warriors wouldn't get any closer, as the Vikings outscored their longtime rival, 29-19, in the fourth quarter.
"They were shooting the heck out of the ball tonight," Hynson said of the Vikings. "Their zero (Perkins) and their number 12 (Pinder), they were shooting the ball real well.
"Our defense was horrible," Hynson added. "We were just sitting there watching their shooters. And we were giving up too many straight line drives to the basket. We'll learn from it. Like I told them, it's over and done with. Just got to move on and get ready for playoffs."
Ja'Kai Brooks led Easton with 19 points.
Jaden Harris had 12 points for Cambridge-SD and Anthony Hughes added 10.
"We got four goals and we just accomplished one of them," said Tucker of winning the North Bayside.
QUEEN ANNE'S 76 KENT ISLAND 73
CENTREVILLE — Vince Gilberto scored 19 points and Collin Woolford went over the 1,000-point mark for his career as the Lions outlasted their county rival in overtime.
Amari Baynard had 15 points for Queen Anne's (16-4, 14-2) and Jadereon Thompson had 13.

AMERICAN CORNER — Dreden Lake scored 23 points and Jazir Dickerson added 20 to pace the Colonels.
Makiah Batson had 15 points and Manny Wallace 12 for Colonel Richardson.
North Caroline's Nasai Bell led all scorers with 24 points. Jarvis Thomas had 17 and Tyson Weber and Quinell Gross each had 12.
GIRLS BASKETBALL
QUEEN ANNE'S 49 KENT ISLAND 33
CENTREVILLE — Kariana Hickson scored 18 points as the Lions clinched the North Bayside title.
Freshmen Laila Coles had 13 points for Queen Anne's (19-1, 16-0) and Bea Holthaus had 11.
NORTH CAROLINE 58 COL. RICHARDSON 28

author: Bill Haufe

Gunston School crew set to join WMIRA

 February 14, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 271
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — The Gunston School will join the Washington Metropolitan Interscholastic Rowing Association (WMIRA), the region's premier rowing conference, this spring.While Gunston has regularly competed against WMIRA teams at national regattas like Head of the Schuylkill in Philadelphia, the school is now eligible to compete in the conference championship regatta on May 5.
"Each year our students and coaches continue to elevate the quality and competitiveness of the program," Head of School John Lewis said, "and we're eager to join the ranks of the best public and private school rowing teams in our area. We're grateful that the WMIRA expanded its geographical reach to include us, and we look forward to welcoming these teams to home regattas at Gunston."
The WMIRA includes independent and parochial school teams like DeMatha, Georgetown Day School, St. Albans, Gonzaga, Holton Arms, and National Cathedral School, as well as Montgomery County public school powerhouses such as Blair, Bethesda-Chevy Chase, Walter Johnson, and Walt Whitman.
"I'm proud of our rowers, and appreciative of the WMIRA," said Natalie Reading, Gunston's head crew coach and assistant athletic director for waterfront athletics. "This opportunity not only enhances the competitiveness of Gunston's rowing team but also opens doors to a broader range of experiences and challenges. We aim to continue to build on our 2023 Maryland State championship performance."
In addition to the WMIRA, Gunston will again host the Maryland State rowing championship on Saturday, April 27, on its 75-acre campus on the Corsica River. Spectators are invited to bring chairs and/or blankets and watch the 1,500-meter sprint style race with 4's and 8's, men and women's varsity, junior varsity and novice event categories.

title: EASTON-CR
author: Bill Haufe
content:
EASTON-CR

 February 13, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 863
 Words 

 Read News Document

 AMERICAN CORNER — Any residue from Saturday night's loss to James M. Bennett at the Peake Challenge was gone.And Easton High's boys basketball team made sure this wasn't going to be a bump in the road as it tried to re-establish its momentum with the postseason approaching.
The Warriors buried five 3-pointers in the first quarter and sophomore guard Marshall Bailey scored a game-high 22 points Tuesday night, pacing Easton to a 73-65 victory over Colonel Richardson.
"We want to establish like a mindset and try to come out and punch 'em in the mouth first and see what happens, and then adjust after that," Easton head coach Dionte Hynson said after the Warriors improved to 14-5 overall, 13-2 North Bayside. "I think we came out and played real well defensively, got up and down a little bit, and that got our offense flowing a little bit."
So did the three-ball.
Ja'Kai Brooks (18 points) drilled the first of his two 3-pointers in the opening minute and Easton never trailed. Brooks popped another trey midway through the first quarter for an 8-2 Easton lead. Bailey, who had three 3-pointers, canned a 3 for an 11-4 lead. Diontaye Copper (13 points) drained one of his three 3-pointers with 1:40 left in the first period before Bailey connected on Easton's fifth of the quarter for a 21-10 lead after one period.
"Our guards were shooting the ball real well," Hynson said.
The Warriors extended their lead in the second quarter behind strong inside play from Tymire Thomas and Kahlil Batson, who each took entry passes and made quick spin moves inside the paint for buckets and a 40-24 halftime cushion.
"The halfcourt offense was really flowing I thought," Hynson said. "We hit a couple high-lows too. We made some really nice passes. Our bigs, they were hitting the high-lows. Even Tymire came off the bench with his high-low."
Three-pointers from Makiah Batson (12 points) and Manny Wallace (13 points) helped Colonel Richardson (11-8, 7-8) trim its 16-point halftime deficit to 10 with 3:46 remaining in the third quarter.
But Easton outscored the Colonels, 14-5, over the final 3-plus minutes of the third, including a 6-point frenzy in the last 30 seconds. Bailey turned a steal into a layup and was fouled. Though Bailey missed the free throw, Zymier Ramirez grabbed the rebound and scored on a put-back. Bailey then made a steal on the inbounds pass and laid the ball in for a 59-40 lead heading into the fourth quarter.
"We just lost our focus there a little at the end of the quarter," Colonels head coach Brad Plutschak said. "We just couldn't get right. I was hoping if we could get it inside 10 we could see what could happen. But we had given up some pretty open looks there in the first quarter. We were chasing points all night at that's tough."
Colonel creeped back within 15, but back-to-back 3-pointers from Copper gave the Warriors a 65-47 lead with just under 6 minutes left in the game.
Up 19, Hynson pulled most of his starting lineup with a little over 2 minutes remaining. Colonel scored the game's final 10 points to make the final more respectable.
"We played a good team on Saturday," Hynson said of Bennett. "We didn't play that bad but we got some stuff straightened out. I thought we bounced back real nice. I told them this is the last week (of the regular season) and we've got to get ready for the playoffs. I think we're headed in the right direction."
Easton is scheduled to host North Bayside-leading Cambridge-South Dorchester (19-1, 15-1) on Thursday.
Notes: Jazir Dickerson had a team-high 15 points for Colonel Richardson, which had its four-game win streak snapped.
CAMBRIDGE-SD 115 ST. MICHAELS 49
CAMBRIDGE — LaShaun Moody scored a season-high 41 points and Sterling Perkins had 26 to power the Vikings to their second victory over the Saints in as many nights Tuesday.
Jaden Harris had 16 for Cambridge-SD and Thomas Wilson 10.
Nakhi Miller led St. Michaels with 30 points.
Perkins had 28 points in Monday's 87-51 win at St. Michaels. Anthony Hughes and Semaj Pinder had 15 points apiece and Wilson contributed 13 points.
Johnny Mautz led the Saints with 19.
SSPP 71, PARK 52
BALTIMORE — Garett Hemingway scored 28 points and Brayden Smith had 12 Tuesday, as Saints Peter and Paul (13-8, 6-3) rolled in a Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association C Conference game.
Robbie Cunningham finished with 10.
Hemingway had 33 points and Smith 13 in Monday's 69-60 victory over Delmarva Christian.
QUEEN ANNE'S 81 NORTH CAROLINE 65
RIDGELY — Senior Vince Gilberto had a team-high 27 points and the Lions raised their record to 15-4, 13-2.
Collin Woolford had 18 points and Jimmy Holthaus scored 10.
GIRLS BASKETBALL
KENT ISLAND 54 SOUTHERN 50
STEVENSVILLE — On Monday, Makayla Kropfelder scored a game-high 18 points as the Bucs topped Southern-Anne Arundel. Lilli Dauses had 17 points and Lacey Dauses had 10. Riska missed a double-double by one point, finishing with nine points and 14 rebounds.
QUEEN ANNE'S 49 NORTH CAROLINE 37
CENTREVILLE — Freshman Laila Coles had 16 points, eight assists and three steals as the Lions improved to 18-1, 15-0.
Freshman Bea Holthaus had 12 points and 12 boards for Queen Anne's and RJ Ensor added eight points, 10 rebounds and three steals.

title: Vikings win title after scare
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Vikings win title after scare

 February 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 934
 Words 

 Read News Document

 LANDOVER — Cambridge-South Dorchester High's boys indoor track and field team was on its way to a third consecutive Class 1A East Region championship Friday night.Then confusion stepped in.
Boys head coach Clint Falduto and assistant Lois Narr couldn't figure out how the Vikings' lead over Largo had suddenly evaporated to almost nothing after the second-to-last race on the boys 1A schedule — the 800 meters.
"Lois was like, 'We should be up by so much further.' And I was like, 'I know. I don't know what happened,'" Falduto said.
As Falduto and Narr continued trying to understand how their comfortable lead had suddenly gone poof, the boys 800 for the Class 4A East meet — which was being held simultaneously with the 1A meet at the Prince George's Sports and Learning Complex — was being run.
That's when Cambridge-SD's Tekai Drummond approached Falduto and Narr with the answer.
"Tekai came up and said, 'That kid that just beat me, he's in 4A,'" Falduto said. "And we're like, 'What?'"
Falduto and Narr went to the officials' table where it was confirmed a 4A runner — wearing the same hip number as a Largo runner — had run the wrong race, and that his points had initially been counted toward Largo's point total. As officials corrected the mistake, Cambridge-SD was getting ready to run its heat of the boys 4x400 relay.
Though Largo won the 4x400, Antonio Blueford, Tori Willis, Tekai Drummond and Teshar Drummond's runner-up finish in the event capped a third regional title for the Vikings, who totaled 91 points to the Lions' 84.
"They were beating us at one point," Falduto said of Largo. "My head was spinning. Oh my goodness, it was exciting. So, so exciting. Freaking bizarre.
"The boys have worked so tremendously hard," Falduto continued. "This group has been together for a good solid three years, the majority of them. And knowing the competition around the state, they knew it was possible. But they knew it was going to be a lot of hard work."
Cambridge-SD's bid for a third straight 1A East crown became even harder because a number of key team members were unable to compete, including Jayden Smith, who was sidelined by an illness.
Despite those losses, the Vikings scored in 10 of the 11 events.
Leading that effort was Willis, who won the 55-meter hurdles in a personal-record 7.87 seconds, placed second in the 55-meter sprint (6.55), and ran a leg on the second-place 4x800 relay, joining Christian Dockins and the Drummonds for a time of 8:54.92.
"Fifty-five-meter hurdles, I really think it was just push and get out, and tried to keep my pace and keep my energy going through the hurdles," said Willis, who took the lead after clearing the second hurdle. "I just wanted to make sure I qualified and made it to states again. Once I get a good start, I know I'm going to push through the hurdles and get the win."
Edwind Torres of Chesapeake Science Point was second in the hurdles with an 8.11, followed by Cambridge-SD's Blueford in third (8.28).
"Fifty-five, there's room to improve," said Willis, who clocked a 6.55, finishing second to Friendly's Donte Long (6.48). Kent County's Tyrell Fennell was third in 6.58.
In addition to their second-places in the 4x800 and 4x400 relays, Cambridge-SD was also second in the 4x200, as Teshar Drummond, Kay'lon Marine, William Jackson and Jakuez combined for a 1:34.55.
The Vikings were second to Largo in all three relays.
Fourth in the controversial 800, Tekai Drummond, who was running sprints a year ago, finished second in the 1,600 with a 4:49.61.
Bolstering the Vikings' fortunes were the second- and third-place finishes by Jackson (11-5) and Preston Adkins (8-11) in the pole vault.
Cambridge-SD swept the hurdles titles, as Enazajah Young broke her own school record to win the girls title in 8.28, beating Largo's Ayniah Fersner (8.56) and Lailah Fersner (8.65).
"By the third hurdle," said Young, when asked when she thought she had the hurdles won. "When you race you can hear people's footsteps. I didn't hear nothing. I was like, 'You got to push through the rest.'"
The defending state champion in the 55 meters, Young got off to a slow start in the sprint after a teammate had been disqualified for a false start. Young finished fourth in 7.34, but qualified for the state championships on Feb. 20.
"She watched her teammate false start right before," Cambridge-SD girls head coach Stacey Brown said of Young in the 55. "It's nerve racking when you're out there. You false start one time and you miss states. I think that goes through a lot of their heads when they're out there. They want to come out of those blocks fast, but they know one false start and they're done."
Young finished sixth in the 300 with a 44.81.
The only other North Bayside athlete to earn a first place in the girls competition was Kent County's Ke'yare Hawkins, who won the shot put with a heave of 35 feet, 3¼ inches.
The Trojans earned a second regional champion, as Larry Steward, competing in just his third competition of the season, won the boys high jump, clearing the bar at 6-2.
"I was pretty confident coming in because I know I can jump high," Steward said. "I'm not so confident in my technique in jumping. I surprised myself with 6-2. I tried to get 6-5, but I plan on getting that at states."
Colonel Richardson's Jackson Jean was second in the high jump at 5-10, followed by Kent County's Rah'zir Wilson in fourth (5-10).
Colonel Richardson also had a runner-up finish in the girls high jump, with Addison Chandler clearing 4-6. Mardela's Lexie Guy won with a 4-10.

title: CHANGING THEIR TUNE
author: Bill Haufe
content:
CHANGING THEIR TUNE

 February 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 851
 Words 

 Read News Document

 WYE MILLS — The talk surrounding St. Michaels High's boys basketball team used to be could it win just one game.That narrative has changed drastically this season. Now, as they enter the second week of February, the Saints are asking themselves can they earn a home-court playoff game?
St. Michaels kept that scenario alive Saturday afternoon, as senior Nakhi Miller scored a game-high 34 points and sophomore Johnny Mautz had 20, pacing the Saints to a 79-47 rout of Mardela in the boys opener of the Peake Challenge at Chesapeake College.
"I told them these last few games, 'No, we can't win the (North) Bayside, but you can set yourselves up to have a home game as far as the seeding goes for the playoffs,'" St. Michaels second-year head coach Boo Ricketts said. "We're not just playing to beat teams. We're playing to make progress and put ourselves in a good position as a team. This is all about the Saints."
While Perryville (12-3) and Colonel Richardson (11-7) hold the top two seeds in Class 1A East Region I, St. Michaels (6-11 overall, 4-10 North Bayside) stayed within reach of No. 3 Bohemia Manor (8-9) and just ahead of Kent County (5-11) in the region field.
"We really didn't lose any pieces from last season," Mautz said. "Just been working and it's starting to come together. I mean I think we should have more than six wins to be honest."
Mautz could certainly point toward a four-point loss to North Caroline on Dec. 12, or Thursday's loss on senior night against Gunston.
"As I tell my guys, 'We're not playing against teams this year,'" Ricketts said. "'We're playing against us. It's all about growing. It's all about progress.' They always ask me, 'Is this team good?' I said, 'We're not assessing teams. Every team is good. Let's show up and play our brand of basketball.'"
The Saints did that against Mardela (1-16), as Miller and Mautz established an early trend of attacking the rim, while helping St. Michaels build a 21-6 lead after the first quarter.
"This game we definitely made up for it," said Miller, referring to the Gunston loss. "We just have to become better. Go to practice and give 100 percent every day."
Mardela actually took a 2-0 lead before the game-clock even started because St. Michaels' Hunter Gottlieb drew a technical for dunking during pre-game warm-ups.
"No coach wants to start the game that way," Ricketts said. "So I pulled Hunter in our huddle and I said, 'If you want to dunk the ball make sure you get one in the game."
Gottlieb did just that with under 2 minutes remaining in the first half, when he got a breakaway and hammered a one-handed slam that brought the crowd to its highest volume of the opening 16 minutes and gave the Saints a 33-15 lead.
"I guess he made me eat my words," Ricketts said laughing.
Up 39-18 at halftime, Miller and Mautz continued driving to the basket in the second half. Mautz drilled one of his two 3-pointers less than 3 minutes into the third quarter, extending the Saints' cushion to 45-22. Mardela's Wyatt Livingstone answered with a trey to get the Warriors back within 20, But St. Michaels closed the third on a 16-6 run, with Miller accounting for 13 in the rally.
"It was just a team effort," Miller said.
A theme the senior guard has undoubtedly picked up from his head coach this season.
"I tell them every time we win games it's a collective effort," Ricketts said. "In the games we've won there's been no one man or two men that are showing up and doing it by themselves. The games we win is when they play together and everybody believes in it. Even our bench. That's what a basketball team is."
The Saints led 61-31 heading into the fourth quarter and watched Mautz reel off seven consecutive points, widening the lead to 68-33. The Warriors put together a 9-0 run to pull within 68-42, but wouldn't get any closer as Ricketts sat his starters late.
"I feel we can always be better," Mautz said. "There's always levels to go up, but I'm decently happy about where we're at right now. Play hard it practice, start to knock down our free throws, there's really no reason why we shouldn't make a run in the playoffs this year."
Christian Elsey led Mardela with 15 points.

author: Bill Haufe

title: Hirschbock, Martin pace Queen Anne's
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Hirschbock, Martin pace Queen Anne's

 March 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: News 
 
 123
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Emily Hirschbock hurled a complete-game one-hitter, striking out five and walking two Saturday, as Queen Anne's County High's softball team defeated Severna Park, 6-2, in Easter Tournament play.Autumn Huber led the Lions (5-0 overall) with a 3-for-5 effort at the plate. Camaryn Jacobi had two hits and Emilie Smith drove in two runs as part of an 11-hit attack.
Queen Anne's also rolled to a 10-1 victory over Calvert on Saturday. Hannah Martin, who blasted a first-inning three-run homer, got the win, yielding four hits over six innings while striking out seven.
Morgan Gottleib, Emily Rendulic, Caroline Taylor, Huber, Martin and Abby Gunther each had two hits for Queen Anne's.
Holiday tournament games do not count toward a team's regular-season record or regional playoff seeding.

title: UP FOR THE CHALLENGE
author: Bill Haufe
content:
UP FOR THE CHALLENGE

 March 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 2069
 Words 

 Read News Document

 North Dorchester High head softball coach Carol Hubbard's approach hasn't changed."We're going into this season exactly the same way we went into last season," Hubbard said.
Well, not exactly.
For the first time in school history, the Eagles will be playing with a significant tag attached to their name — defending state champion.
"I think that's always in the back of everybody's mind, especially the kids that are returners," said Hubbard of making a run at another state crown. "But we've talked. We want to play as many games as we can, and we approach each game one pitch at a time."
That mindset certainly worked last year, as North Dorchester compiled a school-record 22-2 slate that was capped with a 1-0 victory over Catoctin in the Class 1A state title game.
In addition to playing with that same approach, the Eagles will also be playing with a lot of the same players from a year ago, including senior ace and North Bayside pitcher of the year Emilee Cohee, who punctuated a 13-1 season in the circle with a complete-game three-hitter against Catoctin in the state final.
Rock-solid senior Maggie Hubbard is back at catcher, as is the fleet Mackenzie Lewis in center field, giving the Eagles one of the Bayside Conference's stronger defenses through the middle. Also returning are sophomore first baseman/pitcher Jewels Vroman, senior third baseman/pitcher Maddie Nagel, sophomore Emily Boyle, and juniors Averi Warfield and Brooke Outten.
"The potential is definitely there," Coach Hubbard said of a possible state-title repeat. "Like I say, we just try to go one pitch at a time and we'll see where it takes us. We're definitely in a tougher region this year having Mardela in our region."
The Warriors were the only team to defeat the Eagles a year, winning 4-3 in the regular season, then 4-2 in the Bayside Conference championship. Mardela, which fell to Catoctin in last year's state semifinals, has the potential to play North Dorchester three times this season — once in the regular season, a possible rematch in the Bayside championship, and a third clash now that North Dorchester has moved from Region II to I in the 1A East.
"I think this team is definitely up to the challenge," Hubbard said of pushing for a second straight state championship. "I've got a good core group coming back."
As do Queen Anne's, Colonel Richardson and Kent Island, who have opened the season a collective 9-0 and figure to be the Eagles' chief competition in the North.
"I don't take any games for granted," Coach Hubbard said. "Softball is kind of a fickle game. Softball luck can go one way or the other sometimes. So we just try to be as prepared as we can, tell the kids, their job is to know the situation, whether they're in the field or at the plate. And we just take it one pitch at a time.
Here's a look at this year's teams:
COLONEL RICHARDSON
Head Coach: Brett Ireland.
Who's Where: Makayla Newcomb (Sr., P); Kylie Rhinehardt (Jr., C); Eileen Johnson (Sr., 1B); Clarissa Peugh (Sr., 2B); Aubrey Taylor (So., SS); Tyla Dickerson (Sr., 3B); Kendall Sann (Sr., RF); Sadie Prettyman (Fr., CF); Montana Davis (Jr., LF); Ryleigh Porter (Jr., DH); Kayleigh Bradley (Fr., DH); Alaina Hall (Jr., OF); Kailey Cummings (Jr., OF).
Outlook: Not counting the cancelled 2020 season, Colonel has lost to the eventual 1A state champion in the regional finals by one run in three of the last five years — Bohemia Manor (2018), Patterson Mill (2021) and North Dorchester (2024).
"We got to find a way to get one run better," Ireland said.
The move from 1A East Region II — where North Dorchester and Mardela reside — to Region I could help those chances, though the Colonels look to have the goods to again be a serious contender in the North and region.
"It seems like we're going to an easier region, but you never know," Ireland said.
Newcomb, an all-North second-team pick a year ago, returns to the circle. The Colonels also return second-team first baseman Johnson, who batted over .500 last year, as well as Rhinehardt, Sann, Taylor and Dickerson, all honorable-mention picks a year ago.
The Colonels graduated the middle of their defense, but Ireland said Peugh and Taylor are making progress in the move from outfield to infield.
EASTON
Head Coach: Ryan Brice.
Who's Where: Lailah Janes (Jr., C); Lyla Roe (So., 1B/P); Gemma Vogel (So., 2B); Brynlee Buchkoski (So., SS); Olivia Orrell (Jr., 3B); Leigha Bosley (So., LF); Mayah Wilkins (Sr., CF); Kaylee Verley (Sr., RF); Sammy Townsend (So., P).
Outlook: Brice has one of the tougher challenges in front of him in trying to replace longtime head coach Jen Powell, who stepped down last summer after an outstanding career that included state titles in 2011 and 2013.
"The girls are familiar with me so we kind of have a good relationship," said Brice, an assistant on last year's 7-10 team. "But I'm not going to say I'm going to take over for Powell because she was a great coach for a long period of time. She took me under her wing. So I'm just trying to put what I learned over the years that I was under her and put that to good use this year."
The Warriors opened the season thumping Parkside, and were even with Kent Island through four innings before the Bucs ran away with a 20-6 victory.
"We're young," Brice said. "We're good. But I think with the right coaching staff that we have we can make some noise in the Bayside."
KENT COUNTY
Head Coach: Michelle Phillips.
Who's Where: Paige Miller (Jr., C); Kate Cannon (Jr., 1B/P); Anna Bitter (Sr., 2B); Talicia Wright (Fr., SS); Michelle Menequin (So., 3B/P); Asia Wilson (So., LF); Melissa Landon (Sr., CF); Madison Raleigh (Jr., RF/2B); Heather Bilborough (Jr., OF); Aaryona Wesley (Fr., OF); Ariyana Green (Fr., 2B); Laila Johnson (So., 1B).
Outlook: Cannon and Miller were honorable-mention picks a year ago and should again lead a team that finished 5-14 a year ago.
"If I can have all bodies healthy, and they're willing to go where they need to go, they're going to surprise some people," Phillips said. "But we have to eliminate errors, and we have to hit the ball. That's going to be the biggest key."
KENT ISLAND
Head Coach: Jeremy Black.
Who's Where: Mackenzie Mascetti (So., C); Emma Fleshman (Jr., 1B/P); Hayven Applefeld (Jr., 2B/P)); Abbie Mahaffey (So., SS); Ava Blum (Sr., 3B); Lizzie McConnell (Sr., LF); Avery Eaton (Jr., CF); Emily Saunders (So., RF); Bri Kurtz (Jr., P);
Outlook: The Bucs scored 20 runs or more once last year. They've already done that in their first two games this season.
"I wasn't sure what to expect," said Black, who in addition to graduating all-North Bayside Player of the Year Allison Corbin — now at UNC-Wilmington — also graduated all-North first-team picks Rilyn Heyliger and Erin Bowen off last year's 11-8 team. "I knew I had six returning starters that are a year older, a year better, and have some additional travel experience under their belts. The two kids that were freshmen last year, again, another year older, another year stronger, another year smarter. But I just didn't know how well that was going to translate yet. We're still pretty young. I only have two seniors. So it's been a very pleasant surprise to this point. They're all hitting."
If the Bucs are to challenge in the division or region, Black knows his team must continue to hit and play solid in the field."
"We're not going to shut anybody out," Black said. "We just don't have that (dominating pitcher) in the circle. So we have to play solid defense and we have to score. Fortunately for us, the first three games, the scoring hasn't been an issue. But that's going to be the key to success for us. We have to put runs on the board in order to succeed."
NORTH CAROLINE
Head Coach: Lee Hutchison.
Who's Where: Gracie Calloway (Sr., C); Hadley Eigenbrode (Jr., 1B); Maddie Porter (Jr., 2B/3B); Alyssa Garlick (Fr., 2B); Hatteras Ghrist (Jr., SS); Katie Tribbett (Sr., 3B/P); Jordyn Hunt (So., LF); Elizabeth Knott (Jr., CF); Natalie Newman (So., RF); Anna Hutchison (Sr., P); Brooklyn Spencer (So., OF); Emma Hansley (Fr., P); Lilly Carpenter (Fr., C).
Outlook: The defending 2A East Region II champions graduated all-North first-team pitcher Taylor Dawkins — now at Bowie State — and outfielder Lillian Williams, though fellow first-team choices Tribbett and Anna Hutchison return.
But Hutchison, who begins his first full year as skipper, knows if the Bulldogs are to go far, they must shore up their defense.
"What I said at the end of last year, this year we have the same Achilles' heel defensively," said Hutchison, whose team finished 13-8 last season. "We're going to go as far as our defense can take us. Two games and we've got 10 errors. We're going to be able to hit. We're going to score some runs. But we've got to be better defensively."
NORTH DORCHESTER
Head Coach: Carol Hubbard.
Who's Where: Maggie Hubbard (Sr., C); Jewels Vroman (So., 1B/P); Emily Boyle (So., 2B); Kinsley Peters (Fr., SS); Maddie Nagel (Sr., 3B/P); Averi Warfield (Jr., LF); Mackenzie Lewis (Sr., CF); Lola Allen (Fr., RF); Journey Pearson (Fr., RF); Emilee Cohee (Sr., P/1B/3B); Brooke Outten (Jr., OF/DP); Abigail Sann (Fr., OF).
Outlook: With the return of first-team all-North picks Hubbard, Lewis and Cohee, the Eagles figure to again challenge at the division, conference, regional and — if they get that far — state levels.
And though she graduated her dynamic shortstop and leadoff hitter Anna Hopkins — now at Salisbury — Hubbard thinks this year's offense has the potential to be better.
"We lost a great offensive threat in Anna Hopkins," Hubbard said. "But I feel like some of the kids that we've picked up probably overall make us a little stronger offensively than we were last year."
QUEEN ANNE'S COUNTY
Head Coach: Andrew Stewart.
Who's Where: Emilie Smith (Sr., C); Morgan Gottleib (Sr., 1B); Emily Rendulic (Sr., 2B); Caroline Taylor (Sr., SS); Autumn Huber (Sr., 3B); Abbie Denes (Sr., LF); Cameryn Jacobi (Sr., CF); Abby Gunther (Sr., RF); Hannah Martin (So., P); Mikayla Livingston (Jr., C/RF); Nevaeh Truitt (Jr., OF/P); Kiera Corcoran (Jr., OF/C); Emily Hirschbock (So., P); Reese Brooks (So., OF).
Outlook: All-North second-team picks Huber, Denes and Taylor are back for a team that has a senior and experience at every position with the exception of sophomore pitcher Martin. Now, if the Lions can do what often escaped them last season and finish, they could challenge for a second 2A state title in four years.
"The big thing we have to do this year is finish," said Stewart, whose team finished 12-6 last year. "Something we couldn't do last year. We could not finish and I think this group, the leadership in the group, we're going to see that we're going to be able to finish games this year. Offensively and defensively.
"Defense looks extremely well right now," Stewart continued. "We're hitting the ball. We're seeing the ball. Couple miscues on the bases that got to clean up, but other than that, we're looking really good. As long as we hit the ball I think we're going to win. We're going to win a lot."
ST. MICHAELS
Head Coach: David Fisher.
Who's Where: Madi White (Sr., C); Ayla Gowe (Jr., 1B); Katie Jenkins (Sr., 2B); Myla Ramey (Sr., SS/P); Lola Browning (Jr., 3B); Bri Crow (Sr., LF); Brooke Reilly (Sr., CF); Haven Haddaway (Jr., RF); Angel Bock (Sr., P/SS/3B).
Outlook: The Saints went from getting humbled by Mardela in their season opener to routing Snow Hill. And with the rainy preseason — and more forecasted this week — Fisher said it's been hard to fix things.
Jenkins, White and Ramey earned all-North honorable-mention recognition a year ago, and Gowe and Browning return after missing last season due to injury. That combination could help in the effort to improve on last year's 8-10 record.
"We're experienced but inexperienced," Fisher said. "Having them adds a little more depth, a little more experience. Without them there we were going to be very inexperienced at the corners, which can be challenging."
Fisher said he's still trying to figure out his pitching, but if the Saints continue developing they could prove to be a sleeper in the second half of the season and the playoffs.
"We're slowing getting to where we want to be," Fisher said. "It's a work in progress. Everybody kind of knows their position, but getting everybody on the same page with each other is taking a little bit of time."
Editor's Note: Information was not available for Cambridge-South Dorchester.

ST. MICHAELS
Head Coach: David Fisher.
Who's Where: Madi White (Sr., C); Ayla Gowe (Jr., 1B); Katie Jenkins (Sr., 2B); Myla Ramey (Sr., SS/P); Lola Browning (Jr., 3B); Bri Crow (Sr., LF); Brooke Reilly (Sr., CF); Haven Haddaway (Jr., RF); Angel Bock (Sr., P/SS/3B).
Outlook: The Saints went from getting humbled by Mardela in their season opener to routing Snow Hill. And with the rainy preseason — and more forecasted this week — Fisher said it's been hard to fix things.
Jenkins, White and Ramey earned all-North honorable-mention recognition a year ago, and Gowe and Browning return after missing last season due to injury. That combination could help in the effort to improve on last year's 8-10 record.
"We're experienced but inexperienced," Fisher said. "Having them adds a little more depth, a little more experience. Without them there we were going to be very inexperienced at the corners, which can be challenging."
Fisher said he's still trying to figure out his pitching, but if the Saints continue developing they could prove to be a sleeper in the second half of the season and the playoffs.
"We're slowing getting to where we want to be," Fisher said. "It's a work in progress. Everybody kind of knows their position, but getting everybody on the same page with each other is taking a little bit of time."

title: STRONGHOLD
author: Bill Haufe
content:
STRONGHOLD

 March 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Stronghold 
 
 2225
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Colonel Richardson and St. Michaels baseball.It's one of the Bayside Conference's finer —if not finest — high school rivalries in any sport, and there's no signs why it shouldn't continue to be just that heading into this season.
Excluding the 2020 and '21 seasons, when the conference championship was not held due to COVID-19, either the Colonels or Saints have won the last nine North Bayside titles, with Colonel winning six and St. Michaels three.
Those two Class 1A heavyweights figure to be at the top of the division again this spring, though longtime Saints head coach Brian Femi wouldn't be surprised if there's company at the top.
"Kent Island and Queen Anne's always have a load of talent," Femi said. "And both are well coached, and both have a couple really good pitchers that can stifle you. And (North) Caroline has an amazing amount of young talent."
North Caroline, the last team other than Colonel or St. Michaels to win the North title back in 2012, is one of three area teams with a new head coach, as Vince Manetti takes the reins in Ridgely. Joe Brzeczek begins his first year as head coach at Saints Peter and Paul, while Garrett Nepert takes over at Colonel Richardson after Ryan Blanchfield's decision to step down during the preseason.
"I'm excited," said Nepert, a Colonel graduate who takes the helm of a program that has gone 39-9 over the past two years and reached back-to-back state finals under Blanchfield. "We've got a great group of guys. I couldn't be more thankful to walk in a couple weeks into the season with the group of guys we have."
Two of the guys who again make Colonel a state-title contender are senior Daniel Hesson, the 2023 North Bayside Player of the Year who recently signed with Salisbury University, and junior Jordan Regulski, a transfer from North Dorchester, who dueled Hesson in last year's Class 1A East Region II final.
Adding intrigue to the two regular-season dates between the Colonels and Saints — and potentially a Class 1A East Region I postseason showdown — is the return of Jacob Seek to St. Michaels. After spending last year at the Pro5 Baseball Academy in Fredericksburg, Virginia, Seek is back with the Saints for his senior year, bolstering one of the area's tougher staffs.
"Jake Seek coming back is certainly a big plus," Femi said.
Here's a look at this year's teams:
CAMBRIDGE-SD
Head Coach: Mike Tremper.
Who's Where: Noah Marshall (So., C); Nate Huber (Jr., 1B); Justin Marshall (So., 2B/RHP); Tanner Coulbourne (So., SS/RHP); Jacob Mitchell (Jr., 3B); Jaden Ferguson (Sr., LF); Collin Bair (So., CF); Donnell Cephas (Jr., RF); Kamarii Stanley (Jr., DH); Blake LaBelle (Sr., RHP); Landon Ludolph (Jr., RHP); Darnell Matthews (Sr.); Marvin Passmore (Sr.); Jacob Perry (Sr.); George Spry (Sr.).
Outlook: "It's just a rebuilding kind of season," said Tremper, who watched the Vikings go 2-17 last season. "Things are looking good for us. We just got to tie up some loose ends."
COLONEL RICHARDSON
Head Coach: Garrett Nepert.
Who's Where: Brayden Dadds (Sr., C); Daniel Hesson (Sr., LHP/1B); John Beaven (Fr., 2B/SS); Caleb Rouser (Fr., 2B/OF); Cam Todd (Sr., 2B); Jordan Regulski (Jr., RHP/SS); Gavin Whitby (Sr., 3B); Jack Walls (So., LHP/CF); Manny Wallace (Sr., OF/1B); Derrick Mitchell (So., OF).
Outlook: After helping call the shots as the starting catcher at Lock Raven (Pa.) University, Nepert returns to Colonel to begin his first head coaching job.
He takes over a program that went 19-5 last season and had two title bids ended by state champions, falling to 2A state champion Parkside in the Bayside championship before a heart-wrenching 3-2 loss in 11 innings to Clear Spring in the Class 1A state final. Those two losses alone could be enough motivation for the Colonels to push for return trips to both championship games this year.
Leading the way again is Hesson, a senior left-hander who last year went 3-0 with a 1.25 earned-run average, 92 strikeouts, 14 walks and two saves over 56 innings. Hesson was almost as troublesome at the plate, hitting a team-high .390 with 18 RBIs.
He is joined by Regulski, who was 4-1 with a 1.28 ERA and 59 strikeouts last year at North Dorchester where he earned the North Bayside Pitcher of the Year honor. Regulski was also more than solid at the plate, batting .377 with 14 RBIs and 17 runs scored.
"We're pretty confident in our pitching," said Nepert, whose rotation also includes Walls, a sophomore lefty. "We think we're going to be pretty strong on the mound. That's something typical of I guess the best teams at Colonel. We're feeling pretty good about the mound."
Nepert may also be excited as he looks around the field at what figures to be a solid defense, and his batting order.
"There's always pressure," Nepert said of trying to fill Blanchfield's shoes. "But pressure's a privilege.
"We want to be good in all three of those big parts of the game," Nepert continued. "I have a lot of confidence in our team, in our hitters and our fielders. And really I expect a lot out of them because I see how hard they work each and every day. So I'm expecting a lot out of our offense, defense and pitching.
EASTON
Head Coach: Albert Pritchett.
Who's Where: Colin Mooney (Jr., C); Josh Dressler (Sr., C/2B); Cullen Murphy (Sr., 1B/LHP); Alex Rhodes (Jr., 2B); Dustin Blue (So., SS/RHP); CJ Dugan (Sr., 3B); Dylan Cassell (Jr., LF); Kayden Webb (Jr., CF/RHP); Fin McGuckin (Sr., RF); Carter Mooney (So., LF); Garrett Fink (Jr., RHP); Dylan Fink (Sr., RHP); Michael O'Connor (Jr., 1B/LHP); Jonah Rich (Sr., IF); Noah George (Sr., IF); Evan Ensminger (Sr., OF).
Outlook: Pritchett hopes Monday's 18-1 loss to defending 2A state champion Parkside was just one of those bad days.
The Warriors certainly appear to have the personnel to move forward from that setback and perhaps push for their first division title since 2007. A first-team infield pick a year ago, Dugan (.355) starts at third base for the graduated Carson Brown, who led the North in homers (six) and RBIs (24) a year ago. Easton also returns Dressler (.395), Cassell (.317) and Webb (.333) — all second-team choices — from last year's 8-11 team.
"I think we've got pitching," Pritchett said. "Got a great outfield I think. We had no errors on Friday (against Washington), so I think we're going to have a good defense."
If Easton can hit it could contend, but Pritchett cautioned, "I think it's too early to tell."
KENT COUNTY
Head Coach: Jason Conner.
Who's Where: Scottie Ford (So., C/RHP); Noah Iacona (So., 1B); Liam Tidaback (Jr., 2B); Jack Walters (Sr., 2B/RF); Jace Conner (Jr., SS/RHP); BB Dean (So., 3B/RHP); Tanner Beck (Jr., LF/RHP); Trice Moore (Sr., CF); Aiden Crouch (So., LHP).
Outlook: The Trojans got off to a 3-1 start a year ago which included back-to-back wins over St. Michaels and Colonel Richardson, and finished 11-7, losing a 2-1 heartbreaker in the regional playoffs to North Dorchester.'
But with the graduation of all-North first-team picks Ryan Miller and Brandon Cannon, Kent lost the bulk of its pitching and a good chunk of offense.
"It's definitely different this year than last year for sure," said Jason Conner, who also graduated starting catcher Matt Wade. "We have a very young team."
With no junior varsity, the Trojans will carry 17 on varsity, including four freshman. Coach Conner will look to build around his son, Jace, and Dean, Ford, Beck and Iacona.
KENT ISLAND
Head Coach: Brendan Schulte.
Who's Where: Aiden Bonds (Jr., C); Patrick Reilly (Sr., 1B); Jack Grossi (So., 2B/RHP); Noah Anthony (Sr., SS); Hunter Austin (Sr., 3B/RHP); Kerry O'Brien (So., LF); Shane Bogardus (Sr., CF); Gavin Schulte (Jr., RF); Wyatt Offutt (Jr., OF/RHP); Traise Woolford (Jr., LHP); Logan Baierlien (So., RHP); Paul Horner (Jr., RHP).
Outlook: The return of first-team all-North picks Anthony (.340) and Grossi (.342) give the Bucs one of the division's more solid middle infields. The pitching staff looks strong with Austin (3-1 last year) joining Grossi, Offutt, Woolford, Baierlien and Horner.
"Definitely got some guys who can get on the bump and throw well," Schulte said.
Because he rotated players in and out of the lineup in preseason, Schulte was hesitant to judge his hitting, but does like what he has returning.
"Our top six in our lineup can definitely swing it, and we got some guys at the bottom end of the order who got some pretty solid swings," Schulte said. "What they are lacking right now is the experience of the varsity pitching.
After a slow start last year, the Bucs (13-6) went on a nine-game win streak before falling to Parkside, 2-1, in the 2A East II final.
"I like the chemistry," Schulte said. "We've got a young group of guys mixed in with a solid group of upperclassmen that are learning to work together very well. Each day gets a little bit better."
NORTH CAROLINE
Head Coach: Vince Manetti.
Who's Where: Caden Deavers (So., C); Cam King (Jr., 1B/RHP); Will Davis (Sr., 1B); Eric Deck (So., 2B); Thomas Necessary (Fr., SS); David Saathoff (Sr., 3B); Owen Carraballo (Fr., LF); Lewis Higgs (So., CF); Hayden Ogden (Sr., RF); Daylon Strange (Jr., LHP/LF); Johnny Radcliffe (Jr., 1B/LHP); Ethan Poore (So., RHP); Austin White-Eagle (Sr., OF); Jack Myers (Sr., OF); Colson Strange (Jr., OF); Wyatt Eaton (So., 1B/3B); Austin Frank (Jr., C/OF); Nathan D'Orlando (Sr., 1B/LHP); Jordan Kelley (Sr., OF/IF).
Outlook: After one year of coaching the junior varsity, Manetti succeeds Andrew Bishop, who stepped down after last season. The Bulldogs may not challenge for a division title, but that's not Manetti's focus in year one.
"My goal for this team is to just to start to play fundamental baseball," Manetti said. "I want them to do the little things right; moving runners over, playing solid defense. I'm just really looking to kind of build a good foundation for the future."
NORTH DORCHESTER
Head Coach: Dave Morrissette.
Who's Where: TJ Leonard (Jr., C/RHP); Calvin Simms (Sr., 1B); Manny Reyes (So., 2B); Wes Windsor (Sr., SS/RHP); John Boyle (Sr., SS/RHP); Blake Bramble (Jr., 3B); Nate Fracaroli (So., LF); Vernon Price (Sr., CF); Nate Swann (Jr., RF); Brock Warrell (Jr., DH); Brayden Phippen (Fr., IF/OF/RHP).
Outlook: The Eagles went 13-7 last year, closing on a six-game win streak before losing 5-4 to Colonel in the 1A East II final. Morrissette's big challenge will be finding replacements for Regulski — now at Colonel — at Bradley (4-2) — now at Rutgers-Camden (N.J.) College — on the mound.
"We got to figure out pitching wise who's going to make these plays and who's going to step in and fill those two holes," Morrissette said.
Windsor and Boyle should give the Eagles a solid one-two at the top of the rotation with Leonard at three.
A first-team all-North choice a year ago, Bramble led ND in hitting (.451, 23 RBIs, 18 runs) and Boyle hit .364 with 13 RBIs.
"I think offensively we'll be pretty good for the most part," Morrissette said. "We're still going to hit the ball really well."
QUEEN ANNE'S COUNTY
Head Coach: Chris Fitzgerald.
Who's Where: Dulin Clark (Jr., C); Dylan Wingate (So., C); Evan Dickey (Sr., 1B/LHP); Dylan Furrow (Sr., 1B); Noah Cramer (Jr., 2B); Bobby McCarthy (Sr., SS); Noah Palmer (Jr., 3B/RHP); Travis Sutch (Jr., LF/DH); Dalton Brown (Sr., CF/RHP); Colin Siwald (Sr., RF); Jacob Clough (Fr., Utility/RHP); Ethan Keppler (Jr., 2B/3B/RHP); Gavin Leith (Sr., OF); Brendan Parsley (Jr., OF).
Outlook: Despite losing 10 seniors from last year's 12-7 team, Fitzgerald is stoked for the season.
"It's just a really good group of kids that are coachable," Fitzgerald said. "I'm really excited about this year. Our jayvee looks good. I think we have enough arms at the varsity level, and enough seniors that we could really be good this year."
The Lions could be really good at the plate with the return of first-team all-North picks Brown (.435, 10 RBIs) and Dickey (.431, 22 RBIs), and second-teamers Clark (.407, 13 RBIs) and Siwald (.395, 13 RBIs).
The graduated Devin Canter and Cole Glanding combined for nine wins last year, but Dickey (2-4) had a team-low 0.98 ERA and a team-high 46 strikeouts against just 15 walks.
ST. MICHAELS
Head Coach: Brian Femi.
Who's Where: Henry Mulliken (Sr., C); Anthony Massaro (Sr., 1B/LHP); Ethan Royer (So., SS); Brock Grow (So., 2B/RHP); Will Sherwood (Jr., RHP/OF/1B/3B); Pearson Greenwood (Jr., 3B); Jacob Bealefeld (Sr., RHP/3B/OF); Hunter Gottlieb (Sr., LF); Connor Wheeler (So., CF); Bobby Fink (Jr., RHP/RF); Eli Wallace (So., RHP); Jacob Seek (Sr., LHP).
Outlook: The Saints figure to improve on last year's 10-10 slate with the return of not only Seek. Wheeler, who led the team in hitting last year as a freshman (.429), and the versatile Sherwood (.380), who in addition to providing another strong arm, can DH and play almost anywhere in the field, were both first-team all-North picks a year ago.
They are joined by Wallace, who had the team's best record on the mound (3-1) last year as a freshman, fellow all-North second teamer Massaro, as well as Grow, Bealefeld and Queen Anne's transfer Fink.
"I think that's been our strength in the preseason" Femi said of his pitching." They've thrown really well. That's been a real plus for us. And we've actually played pretty good defense. We need to hit better. That's a big part of baseball."
The fact the Saints faced Wallenpaupack (Pa.), Patuxent, Severna Park and Stephen Decatur during the preseason was a large factor for that lack of preseason hitting.
"We're still trying to figure out how we can get our best nine batters in the lineup," said Femi, whose team has opened the season 2-0.

CLOSING STATEMENTS

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 Words 

 Read News Document

 UPPER MARLBORO — Giuseppe Mellinger didn't storm past his coaches, chuck his headgear in a fury, or try to leave an impression on the nearest concrete wall with his fist.The opportunity to direct blame was certainly there, but the Kent Island High senior refused to point a finger.
"I'm not going to make excuses for myself," Mellinger said in the wake of a 3-2 ultimate-tiebreaker loss in the 175-pound final during the Class 2A/1A state wrestling championship tournament at the Show Place Arena on March 2. "You try not to let refs dictate your match. Wrestling you know, you've got to be accountable. It's only you out there wrestling somebody else."
Of the 16 wrestlers from North Bayside schools that qualified for states, Mellinger was the only one to reach the finals in the boys competition.
"Coming from Kent Island, we rarely have people that make it that far," said Mellinger, who became just the third Buccaneer to reach the finals during Tommy Sitar's eight seasons as head coach — joining Matt Miller (2020) and Justin Thomas (2016). "So it was surreal to be there in that moment.
"Senior year. You've wrestled three years of high school," Mellinger added. "Wrestled since you were like five or six years old, and then you make it to the state finals. Like wow. This is it. But I felt pretty confident. I felt relaxed. That was my last match ever so I'm going to go out there and let it fly. Like it's just one more match."
On the way to that last match, Mellinger had earned a first-round 15-13 win over Hammond's Jaden Timithy in the first sudden-victory period, took a forfeit in the quarterfinals, then defeated Middletown senior Kashton Dalhouse (47-4) via a 5-4 decision in the semifinals.
That set up his title shot with South Carroll sophomore Anthony Rodrigues (47-3). With 45 seconds remaining in the first period, the lead official held up two fingers, signaling a two-point takedown for Mellinger. But that initial call was waved off when the official ruled Mellinger did not to have enough control.
"I thought I did too," said Mellinger when asked if he thought he had the takedown. "I didn't hear anybody argue against it. And the South Carroll guys, their body language was like, 'Yeah, wow. We got saved on that one.'"
Though he did not protest or go to the scorer's table for an explanation, Sitar also thought Mellinger had a takedown.
"I would have liked to see that call stand at two," Sitar said. "It wasn't something where they came to the table an overturned it or anything like that, or even that the second ref came in and overturned it."
It remained scoreless through the remainder of the first. Starting on bottom, Rodrigues scored an escape just two seconds into the second period for a 1-0 lead. Sixteen seconds into the third, Mellinger escaped off bottom, to make it 1-1. Mellinger blocked a shot 14 seconds later and after two restarts, the score remained 1-1 heading into overtime.
Mellinger got two deep shots in during the 1-minute overtime, but Rodrigues wouldn't be taken down as the duel moved into the two 30-second ride-out periods. Rodrigues again escaped with only two seconds elapsed for a 2-1 lead. Mellinger answered with an escape with six seconds left in the second ride-out, forging a 2-2 deadlock heading into the ultimate tiebreaker.
Because he had scored the match's first point, Rodrigues got to choose top or bottom to start the final period. Rodrigues took bottom and six seconds into the final stage pulled his left leg from Mellinger's grasp for a 3-2 victory.
"That (takedown) would have won the championship," said Sitar (39-6), who was bidding to become Kent Island's first state champion since 2015 when Stevan Smith won his second straight state title. "Whoever had a takedown was going to win because shots were so hard.
"I was hoping for a state title," Mellinger added. "But at the end of the day I was the aggressive wrestler. As the match went on, offense got harder and harder, especially when we got sweaty. Nothing you can down now."
Kent Island senior Greg Couch (132 pounds) had his hopes for a state championship end in Friday's semifinal round, when he lost a 12-6 decision to defending — and eventual — state champion JoJo Gigliotti of South Carroll.
"I think he gave him his toughest match," Sitar said of Couch's battle with Gigliotti. "I think he knew he had a match with Couch. I think had Couch been on the other side of the bracket I might have had a couple of finalists. Greg wrestled his butt off. He was peaking at the right time."
Couch looked headed for the consolation bracket, when he fell behind 4-0 in the first period of his opening match to Southern Garrett's Hayden Harvey.
"He got taken down twice and then it was like the switch was flipped," Sitar said of Couch. "He was ready to go. He was comfortable and he just let the rest of the weight class have it from there."
Starting with Harvey, who would not score another point while Couch was rallying for a 13-4 major decision. Couch earned a 7-1 decision over Huntingtown senior Jett Cramer (24-5) in the quarterfinals but then lost 12-6 to Gigliotti (51-1), who pinned his other three opponents in the tournament en route to his second state title.
"When I got into the consi round I realized, 'This is all or nothing,'" Couch said. "'This is my senior year. This is all I got left.'"
And it took some doing.
Couch and C. Milton Wright's Mitchell Nguyen (36-8) were tied 2-2 through regulation and overtime. Couch then rode Nguyen out through the first ride-out stage before working an escape in the second ride-out for a 3-2 win.
"That was definitely one of my hardest matches of the year, it not the hardest," Couch said of his bout with Nguyen.
In the consolation final, Couch crafted a 7-2 victory over Northern Garrett's Mason Glotfelty (39-5) for his 100th career victory and a third-place finish.
"I had a lot going through my mind before that last match," said Couch, who finished 33-9. "I had the support of my family. My dad and my uncle were on the mat coaching for me in my corner. It definitely provided me with everything I needed for that last match.
"It was definitely a hard path back to try to get third," Couch said. "They say second place usually looks the most upset and third is smiling a lot more, and I can definitely agree with that. Definitely makes a difference ending it on a win rather than a loss."
Queen Anne's County senior Tremaine Jackson earned his 100th career win when he earned a 54-second fall in his first-round match on Thursday, but watched his state-title aspirations end Friday with a 4-2 loss to Northern Garrett's Devon Opel (38-7) in the 126-pound quarterfinals.
"I had the whole night (Friday) to think about what happened," Jackson said of his loss. "I mean it hurt, but I knew I just had to bounce back, just start doing what I do best."
Jackson's road to the consolation final started Saturday morning with a 15-0 technical fall over Liberty's Alex Pearl in 3:15. He advanced to the consolation semifinals with a forfeit, then put together a 13-0 major decision over Eastern Vo Tech's Chase Ullman."
"The tech fall, the (Pearl) kid walked off the mat and he was like, 'Man, that kid is fricking good,' when he shook my hand," Queen Anne's head coach David Stricker said. "We were like, 'Yeah, we know.'
"He could just stop putting the pressure on himself and just go be Tremaine, and pretty much show off his full talents; his full arsenal," Stricker said of Jackson after his quarterfinal loss. "When he's there and he can just let it fly, there's not a whole lot of people that can stop him."
That included Rising Sun's Xzavier Brown, who faced off for a fourth time this season against Jackson in the consolation final and lost 5-2.
"It was close but I feel like I calculated that match," said Jackson, whose second consecutive third-place finish at states capped a 40-4 season. "I wrestled him a bunch of times. And that was my last high school match, so I was coming out on top regardless."

title: ESCR schedules Learn-to-Row clinics for May
author: Bill Haufe
content:
ESCR schedules Learn-to-Row clinics for May

 March 20, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 369
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — The Eastern Shore Community Rowers, an adult rowing program, has scheduled free information sessions for April 20 and May 4, from 8:30-9:30 a.m., at Evergreen 770 Port Street.This is a chance for interested rowers to meet the ESCR coaches and team members, learn about the boats, and how rowing is the most fun exercise on the Shore.
"There is nothing else like it," said Doug Webb, a new member who recently began rowing. "It has changed my life."
ESCR members learn to row a variety of boats, from eight-person boats to single-sculling boats.
ESCR has scheduled two week-long Learn-to-Row clinics, May 13-18 and May 20-23. The clinics are Monday through Thursday from 5:30-7:30 p.m., and Saturdays, from 8:30-10:30 a.m. The cost is $400 for the week-long, three-coach lessons of which 50% can be applied to membership for those who wish to join the club.
ESCR is dedicated to teaching the community to row while offering more access to area rivers. The club welcomes everyone and offers scholarships.
Beginners are encouraged to join the Learn-To-Row clinics, or to take private lessons from one of ESCR's accredited coaches to acquire the skills needed for practices.
"The only criteria," Board Safety Officer and registered nurse, Terry Gleim said, "are that you be able to swim and that you are strong enough to properly hold an oar and help lift the boats."
If swimming is an obstacle, ESCR will assist in helping you learn.
All scheduled workouts are accompanied by a chase boat for safety and coaching.
The rowing season runs from March through December, with early morning workouts Monday, Wednesday and Friday, and later morning rows on Tuesday and Thursday. Saturday rows are at 7:30 a.m. for all members. Evening rows are available for more experienced scullers during the summer.
"ESCR is open to anyone over 18 interested in having fun, getting healthy, and appreciating our beautiful waters," said Chloe Tong, the executive director. "The health of our rivers, as well as personal health, is an intrinsic part of our conversation."
As a non-profit, Eastern Shore Community Rowers raises money through private donations, grants, and membership dues needed to fund additional boats and necessary equipment for next year's season.
For more information visit www.ESCRowers.org, or email head coach Chloe Allen: Director@escrowers.org

title: Scheffler has a big game buty not a big head
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Scheffler has a big game buty not a big head

 March 19, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 879
 Words 

 Read News Document

 PONTE VEDRA BEACH, Fla. — Scottie Scheffler would rank near the bottom if the popular "strokes gained" statistic of golf had a category for celebrations. And he would be the first to concede that.Just two weeks ago — right before he earned $8.5 million for winning two big trophies in a span of 10 days and erased any questions whether he deserved to be ranked No. 1 in the world — Scheffler spoke about how quickly he can forget the past, win or lose.
"I don't celebrate accomplishments that well. I don't feel like I dwell on failures that much either," Scheffler said. "If you ask my wife, she would say I need to celebrate more. She's definitely right."
Then he won the Arnold Palmer Invitational and the celebration was on — cheeseburgers in the Bay Hill clubhouse with his family, followed by a two-hour drive to the TPC Sawgrass.
Woo-hoo!
The day after Scheffler became the only player in 50 editions of The Players Championship to win back to back, he was texting swing coach Randy Smith about their practice schedule.
Scheffler is a big man in golf with a big game. What he lacks is a big head.
"Given the things that have gone on the last year or so, and watching him, he is definitely grounded — more than what you can dream of," Smith said. "And he has created a lot of things that could keep him from being grounded.
"He knows you're not bigger than anything else because of anything you do."
The money?
His latest victory pushed him over $50 million for his PGA Tour earnings in just five years, one spot ahead of Jon Rahm on the career money list. Rahm had a four-year head start.
The ranking?
He has been at No. 1 since last May, and his gap over everyone else is the largest since Dustin Johnson seven years ago. Barring injury, Scheffler has a chance to become the first player since Tiger Woods in 2009 to hold the No. 1 ranking for an entire calendar year.
The platform?
Scheffler doesn't go out of his way to share his opinions. Insightful answers start with a good question, though he showed last week he is not afraid to speak his mind. He was asked whether fans were disillusioned by the splintering between the PGA Tour and LIV Golf.
"If the fans are upset, then look at the guys that left," he said. "We had a tour, we were all together, and the people that left are no longer here. At the end of the day, that's where all the splintering comes from. As far as our tour goes, we're doing our best to create the best product for the fans."
And then there's the attention, the least of his worries because Scheffler doesn't spend much time on social media.
He also takes precautions not to listen or read about himself, whether it's his nine worldwide wins in the last 25 months, his two PGA Tour awards as player or the year or the putting struggles that kept him from winning even more.
"When it comes to reading things about yourself, let's say I remember all the good things. Then I walk around with a big head thinking, 'This is how great I am.' That's not good, either," Scheffler said in an interview before he went on his most recent run.
"If I read the bad stuff, that's all I'm going to remember is the bad stuff. 'Scottie can't putt. He hadn't won in a year. Is he the best player in the world?' It's a losing game."
Mostly what keeps him grounded are the people around him. His mother has been a chief operating officer for law firms in New York and Dallas, and his father stayed at home with Scheffler and his three sisters.
His wife, Meredith, is pregnant with their first child, due around the end of April. She's the one who told Scheffler on Sunday morning of the 2022 Masters, when he had a three-shot lead and woke up with tears and self-doubt, "Who are you to say that you are not ready?"
He wound up winning his first major, building such a big lead he mindlessly four-putted on the final hole and still won by two. More tears.
"Crying for me is not an abnormal thing," he said with a laugh.
That much was clear when he was at TPC Sawgrass a few weeks ago to promote The Players, reliving the winning moment on the 18th green. His voice choked up just mentioning his family.
"I always get emotional when I talk about Meredith for some reason," he said.
That was the point Scheffler drove home Sunday evening, as he moved the gold trophy on the table to be able to make eye contact with whomever was asking a question.
"At the end of the day, it all goes back to the support system I have at home," he said. "I have a great wife, and if I started taking my trophies and putting them all over the house and walking in all big-time, I think she would smack me on the side of the head and tell me to get over myself pretty quickly.
"Winning golf tournaments doesn't give me any brownie points at home," he said, stifling a laugh. "So I just try and do my best."
It seems to be working.

title: NEW HEIGHTS
author: Bill Haufe
content:
NEW HEIGHTS

 March 19, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 804
 Words 

 Read News Document

 As March Madness is set to tip off, three of the most recognizable names in college basketball are in the women's tournament: Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers.Clark drew record crowds and ratings all season long. Reese has LSU in contention for a second straight national championship. Bueckers is finally healthy and doing things on the court for UConn reminiscent of her freshman season when she was the AP Player of the Year.
Throw in a few stellar freshmen like JuJu Watkins and Hannah Hidalgo and the game is reaching heights it's never seen.
"One thousand percent we've seen a shift in just the perception of women's college basketball in general," USC coach Lindsay Gottlieb said. "It doesn't have to be at the detriment of men's college basketball. The increased coverage and star power these players have; they are legitimate, popcorn-worthy type of players."
For countless seasons, the buzz around the NCAA tournaments have often been on the men's game. The one-and-done stars, the juggernaut blueblood programs, the buzzer beaters and athleticism all getting more attention. The women's game has pretty much all of that too, and the ratings and attendance this season suggest casual fans are fully engaged with a game that boasts star power and an increasingly high level of play.
It helps that the women's players stick around for three, four or even five years without the chance to leave early for the pros so fans get to know them and watch them grow. Three years ago, Clark said she thought women's players should be allowed to turn pro after their freshman year, like the men can.
Instead, she stuck around and had a record-setting year that grabbed the nation's attention.
"It's really, really evident that there's stars out there in this game," UConn coach Geno Auriemma said. "Whereas before I think they were there, but nobody wanted to acknowledge it and appreciate it as much. ... They're just really good. Everybody is going around telling everybody how good they are. They're all visible."
ESPN said it just saw the most watched women's college basketball regular season in more than 15 years, with viewership up 37% on its platforms from last season. That doesn't really even include the Clark effect as Iowa's star wasn't on the network much this season. Iowa's ratings on Fox Sports were the highest in a generation.
ESPN plans to show all of Iowa's games, including a few on ABC, as far as the No. 1 seed advances in the tourney.
"It's not just UConn and Tennessee on TV," Auriemma said. "Those kids are on TV a lot. They're in the limelight a lot. They know how to handle it because they're used to it now."
Clark, who broke the NCAA all-time scoring record this season, has helped six different networks reach all-time viewership marks for women's basketball over the past year, starting with last season's NCAA championship game that drew nearly 10 million viewers.
"I kind of get to be in the spotlight and I get to change people's viewpoint of how they see women's basketball," Clark said before the season. "The amount of people that have come up to me and said, 'I've never watched women's basketball before before you and your team ... .' Some people could take that as a negative. But to me that's a positive. We're finally getting them to turn on the TV and watch it, but not only watch it once. They're coming back for more."
People aren't just watching, they are also coming to games too. All five of the power conferences had huge crowds for their tournaments. The SEC and Big Ten had their best attendance ever. The Pac-12, ACC and Big 12 weren't far behind.
"The big names continue to put up big numbers and people are watching and the media is paying attention," Bueckers said. "The tournament will be great and will continue the rise of women's basketball."
Fans who pack the arenas are also sticking around afterward, hoping to get a coveted autograph. The importance of the moment isn't lost on the game's stars. Clark, Reese, Bueckers, Watkins and many others spend time postgame signing and taking pictures with not only young girls, but boys, too.
"There were 400 people in the stands before she got here and now we're selling out," Gottlieb said of Watkins. "We've got NBA players who want to see her, WNBA players, musicians and actors too. Regular fans also, it's a diversified crowd. Little boys and girls who ask me if I know JuJu. Could they meet Juju? Grown men you run into in downtown LA."
Even when Clark leaves for the WNBA after the NCAA Tournament, the future of women's basketball is still strong with Bueckers, Watkins, Hidalgo and many other up-and-coming players.
"It's going to get even better. So many kids coming out of high school are just unbelievably good," Auriemma said.

title: Vikings' title shot falls shy
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Vikings' title shot falls shy

 March 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1051
 Words 

 Read News Document

 COLLEGE PARK — Maybe the stage was too big. Or maybe the team from the big city was just too good.Either way, Cambridge-South Dorchester High wasn't going away.
Down 10 in the first quarter, the Vikings rallied to pull even with Edmondson-Westside of Baltimore with under a minute to play in the first half.
Maybe the defending state champions thought an early third-quarter flurry that pushed their lead to 11 was enough to wilt the team from the Eastern Shore. No such luck. Again Cambridge-SD battled back to tie with one quarter remaining.
Certainly the back-to-back 3-pointers that gave the Red Storm a nine-point cushion with less than three minutes left was enough to make their opponent concede. Still no dice, as Cambridge-SD twice cut that deficit to four in the final two minutes.
"They wouldn't quit," Edmondson head coach Darnell Dantzler said of the Vikings.
They wouldn't. But they wouldn't win either.
No. 2 seed Edmondson converted 5 of 6 free throws in the closing 33 seconds Saturday to finally seal a 69-65 victory over top-seeded Cambridge-SD in the Class 1A state boys' basketball championship at the University of Maryland's Xfinity Center.
"Unfortunately, we didn't come out on the right side of the clock and the game," said Cambridge-SD head coach Shawn Parker, whose team finished the season 25-3. "But man, you saw, they fought to the end. And that's what these guys have been doing all year; fighting 'til the end."
Bidding for its first state basketball title since 1996, Cambridge-SD fell behind 14-4 with less than a minute left in the first quarter, when Edmondson's Kyrie Sherrod hit a 3-pointer. Senior guard LaShaun Moody (team-high 17 points, 10 rebounds) scored a layup and a pair of free throws to get the Vikings within six before Xavier Davis (11 points) scored to beat the buzzer and give the Red Storm (26-2) a 17-8 lead after the first quarter.
Down eight, Cambridge-SD pieced together the first of its comebacks. Semaj Pinder (11 points) and Sterling Perkins drained back-to-back 3-pointers before Kobe Ennals (12 points) scored a lay-in to forge a 23-23 tie with 51 seconds left in the first half.
But Chase Foster, Edmondson's talented 6-foot-10 sophomore center who finished with 18 points, 13 rebounds and five blocked shots, hit a pair of free throws before Sherrod drilled a 3-pointer just before the halftime buzzer for a 28-23 Red Storm lead.
Edmondson looked on the verge of taking control in the opening 2:33 of the third quarter, as Ennals picked up his third foul while the Red Storm were in the midst of a 10-4 run that gave them a 38-27 lead with 5:27 to go in the third.
But trailing 39-31, Cambridge-SD again began whittling away its deficit. Moody made a three-point play, then scored on a put-back to make it a three-point game. Darnell Dantzler Jr.'s jumper with 2:07 to go in the third gave the Red Storm a 45-38 lead.
But Darren Belizaire (10 points) hit a trey. Moody made yet another three-point play. Belizaire converted one of two free throws, before Moody zipped one of his five assists to Anthony Hughes for a layup just before the buzzer, tying the game at 47-all entering the fourth.
"Unfortunately, you don't want to get down that big 'cause it takes a lot of energy to come back," Tucker said. "But one word that sticks out to my head is resilient. We're resilient. No matter what, we're going to fight until the end and that's what we did."
Foster's follow nudged the Red Storm back in front at 49-47. Ennals answered with a jumper to create the game's fourth and final tie.
It remained close. But Josiah Brown (13 points) hit two free throws and a 3-pointer before Sherrod nailed a 3 for a 60-51 Edmondson lead with 2:20 remaining.
Pinder's 3-pointer and Hughes' layup off a steal pulled Cambridge-SD within 60-56 with 1:57 left.
"They played hard," Coach Dantzler said. "Even when we went up a couple points they came down and hit a couple big shots."
Dantzler Jr. scored on a drive, extending Edmondson's lead to 62-56. Ennals hit a free throw. Brown scored inside to make it 64-57 Red Storm. But Pinder drilled a 3-pointer with 52 seconds left, getting the Vikings within four again at 64-60.
Brown made one of two free throws with 33.4 seconds left for a five-point edge. Pinder fouled out when he was called for a charge. Ennals tipped the ensuing inbounds pass, but the Vikings could not come up with the ball. A quick foul by Moody sent Foster to the foul line, where he made both free throws for a 67-60 lead with 19.9 left.
Belizaire connected for a 3-pointer with 10.6 seconds left, drawing Cambridge-SD within 67-63. But Dantzler Jr. hit a pair of free throws with 9 seconds to go for a 69-63 advantage.
"It says that we wanted it," Moody said when asked about the Vikings' unwillingness to fold. "We came up a little short but it definitely says that we wanted it."
Tucker agreed.
"When that buzzer went off we just fell a little short," Tucker said. "We competed. We showed everybody in the state of Maryland that we can compete."
It was Edmondson's fourth state championship under Dantzler, and the second time the Red Storm have won consecutive titles, matching the 2013 and '14 teams. But it was the first time Edmondson has won the Baltimore city title and state championship in the same year.
"It just speaks volumes about these kids," said Dantzler, who has coached Edmondson for 18 seasons. "They went undefeated in Baltimore city, they won the city championship, and then to come in and win the state championship. Who could ask for anything more when it comes to these kids? This is the best record I had overall to be 26-2. It's a remarkable season that these guys had."
Dantzler had similar praise for Cambridge-SD.
"I told all of them when we were shaking hands that they played well," Dantzler said. "And I told the coach I know this is only his first year down here, and he's only a second-year coach, but they did a remarkable job."
