title: Sabres' first game may be toughest of season
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Sabres' first game may be toughest of season

 March 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 632
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Saints Peter and Paul High's girls lacrosse team may not play a tougher opponent this season."I knew this was going to be a great matchup," Sabres head coach Alison Beyer said of Friday's season-opening clash with St. Mary's. "It was just an exciting game to watch. This is how lacrosse should be, and that's what I told them at halftime. I said, 'Just play lacrosse. Play like you know how to play.' And that's what they did."
Sts. Peter & Paul shaved a five-goal deficit to one midway through the third quarter, but couldn't get any closer, as the Saints scored seven of the game's last eight goals on the way to a 16-9 victory on a cloudy afternoon.
"This will be our toughest game of the season," Beyer said. "I got to see how I know they can play. I saw some real good things."
Among those good things was sophomore goalie Kylie Kroniser, who made five big saves to keep the Sabres within striking distance until late.
"Kylie (Kroniser) played a heckuva game," Beyer said. "She was on fire. I'm loving Kylie this year. It could have been way worse than it was. She made some real difficult saves, at real key moments too. That was crucial."
Sophomore Caroline Ewing (three goals) scored twice and classmate Avery McCall (three goals) once to give Sts. Peter & Paul and early 3-2 lead. But Sydney DeMaio (two goals), Kendall Kemezis and Anna Ervin (two goals) each scored in a 2-minute, 21-second span to give St. Mary's a 5-3 lead after one quarter,
Ervin scored her second goal 39 seconds into the second quarter, but Sabres senior Morgan Quade countered. Circling from behind the net, Quade took a stick check to the head before slipping a shot past St. Mary's goalie Addy Drain to get Sts. Peter & Paul back within two at 6-4.
But St. Mary's steadily passed the ball around the perimeter before working a weave in front of Kroniser that produced goals from Chloe Wiese (hat trick), Ellie Spurge and Jayci Frederick for a 9-4 advantage heading into the break.
"St. Mary's knew how to work us," said Beyer, who watched nine different Saints score, including six with multiple goals. "And they're just good. They knew exactly what angle to get through our defense, and they were killing us on the slide."
Sts. Peter & Paul rallied though in the third quarter.
Ewing bounced a free-position opportunity into the net 1:15 into the third. Freshman Emery Zimmerman tallied on another free-position chance with just under 9 minutes left in the period. McCall capitalized on another free-position shot with an overhand shot, drawing the Sabres within 9-7. Quade then took possession behind the left post, was knocked off her feet, but on the way down slid a shot into the net to make it 9-8 with 5:31 to go in the third.
"I love that I have so many contributors," Beyer said. "We have such a young team this year. And again, like every year, I can put my girls on offense or defense. And I can move them around and switch them back and forth. And no matter, I have contributors at every angle."
St. Mary's also appears to have a slew of contributors heading into the season, and showed that quality the remainder of the game. Marin Hodor (two goals) and Frederick (two goals) scored 10 seconds apart to give the Saints an 11-8 lead entering the fourth quarter.
McCall scored 38 seconds into the fourth to get the Sabres within two. But St. Mary's got two goals from Wiese and one apiece from Hodor, Grace Mitchell (two) and Maggie Marohl over the final 10:32 to pull away.
"It just happened our very first game was against St. Mary's and this was the best game of the season." Beyer said.

title: Hard Knocks: Maryland's women of roller derby
author: Ted Black tblack@somdnews.com
content:
Hard Knocks: Maryland's women of roller derby

 March 15, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Ted Black tblack@somdnews.com | Section: State News 
 
 503
 Words 

 Read News Document

 While they may not have all been childhood friends who grew up in close proximity to one another, the members of the 301 Derby Dames roller derby team that competed in their season opener on Saturday evening at the Charles County Fairgrounds have since been able to form a genuine common bond.The 301 Derby Dames defeated the DC Roller Derby 399-56 on March 9 in front of a packed facility of family and friends who lined the mat inside the pavilion. When many of the current members of the 301 Derby Dames initially joined the team 10 years ago, they practiced and played on the concrete floor of the building. It has since been covered with a softer, yet slicker mat.
"I love being able to come out here and play with these women," said Lauren (Creech) Hare, who was born and raised in Charles County and is a 2006 Lackey High graduate. "I first joined back in 2015, but then I took a few years off when I had some kids. Now that they're a little older, I came back and it's been a lot of fun."
On Saturday evening, Hare, whose roller derby moniker is "Vicious Creature" a play on her maiden name, was named the most valuable player of the 301 Derby Dames by members of the opposing DC Roller Derby. At the end of each bout, each team is asked to select the top blocker and top jammer of their respective foe from that evening's contest, and Creech was the choice as top jammer.
Kristi Zapfe, who goes by the simplistic "Zap" during the matches, was born and raised in Chicago and after her time in the Navy relocated to St. Mary's County. Initially while in the Navy, Zapfe had thoughts of playing rugby, but one of her fellow midshipman encouraged her to pursue the roller derby circuit and she has been part of the 301 Derby Dames for the past four years.
"I'm not entirely sure what brought me to St. Mary's County, but I'm glad that I did," Zapfe said. "I really enjoy being able to practice and play with these women. It gives us all a chance to grow together and bond together and participate in a sport that we love and where we can knock each other down."
Hal Metzler is the coach of the 301 Derby Dames and each week he enjoys having the women come together for practices and then roughly six or seven bouts each season. Like his players, Metzler is there on a voluntary basis and simply enjoys the camaraderie of practicing and playing together in front of their enthusiastic family and friends.
"For me, the fun is seeing how competitive the women can be while still having a fun time," Metlzer said. "At the end of the day, no one is getting paid. No one is going pro. It's just a good chance for them to have a good time doing something they love and having their family and friends here to cheer them on."

title: C-SD locked in for last dance
author: Bill Haufe
content:
C-SD locked in for last dance

 March 14, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 964
 Words 

 Read News Document

 When Darnell Dantzler brought his Edmondson-Westside High boys basketball team together for its first practice Nov. 15, he established the same goal he's set the previous 17 seasons as head coach — winning a state title.That same day, Shawn Tucker, starting just his second season as Cambridge-South Dorchester's head coach, provided a string of goals for his team that included winning the North Bayside regular-season title, the Bayside Conference championship, the Class 1A East Region II crown and the state championship.
Tucker and the top-seeded Vikings (24-1) hope to complete that title string Saturday beginning at 1 p.m., when they face the No. 2 seed and defending state-champion Red Storm (22-2) for the Class 1A state championship at the University of Maryland's Xfinity Center.
"You had a lot of good pieces that needed to learn to play basketball together as a team really quickly," Tucker said, recalling his first impression of this season's team. "But there wasn't quite a team."
Tucker has quite a team on his hands now, one that won its first 13 games this season, lost its one and only game to Queen Anne's, then reeled off 11 consecutive wins to earn a shot at the school's first state title in basketball since 1996.
"It's going to be a really, really good challenge," Tucker said of Edmondson. "But I go back to us playing in the Bayside (Conference) championship versus a team like (Stephen) Decatur. It prepared us."
Cambridge-SD fell behind 8-0 to Decatur on Feb. 22, settled itself, then raced to its first outright conference championship since 1996.
The Vikings got off to blazing starts in their state quarterfinal and semifinals wins. The second of those came Tuesday against Fort Hill, when a one-time 17-point lead was whittled to just three with 5:38 remaining. But instead of calling timeout, Tucker let his team continuing playing, and watched as Anthony Hughes came up with two huge steals to spark a decisive 8-0 Vikings run.
"When that kid hit a three, I could have called a timeout," Tucker said of Jabril Daniels' trey that got the Sentinels within 47-44. "And I looked at them and I said, 'Nope.' I'm going to let them play through that because this is the only way they're going to learn this scenario. They know that's me. In that situation, I call a timeout and I don't have any faith in them. So by not calling that timeout, it showed them that I faith in them and they responded."
Now, the Vikings prepare for an Edmondson program that makes its sixth final appearance in Dantzler's 18 seasons at the helm, which include state championships in 2013, '14 and '23.
"First day of practice my goal always is to make it to the state championship, setting goals up as high as you can set 'em," Dantzler said during a phone interview Wednesday. "But sometime being realistic, you might not be as good. But the number one goal is to always win a state championship."
Danztler though wasn't sure the Red Storm would get the chance to defend their title this season.
"I'm really surprised," Dantzler said of reaching the state final. "We had a couple of people that graduated and transferred out. So going into the season I didn't think we were going to make it there. But through playing hard, I'm just happy and fortunate to make it there."
Adding even more meaning to this championship trip for Dantzler is the fact his son, Darnell Jr., is the Red Storm's starting point guard.
"It's been a dream come true," Coach Dantzler said. "Sometimes it's tough trying to draw the line as father and coach, but I wouldn't trade it for the world, just to have the experience of him being a part of my team, and me being part of his success for his high school career."
A 5-foot-9 junior, Dantzler Jr. has averaged 16.5 points and 11 assists a game this season. He is joined in the backcourt by senior Kyrie Sherrod (13.3 points per game). Then there is Edmondson's frontcourt that features 6-8 sophomore forward Chase Foster (19.8 ppg.; 11 rebounds per game) and 6-4 senior forward Josiah Brown (14.5 ppg., 11.5 rpg.).
"They've played hard all season," Coach Dantzler said. "Hopefully we can bring it home when we play."
That is also the hopes of a Cambridge-SD team that has hounded the opposition on defense this season and attacked the boards on both ends of the floor.
Leading the attack has been 5-9 senior point guard LaShaun Moody (25 ppg.) whose quickness has been a problem for opponents on both ends of the court. Moody may run the show, but has plenty of help. Koby Ennals, a 6-5 junior (19 ppg., 10 rpg), can slash to the rim or bury the 3-pointer. And there's the 6-2 Hughes (10 points), who has come up with huge rebounds, steals and buckets throughout the Vikings' run.
Complementing that trio has been a rotation that includes junior Darren Belizare and sophomores Semaj Pinder, Sterling Perkins (12 ppg) and Thomas Wilson, who have more than made their share of big plays throughout this season.
"I hear they're really good," Coach Dantzler said of Cambridge-SD.
Really good, and really locked in, a quality Tucker has praised during this postseason stretch.
"I wish people could be in the locker room for the pre-game speech," Tucker said. "When I say they are zeroed in, they are locked in. And I've never experienced a group of young men that get locked in so fast. Like one minute they can be joking and playing and when we say, 'All right, let's go,' they just locked in immediately. I thought that wasn't something possible, 'cause you know you can get caught turning that switch on and off. When they lock in, they're in. And that's the way we're going to have to be against Edmondson."

title: GOLDEN DELIVERY
author: Bill Haufe
content:
GOLDEN DELIVERY

 March 14, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 962
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Easton High head swim coach Tim Kroeger calls the 200-yard freestyle a hard race to swim."Everybody seems to have a love-hate relationship with that event because it's too short to be distance, and it's too long to be a sprint," Kroeger said. "It's one of those things you have to train for, you have to get a feel for. In a sense a lot of kids don't like swimming it because it's just hard. It's hard to find those kids who are really good at it."
In the 16 years the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association has held the state swimming championships, the Bayside Conference has had only four champions — all girls — win the 200-yard free, including three from Easton.
The Warriors added a fourth Feb. 24.
Maddie Weems showed why she was a heavy favorite in the event, as she outdistanced her closest competitor by over 4 seconds en route to winning the girls' 200 freestyle title during the Class 3A/2A/1A state championships at the University of Maryland's Eppley Recreation Center.
"Maddie always delivers the big swims when we she needs it," Kroeger said of his sophomore star who was the only Bayside swimmer to win a state title this year. "She's been very consistent.
"She's kind of branched out," Kroeger added. "Last year she was more of a freestyle sprinter for us, and this year she wanted to explore some of the other events. I mean she's good at all of the events, which is a good and bad thing for any swimmer really."
Weems was second in the 100 freestyle and third in the 50 free at last year's state meet.
She changed things up heading into this year's postseason, winning the 100 butterfly and 100 breaststroke at the conference championships in early February.
But when it came time for regionals and states, Weems opted for events she thought she could place in.
"I thought about doing the 100 fly and 100 breast, but then I really wanted to do freestyle," Weems said. "And I looked at where I would maybe place the best. I was like, I feel the best in the 200 free."
But.
"I've never liked the 200," Weems said smiling. "But I had been practicing it a lot, and I just felt the most comfortable in it. So I was like, I'll just try and give it my best."
Weems practiced a lot. She also swam a lot.
Because of poor weather conditions, the 3A/2A/1A East Regional championships were moved from Feb. 17 to Feb. 20 — four days before states. A member of the Talbot County YMCA team, Weems was also competing in the Maryland Club State Championships at St. Mary's College, which were sandwiched around the MPSSAA state meet.
Weems was admittedly tired and sore after swimming five events — including preliminaries — the Friday before the MPSSAA state meet. She didn't do well in the morning prelims of the 200 free, but rebounded that night, clocking a personal-record time of 1:54.17.
And though that effort potentially stoked Weems' confidence heading into Saturday's MPSSAA meet, it may have also added a bit more pressure to the favorite's shoulders.
"Everybody was telling me I was going to win," said Weems, who was seeded No. 1 by 6 seconds. "But I was like, 'I don't know.' I was nervous, but I felt confident. And even if it ended up being close I knew that I would be able to push through."
She did just that, reaching the first turn with a lead she never relinquished on the way to a first-place 1:54.53, giving Easton its third straight title in the 200 free. Kroeger's daughter, Molly, won the championship in 2022 (1:53.76) and last year, when she set a 3A/2A/1A record of 1:51.94. Weems' cousin, Tori Weems, won the event in 2017 (1:55.96).
The only other Bayside swimmer to win the 200 was Queen Anne's County's Kelsey Lessard (2:03.6) in 2010.
Weems was back in the pool for the 100 fly, and held the lead before getting passed over the final 25 yards, taking fourth in 1:00.58.
"My body just kind of gave out," Weems said.
Weems teamed with Katheryne Kelsey, Claire Morris and Isabella Westerfield to place sixth (1:59.42) 200 medley relay and fourth in the 400 freestyle relay (3:50.12), helping defending state champion Easton place sixth in the final girls standings — the highest finish by any Bayside team.
A senior, Westerfield posted fifth-place finishes in the 50 free (25.24) and 500 free (5:35.89).
Kent Island's girls finished seventh, led by freshmen Clare O'Keefe, who was second in the 50 free (24.82) and Kara Seymour, fourth in the 100 breaststroke (1:11.18), eighth in the 200 individual medley (2:24.88). Seymour and O'Keefe joined Marissa White and Maddie Parks to take fifth in the 200 free relay (1:45.29) and seventh in the 200 medley relay (1:59.86).
Queen Anne's sophomore Madalyn Clagett was fourth in the 100 free (55.50) and sixth in the 200 free (2:03.29). Kent County sophomore Mary Jane Joiner was ninth in the 200 free (2:06.74).
Kent County junior Henry Martinez delivered the top efforts of any Bayside swimmer on the boys side, finishing fourth in both the 50 free (22.32) and 100 free (49.71).
Easton again had the best finish of any Bayside boys team, placing 11th. Senior Brady Tipton was seventh in the 200 free (1:52.08), ninth in the 500 free (5:08.76), and teamed with Bryce Slaughter, Aiden Lavezzo and Alex Harding to take eighth in the 400 free relay (3:35.88) and ninth in the 200 free relay (1:37.31).
Kent Island's Jack Da Rosa, Reef Adams, Johnathan Mangold and Giovanni Aguirre were 10th in the 200 free relay (1:37.32). Mangold later joined Dylan McCormick, Jacob Reeder and Keefer Pullen to finish 10th in the 400 free relay.
Queen Anne's William Meyer, Quinlan Justice, Giles Stanton and Jacob Gardner were ninth in the 400 free relay (3:39.22).

title: Late push seals Vikings' title shot
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Late push seals Vikings' title shot

 March 12, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 691
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SILVER SPRING — Anthony Hughes and Koby Ennals know basketball can be a game of runs.The two juniors were part of the run that mattered most Tuesday night.
A one-time 17-point lead reduced to three, Hughes and Ennals helped fuel a decisive 8-0 fourth-quarter burst that returned momentum back to Cambridge-South Dorchester High's boys basketball team en route to the Vikings earning a 60-53 victory over Fort Hill in a Class 1A state semifinal at Montgomery Blair High School.
Top-seeded Cambridge-SD (24-1) will bid for its first state title since 1996 Friday, when it faces No. 2 seed Edmondson-Westside (22-2) for the Class 1A championship at the University of Maryland's Xfinity Center. Edmondson defeated third-seeded Smithsburg, 79-59, in Tuesday's other 1A semifinal.
"We just got a believe attitude," Cambridge-SD head coach Shawn Tucker said. "We told them, 'If we just slow it down we'll be fine. We just got to be patient.'"
The Vikings went on an 11-1 run to open the game, and packaged a 13-2 scoring spree during the second quarter, when they outscored the Sentinels, 23-8, to carry a 37-20 lead into halftime.
"We turned it over way too much in the first half," Fort Hill head coach Thad Burner said. "I thought that their energy was a lot better than ours, particularly in the second quarter when they extended that lead."
Senior point guard LaShaun Moody (team-high 18 points) had a three-point play and a drive that helped Cambridge-SD build its early 11-1 lead. But Fort Hill (19-4) got 3-pointers from DeShaun Brown (team-high 18 points) and Jabril Daniels (10 points) in the final 3:16 of the first quarter to pull within 14-12 heading into the second quarter.
The Vikings led 16-14 when they pieced together a 9-0 run midway through the second quarter. Ennals (13 points), who scored his 1,000th-career point in the first quarter, converted a Moody dish for a bucket off the glass. Semaj Pinder (nine points) hit a turnaround jumper then scored on a drive. Ennals scored on a put-back before Thomas Wilson canned a 3-pointer for a 27-14 Vikings lead.
Brown hit another trey to end a three-plus minute Fort Hill scoring drought. But Moody hit a 3-pointer, Ennals made two free throws, and Darren Belizare scored on a follow before Moody splashed another trey at the buzzer for a 37-20 Vikings lead.
"We preach getting off to a fast start," Tucker said. "We knew Fort Hill was a second-half team and it was going to be a battle. So to get out on a team like that early is huge."
The Sentinels went on an 11-2 run to start the third quarter, getting within 39-31 with 4:36 to go in the period. Hughes stopped that momentum briefly when he converted a steal into a layup, putting the Vikings back up by 10. A pair of Sterling Perkins free throws moved Cambridge-SD to a 44-33 lead heading into the fourth quarter.
Fort Hill came out bombing in the fourth. Landon Sensabaugh hit back-to-back three-balls and Brown turned a steal into a layup, cutting Cambridge-SD's lead to 45-41 with 6:30 left. Tucker called time and watched Hughes score another big bucket inside to make it a six-point lead.
Jabril Daniels answered with another 3, shaving Fort Hill's deficit to three at 47-44 with 5:38 remaining.
But Cambridge-SD showed it too could respond.
"We just had to come back and be ourself," Hughes said. "It's win or go home."
Hughes scored on a put-back. Ennals converted a pair of free throws. Moody scored on a follow before Ennals snatched a rebound and raced coast-to-coast for a bucket that pushed Cambridge-SD's lead to 55-44 with under 4 minutes to play.
"We made some pretty good runs in the third and the fourth, but (number) two (Ennals) and five (Moody), they were pretty good," Burner said.
The Sentinels wouldn't get any closer than nine the rest of the way, as Moody scored on a drive and made three of four free throws in the final 1:24 to cement the victory and Cambridge-SD's first state final appearance since 1996.
"They're a team that's not going to give up," Ennals said of Fort Hill. "But we're a team that's not going to give up either."

title: QA's-Carver playoff cut short by altercation
author: Bill Haufe
content:
QA's-Carver playoff cut short by altercation

 March 9, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 516
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Friday night's Class 2A boys basketball state quarterfinal playoff between Carver Vo-Tech and host Queen Anne's County High was stopped with 6:57 remaining in the third quarter when an altercation broke out between the two teams that left one Queen Anne's player injured.In a press release late Friday night, the Queen Anne's County Office of the Sheriff said, "it was actively investigating an assault that took place Friday on a Queen Anne's County High School basketball player at the game.
"We have obtained and are currently reviewing video surveillance footage as part of our ongoing efforts," the release stated. "No arrests have been made at this time as we continue to review evidence and fully investigate this incident."
Carver was winning 42-15 at halftime and extended that lead to 47-15, when Dorrian Sands hit a baseline jumper and a 3-pointer in the first minute.
Queen Anne's was approaching mid-court on its ensuing possession when a cross-court pass was intercepted by a Carver player, who drove quickly to the basket and was fouled from behind by Thompson. A Carver player confronted Thompson.
Video footage on Twitter showed players from both teams exchanging words near the Carver basket. Players and coaches from both benches came onto the court. The video then shows the altercation escalating when a Queen Anne's player is punched in the face. It is not clear from the video who struck the Queen Anne's player.
Members of the Queen Anne's County sheriff's department, Queen Anne's school administrators and staff, and both coaching staffs quickly separated players. The game's three officials conferred and decided to officially call the game.
"Our players, teams, community and school staff deserve a safe environment, we have zero tolerance for this type of behavior at our public events, and we can assure our community that this investigation will be thoroughly completed, and appropriate charges will be done at the conclusion," Queen Anne's Sheriff Gary Hofmann said in the press release.
Queen Anne's County athletic director Kwandrey Wilson and head basketball coach Jeff Hollis would not comment on the incident.
Carver advances to the semifinals where it will meet Middletown.
As of Saturday afternoon, it was not known if the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association would take any action on the incident or dole out any punishment.
Queen Anne's (18-4) took a 2-0 lead on a pair of Vince Gilberto free throws 1:23 into the game. The Bears (16-4) rattled off the next nine points before Collin Woolford hit a 3-pointer for the Lions midway through the first quarter.
Carver, which used a suffocating, in-your face pressure defense, stretched its lead to 16-5 when Sands (game-high 25 points) drained one of his five 3-pointers. Gilberto hit two free throws to get Queen Anne's within 16-7. But with 54.9 seconds left, Gilberto appeared to suffer an ankle injury while driving to the basket and was carried off the court. The senior guard did not return the rest of the game.
The Bears led 18-8 after one quarter, widened their lead to 32-14, then went on a 10-0 run to close the first half, taking a 42-15 lead into the locker room.

title: Regulski, Hesson deliver Colonel to North championship
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Regulski, Hesson deliver Colonel to North championship

 April 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 746
 Words 

 Read News Document

 AMERICAN CORNER — Jordan Regulski never let the door get open. Daniel Hesson made sure it stayed shut.Colonel Richardson High's dynamic pitching duo combined to throw a two-hitter Tuesday as the Colonels defeated St. Michaels, 3-1, to clinch the North Bayside baseball championship.
"When you walk into a situation like this, I'm a lot more blessed than a lot of people that take over programs," Colonel Richardson first-year head coach Garrett Nepert said after the Colonels improved to 15-1 overall, 7-0 North Bayside with their 11th straight victory. "I'm grateful. But this is all about the kids. I don't do too much. They do it all."
Even if Colonels loses Thursday at North Dorchester, it would still win the division title based on defeating St. Michaels (14-2, 7-1). Colonel defeated the Saints, 6-5, last week, but Tuesday's second meeting between the two teams is the one that counts toward the division standings.
"We didn't deserve to win," St. Michaels head coach Brian Femi said. "You can't give a good team like this all the opportunities that we gave them. And they played better defense and made smarter plays that we did. I told our guys their baseball IQ just wasn't there today. I told them that's not their fault. That's my fault because we've got to find away to teach it better."
Regulski and St. Michaels ace Jacob Seek were locked in a scoreless duel, when Colonel scratched across two runs in the bottom of the fourth.
Brayden Dadds worked a one-out walk. Derrick Mitchell was hit by a pitch. Both runners advanced on a wild pitch. Manny Wallace then popped out to St. Michaels first baseman Anthony Massaro in foul territory on the first-base side. With no one covering home, Dadds broke for home and dove across the plate in a cloud of dust for a 1-0 lead. Massaro got the ball to catcher Hunter Gottleib, whose tried to throw out Mitchell at third. But the throw to third was off the mark, bringing home Mitchell for a 2-0 lead.
"We did what we needed to do for sure," Nepert said. "We still got a way to go. We've got a week before we've got to play our best baseball."
St. Michaels pulled within 2-1 in the top of the fifth. Regulski issued a leadoff walk to Ethan Royer. The junior right-hander struck out Brock Grow before getting Connor Wheeler to bounce into a fielder's choice. Wheeler stole second, moved to third on a passed ball, then raced home on a passed ball. Regulski struck out Jacob Bealefeld to end the inning.
Colonel regained its two-run lead in the home fifth. Seek walked Jack Walls and Regulski to open the inning. Hesson then dropped a bunt up the first-base line. Massaro fielded the ball, looked to third, then threw late to first, loading the bases. Seek fanned Dadds, but Walls scored on a passed ball to make it 3-1. Seek walked Mitchell before retiring the next two batters to end the inning.
Regulski yielded a clean single to Pearson Greenwood (2 for 3) to leadoff the second. But that was the only hit St. Michaels mustered against the Colonel starter. Regulski allowed one run, walked four, hit Will Sherwood twice with pitches and struck out seven.
"He competes," Femi said of Regulski, who has verbally committed to Wake Forest University. "He battles you. He is crazy athletic; makes plays that pitchers might not make, but makes them look easy."
Hesson came on at the start of the sixth inning. The senior left-hander who is headed to Salisbury University after graduation, gave up a one-out single to Greenwood in the sixth and nothing else, striking out four of the seven batters he faced.
"They're both fantastic kids," Femi said of Hesson and Regulski, who have worked at Femi's baseball camps the past two summers. "Not only are they good baseball players but they're good people.
"He carries this team," Femi said of Hesson. "Mentally, he's a leader for them."
Nepert kept his praise for his two pitchers brief and to the point.
"Excellent," Nepert said. "That's about all I got. I thought they attacked the zone. They worked to their strengths."
Seek, who struck out seven and walked seven, gave up a leadoff single to Walls (2 for 3) to start the game. It was Colonel's only hit off Seek. Grow came on in relief with a man on in the sixth. he gave up a one-out single to Walls in the sixth and finished with two strikeouts and a walk.

title: Quade closes on milestones, SSPP tops NC
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Quade closes on milestones, SSPP tops NC

 April 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1017
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Morgan Quade is closing on two impressive milestones.And though Saints Peter and Paul High's senior star said she has not felt pressure from others, she admits she'd like to score her 200th career goal, notch her 400th career point and move forward.
"It will be a weight lifted off my shoulders," Quade said.
Quade almost slipped those weights off her shoulders in Monday afternoon's heat, scoring six goals and setting up another to help the Sabres' girls lacrosse team to its 11th straight win via a 12-5 victory over North Caroline.
"I'm trying to not focus on it and just let it happen naturally, but it's hard," said Quade, who is one goal shy of 200 and five points short of 400. "I've definitely been in my own head about it. It's not like other people pressuring or anything. It's hard to keep it up."
Monday's high temperatures — it was 89 before the opening draw — may have been one of the reasons why Quade did not start the game. The heat took a toll on a number of players, including Sabres sophomore Caroline Ewing, who scored three goals and set up another to help Sts. Peter & Paul (11-1) carry a 4-2 lead into halftime.
"I think today we definitely started off slow," said Quade of a game that was tied 2-2 after one quarter. "We haven't played in heat like this. I think that was part of it. But after halftime we really got on a roll there and we were moving the ball fast. Once we move the ball and find people open it's just a matter of time."
Sabres head coach Alison Beyer agreed the afternoon heat was a contributing element in her team not getting off to its usual fast start.
"The heat was a huge factor," Beyer said. "We haven't played in this heat and once we got accustomed to the heat we had to regroup, reset and we came back out and played like we play."
Ewing (three goals, two assists) scored on a free-position chance 43 seconds into the second quarter, then set up Quade's first goal a little less than 2 minutes later to give Sts. Peter & Paul its two-goal halftime edge.
Both Sts. Peter & Paul goalie Kylie Kroniser and North Caroline's Ashley Lawry made a slew of big saves throughout the first half to keep the game close.
But the Sabres started finding openings in the Bulldogs defense in the third quarter, turning a two-goal lead into a five-goal cushion heading into the fourth.
"I feel like we play our game," Beyer said. "And I think our game is like trivial. It's like, 'Let's see what we can do. Let's try this. That's not working. OK, let's try this.'
"It's not that we can't do anything because we know we can," Beyer continued. "It's like, 'Let's test them. We haven't seen this team before. Let's see what they can do, and see what we can do in reference to what they're doing'. And that's what we did."
Quade set up Eden Zimmerman's first goal 49 seconds into the third quarter. Eden Zimmerman scored her second goal with 8:37 left in the third for a 6-2 lead. Quade then gained possession behind the net, swept left, hit the brakes and wheeled in from the right side for a goal a little over a minute later.
Ashley Kercheval ended North Caroline's 25-minute, 36-second scoring drought with 1:21 left in the period to make it 7-3. But Quade responded with her third goal with 3 seconds left in the quarter.
"I expected a different outcome," North Caroline head coach Mandie Shockley said after the Bulldogs slipped 7-4. "I think we are 100 percent capable of winning that game. I think the areas that we continue to struggle in are the areas that cause the losses. But a tight game, or a two-goal game after an entire half tells me we are capable of winning these games. And it's just a matter of time before it clicks for them. I think a lot of it is mental. It's not like we don't have the talent."
Shockley was encouraged her team held Sts. Peter & Paul to its lowest goal output since its 16-9 season-opening loss to St. Mary's. But North Caroline couldn't trim its deficit any further in the fourth. Emery Zimmerman weaved through traffic down the middle of the field for a goal and a 9-3 lead with 9:11 remaining. Quade slung a sidearm shot in on a free-position opportunity with a little under 7 minutes to play, moving the Sabres to a 10-3 lead.
Riley Walstrum's goal with 4:14 left reduced the Bulldogs' deficit to six. But Ewing connected with Quade for a score just 18 seconds later. Quade added her sixth goal with 3:12 to go before Reece Bisesi scored the game's final goal with 50 seconds remaining.
"I was concerned," Beyer said. "After the first quarter I said, 'Let's play with some consistency. Let's play our solid game.' After that first quarter I think we settled in and came back out and played our game."
BASEBALL
NORTH DORCHESTER 20, CAMBRIDGE-SD 0
CAMBRIDGE — TJ Leonard tripled twice, driving in two runs and scoring two, and freshman Gage Kral tossed three innings of no-hit ball Monday, as the Eagles rolled in four innings.
Kral struck out six of the 10 batters he faced. Sophomore Manny Reyes had two hits and scored three runs for North Dorchester (7-7), Vernon Price (2 for 2) scored three runs, and Nate Fraccaroli (two RBIs) and Nate Swann (RBI) each had two hits and two runs.
SOFTBALL
QUEEN ANNE'S 9, KENT ISLAND 6
STEVENSVILLE — Autumn Huber doubled in a run and Abbie Denes drove in another, both in the eighth inning Monday, as the Lions rallied from a four-run deficit Monday to defeat the Buccaneers.
Huber was 3 for 4 to lead Queen Anne's 13-hit attack, and Camaryn Jacobi and Denes each had multi-hit games.
Hannah Martin earned the win in relief. Queen Anne's tied the game in the top of the fourth, when Keira Corcoran stole home, Jacobi singled, and Caroline Taylor doubled.
Lizzie McConnell tripled for Kent Island and Haven Applefeld singled.

title: Franklin gets call from Ravens
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Franklin gets call from Ravens

 April 29, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 768
 Words 

 Read News Document

 For three days, Ja'Mion Franklin waited for his name to be called during the NFL draft.It never was.
But Franklin kept coming back to something his Aunt Ty Bolden, told him during a pre-draft party.
"She was like, 'It doesn't matter when the phone rings, as long as it rings,'" Franklin said. "Low and behold, I got a ring. Literally as soon as the draft ended I got a call."
That call Saturday was from Franklin's agent, John Apple, who told the 2018 North Caroline High graduate, the Baltimore Ravens were going to give him a chance as an undrafted free agent.
"I was shocked," Franklin said of his selection during a phone interview Monday afternoon. "It's crazy. You can't write a better story. To go through all I've been through, and then to finally get an opportunity to not only chase my dream as being an NFL player, but to do it at home, for the home team that I always rooted for. I was ecstatic. He (Apple) said, 'I know this has been a stressful day but we're going to send you to Baltimore.' And I was like, 'I'm ready. Let's do it.'"
A 6-foot-1, 313-pound defensive tackle/nose guard who graduated from Duke University last May, the 24-year-old Franklin reports to the Ravens' training facility in Owings Mills this Thursday to begin a four-day mini-camp. He will be given a physical, sign his contract, and begin meetings and learning the playbook.
"I'm excited," said Franklin, a Ridgely native. "I'm obviously anxious but this entire process has been stressful, and not really a lot of football. But now I get to do what I love to do."
Franklin played three years at Notre Dame before transferring to Duke in December 2020. He made 16 tackles his first season in Durham, and improved those numbers the following year, logging 26 tackles, including three sacks. He was a captain this past season, totaling 31 tackles and a sack for the Blue Devils, who capped an 8-5 season with a 17-10 victory over Troy in the Birmingham Bowl.
It was over the past two seasons Franklin began adding fuel to his hopes of someday playing in the NFL.
"I always had the aspirations of playing in the league," Franklin said. "But the last two years at Duke really showed me I could do it. It was attainable. Starting every game the last two seasons and producing the way that I did, and being around the people I was around. I just took it and ran with it, and here we are."
Two people who further stoked that dream were Franklin's strength coach, David Feeley, and former Duke defensive tackle coach Jess Simpson, who coached previously in the NFL, and is now an assistant at Georgia Tech.
"Those are the two guys that told me really this is possible," Franklin said of Feeley and Simpson, "to keep doing the things that I was doing, and everything will take care of itself. And that's what I was doing.
"He was like, 'I've coached guys just like you in the league so I think you should pursue it,'" Franklin said of Simpson. "I just started thinking about it a lot more serious. Being a captain this past season got me a lot more attention. And being a leader and being up for the national awards for community service. Just getting my name out there in positive ways as much as I can."
Franklin, who has been training at Grosetti Performance in New Castle, Pennsylvania outside Pittsburgh prior to the draft, did not attend this year's NFL combine, but thought he impressed during Duke's Pro Day on March 28.
"I knew I was going to get an opportunity," said Franklin, who spoke with scouts from Baltimore, Houston, Miami, Minnesota, Denver and Chicago. "There's been too much invested, and I absolutely killed my pro day. I walked away confident. And I walked away knowing somebody was going to give me an opportunity to do what I do."
Franklin thought he might hear his named called during Saturday's fifth or sixth round, but it didn't happen.
"There was definitely the possibility," Franklin said of being drafted. "I think it just shook out different because the way the draft started. A lot of the guys that were ranked ahead of me went a lot later than they were supposed to.
"I knew that there was a chance, but it was definitely nerve wracking, man," Franklin added. "It's a stressful situation. Putting in all the work and controlling all you can control is all you can do. But it's all good. And you know the Baltimore Ravens took a chance on a hometown kid."

title: Lions move closer to first North Bayside title in program history
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions move closer to first North Bayside title in program history

 April 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 CENTREVILLE — The walls of Queen Anne's County High's gymnasium are plastered with banners celebrating past champions in just about every sport.But with the exception of the banner commemorating head coach Dee Fisher's 200th career victory last year, girls tennis is not represented on the gym walls.
"Girls tennis doesn't have anything," said Lucy Taylor, Queen Anne's No. 1 singles player. "Sometimes those posters are kind of behind (in being updated). And we joke that it's like a forgotten sport. But we're out here showing we can win stuff too."
The Lions have shown they can win quite often this year.
It started in the season-opener, when Queen Anne's ended Kent Island's impressive 102-match win streak against Bayside Conference competition. The Lions defeated the six-time defending Bayside champions again Friday by a 7-0 count, this one moving them within a victory of their first North Bayside title in school history.
"At the beginning of the season we had like an inter-squad scrimmage and that was like the best thing ever," Fisher said after his team improved to 11-1 overall, 9-0 North. "Because when I matched them up they were just pushing each other."
What has also helped is having players who have won conference or division titles in other sports this school year.
"I have volleyball players who had a great (Bayside title) team," Fisher said. "Basketball players who had a great (North Bayside title) team. Field hockey players that had a great (Bayside championship) team. Soccer (which won the North Bayside). So I have a team of winners basically. They win at every sport they play. So it kind of trickled over to tennis."
But Fisher admitted he did not see this coming after graduating nine seniors last year, most of which made up his starting lineup.
"We had a full team of juniors and sophomores," Fisher said. "So this was going to be my get-them-used-to-playing year. Next year would be the year.
"A lot of the players hadn't played doubles and singles," Fisher said of his team. "So this was a chance to get their feet wet. But our program has a lot of girls, so I always try to build that up through exhibition. I'm always encouraging exhibition matches, lot of practice, and just having fun."
In the process, Fisher's get-them-used-to-playing year has turned into the get-them-used-to-winning year."
Queen Anne's got an early start on that Friday, sweeping doubles play for a 3-0 lead. Lucy Taylor and sister Meg Taylor, who have lost only once this season, defeated Jamie Tranquill and Isabelle Gamez, 8-2 at No. 1. The No. 2 tandem of Hayden Legg and Marylee Kline put together a similar 8-2 result over Gianna Tamburo and Taylor Harding. Sydney Pinder and Kara Ringold completed the sweep with an 8-4 win over Grace Turner and Jasleen Paquer.
"Last year we lost, what, nine seniors?" Lucy Taylor asked. "Most of which were in the lineup. This year, Hayden and Marylee have both come so far, and they have been able to pick up big wins for us. The same with Sydney and Kara. I think it's just like, keep building on those skills we learned freshman year. It's just amazing how much everyone has grown."
Queen Anne's lead continued to grow through singles play.
Meg Taylor defeated Gamez, 8-4, at No. 2. Legg was an 8-4 winner over Tamburo, and Kline earned an 8-2 win over Harding.
In the marathon match of the afternoon, Lucy Taylor, who lost both her singles matches earlier in the week, fell behind 3-0 to Tranquill. This wasn't exactly anything new for the Lions' No. 1, who rallied from a 4-0 deficit to win when her and Tranquill met in the season-opener.
"I was just thinking, 'I've done this before. I can get it back,'" Lucy Taylor said. "I used the same mentality I did last time which is just like, one point at a time, one game at a time. And then I was able to build off of that."
Taylor rallied to take an 8-7 lead, but Tranquill showed she too could battle back, pulling even at 8-8 to force a tiebreaker.
"This time was a little harder because we went back and forth so many times," said Taylor, who won the tiebreaker 9-7. "This one really felt good."
A win over visiting Easton on Tuesday or against Cambridge-South Dorchester on Wednesday clinches the division title for Queen Anne's.
Do the Lions feel any pressure one victory shy of history?
"I think they don't think about it," Fisher said smiling. "I think they just go out and just play hard and have fun. No. We really don't talk about it.
"This is our throw-away year," Fisher said, referring back to this being a season of preparation for next year. "I don't know how to explain it. We just go with the flow."
Primarily an exhibition player, junior captain Sydnee Carr said it's been a joy to be on the ride toward a potential first division title.
"It's hard for me to speak on it because I'm typically an exhibition player," said Carr, who has won all her doubles matches when Fisher has inserted into the starting lineup. "But it has been fun to watch everybody improve. Definitely Hayden and Lucy and Marylee. Just seeing them come out the past two years and improve in so many ways, and then be able to be in the starting lineup and excel is really fun to watch.
"Being on the field hockey team and being on the swim team, our teams have a lot of banners," Carr continued. "So it will be fun to see my third sport be represented up on the wall."
GIRLS LACROSSE
SSPP 21, SALISBURY SCHOOL 3
SALISBURY — Sophomore Caroline Ewing scored five goals and set up another, and senior Morgan Quade distributed nine assists and scored twice Friday, as Saints Peter and Paul won its 10th straight.
Eden Zimmerman had four goals and Kendall Kroniser (assist), Avery McCall (two assists) and Eryn Callahan (assist) each recorded hat tricks for the Sabres (10-1, 6-0 Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference). Kate Sweeney (goal) and Emery Zimmerman had two assists apiece.

CAMBRIDGE — Calleigh Tribbett and Ashlynn Bisesi (assist) each notched hat tricks Friday to pace the Bulldogs to their second straight victory.

title: RIGHT IN THE MIX
author: Bill Haufe
content:
RIGHT IN THE MIX

 April 25, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 925
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — The North Bayside softball championship.Defending division and Class 1A state champion North Dorchester was certainly cast among the favorites at the beginning of this season. Queen Anne's County and Colonel Richardson also figured to be right at the top.
Easton?
After a 1-3 start, some may have brushed the Warriors to the side, thinking this was a season of rebuilding, or at least readjusting under first-year head coach Ryan Brice. Well, Brice's bunch showed again Thursday afternoon they have adjusted just fine, notching their seventh win in eight games via a 10-0 five-inning shutout of Cambridge-South Dorchester.
Easton (8-4 overall) improved to 5-1 in the North, tied with Queen Anne's (13-1, 5-1) and North Dorchester (12-2, 5-1) — though the Eagles hold the tiebreaker over the Warriors, having won the only meeting between the two teams. Queen Anne's plays Easton on Tuesday.
"We're on a roll," Brice said. "Hopefully we can keep this going until next week because we have three straight (Queen Anne's, James M. Bennett, North Caroline), Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday."
Brice is also hoping Sammy Townsend can keep it going. With Lyle Roe not pitching this week due to an injury, Townsend (7-2) started all three games in the circle for the Warriors. The sophomore punctuated her week by throwing Easton's first shutout of the season, a three-hit gem that including 11 strikeouts — eight swinging — and no walks.
"Sammy did an amazing job, not only today, but the past three games that we had," Brice said. "Three-and-oh. She pitched amazing today with a shutout. I can't say enough about her. She's one of the best pitchers I've ever had the pleasure of coaching."
Townsend gave up a game-opening single to Enazajah Young, who raced to second when the ball bounced and hit center fielder Leigha Bosley in the throat. Townsend promptly struck out the next three, leaving Young, who stole third, stranded at third.
Camryn Russum singled sharply to left field with one out in the second, but was thrown out stealing by Warrior catcher Laillah Janes. Townsend fanned Evelyn Windsor to end the inning.
"I felt like my spins were really tight today, and the past couple of games," Townsend said. "I felt like this week I've pitched the best that I've pitched all season."
Townsend set the Vikings (6-7, 1-5) down in order in the third before Laila Insley reached with a bunt single down the third-base line to open the fourth. Townsend got Emma Robinson to pop out to short, watched Lainey Jones move Insley to second with a sacrifice bunt before striking out M'Kya Molock to end the frame.
The right-hander fanned the first two batters she faced in the fifth before Keyth Rodriguez smacked a comebacker off Townsend's glove. But Townsend finished the mercy-shortened game with her fourth inning-ending strikeout of the game.
"I knew my defense had me," Townsend said. "I feel like we have a set infield and outfield now, because I know in the beginning of the year we were all wishy-washy with who we were going to put where."
The Warriors took a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first, when Mayah Wilkins (2 for 3) reached on an infield hit, dashed to third on a two-base throwing error on the play, and scored on a wild pitch.
Back-to-back, bases-loaded walks with two outs in the second extended that lead to 3-0.
Easton widened its advantage to 5-0 in the third. Townsend (2 for 3, two RBIs) roped a leadoff double into the left-field corner and scored on an error. title: Seek, Saints outduel Palmer, Lions
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Seek, Saints outduel Palmer, Lions

 April 23, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1419
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — Like many a game that shapes a division race, it was close.Each team turned an inning-ending double play.
Each team had a batter hit by a pitch and another intentionally walk.
Each team got outstanding performances from their big-name pitchers.
And each team finished with five hits.
But it was St. Michaels High's baseball team that produced the decisive — and what proved to be the last — hit. That hit came with two outs and the bases loaded in the bottom of the fifth inning Monday, when Jack Brennen chopped a slow bouncer down the third-base line for an infield hit that scored Pearson Greenwood with the winning run in a 3-2 Saints victory at Harold Baines Field.
St. Michaels (12-0 overall, 5-0 North Bayside) entered Tuesday tied atop the division with Colonel Richardson (12-1, 5-0) while Queen Anne's slipped to 9-3, 2-2.
"It was a very good high school baseball game," St. Michaels head coach Brian Femi said. "Both teams played well. It was an outstanding pitching duel. Both teams got timely hits. Both played good defense."
And both had scored two runs apiece heading into the bottom of the fifth.
That's when Will Sherwood lined a one-out single to center field. Queen Anne's right-hander Noah Palmer (3-1) walked Greenwood. Both runners advanced on a wild pitch before Palmer issued an intentional pass to Jacob Bealefeld, loading the bases. Henry Mullikin grounded to third baseman Jacob Clough, who threw home to force Sherwood at the plate for the second out.
Brennen then beat a grounder down the third-base line. Clough got to the ball, but didn't have time to make a throw to first as Greenwood raced home with the go-ahead run. Femi and Queen Anne's head coach Chris Fitzgerald agreed Brennen's bouncer was an infield hit — the last hit for either team the rest of the game.
"Heavyweight game for sure," Fitzgerald said. "They got the hit they needed and came away with the W."
Both pitchers were impressive, with St. Michaels senior left-hander Jacob Seek (4-0) striking out a season-high 13 in a complete-game victory. Seek allowed one earned run and walked two.
"This is what he's done all year," Femi said of Seek. "He just goes out and makes big pitches in big situations. The bigger the situation the bigger the pitcher. And he's a leader."
Queen Anne's Dalton Brown led off the game with a single, but Seek struck out the next three batters.
Down 2-0, the Lions had a rally working in the second, when Clough walked on four pitches and Colin Siwald singled to left. Seek fanned Bobby McCarthy, but Palmer reached with a bunt single up the third-base line, loading the bases. Gavin Leith grounded into a fielder's choice that plated Clough to make it 2-1. Seek ended the inning when Brown skied out to center.
"At moments it was little tight, but I think we did a good job of pulling out of it and being efficient," Seek said. "My curveball was on point today I felt like. I felt like I had a little mechanical issue that I had to (work the) kink out early. And I think when I figured that out in that second inning it kind of picked up for me and I was able to be more efficient with my pitches and hit my locations."
The Lions though pulled even in the top of the third. With one out, Seek struck out Dulin Clark. But the ball kicked away from Mullikin behind the plate. By the time St. Michaels' catcher located and retrieved the ball over by the St. Michaels dugout, Clark was on second. Evan Dickey then laced a 1-2 offering up the middle to score Clark with the tying run.
The closest Queen Anne's came to breaking the 2-2 tie was in the fourth. Leith reached on an infield hit and moved to second on a passed ball. After Brown was intentionally walk, Seek fanned Noah Cramer to end the inning.
Seek retired nine of the final 10 batters he faced. McCarthy reached with one out in the sixth when he was hit by a pitch before Palmer bounced to Bealefeld at third to a 5-4-3 inning-ending double play.
"That turned the game around I thought," Femi said. "Jake's played well for us all year. And that just swung the momentum our way."
Palmer delivered yet another quality performance for the Lions, striking out eight and walking four in 5 1/3 innings.
"I thought he was fantastic," Femi said of Palmer. "He beat us last year. We haven't hit him in two years. He competes. He changes speeds. He throws multiple pitches. I think he's one of the better pitchers in the Bayside."
But the Saints pushed two runs across in the home half of the first. Connor Wheeler was hit by a pitch and stole second base. Sherwood reached on an error, advancing Wheeler to third. Palmer looked like he might escape any damage when he struck out Greenwood and Bealefeld. But Mullikin drove a 1-1 pitch up the middle to score Wheeler and Sherwood for a 2-0 lead. Brennen followed with a single before Palmer fanned Bobby Fink to end the frame.
"After that first inning, it was rough," Palmer said. "But I came back and I feel like I was dialed in."
Blending his fastball and curve, Palmer wouldn't face more than four batters over the next three innings. Wheeler hit a two-out single in the second, stole second base and moved to third on a passed ball before Palmer got Sherwood to bounce out to third. The right-hander walked Bealefeld with one out in the third. Mullikin flew out to center fielder Brown, who fired a strike to first to double off Bealefield for the inning-ending double play.
Brock Grow got on via a two-out walk in the fourth and advanced to second on a passed ball. But Palmer got a called third strike on Ethan Royer to strand Grow. St. Michaels stranded seven baserunners, six in scoring position.
"He hasn't had a bad game," Fitzgerald said of Palmer. "We've put him up against all the big teams we got to go up against and we're proud the way he's handled himself all year. This wasn't surprising. Every game he's always performed like he did today. Just a stud for us. Proved it again today. Wish we could have gotten a couple more hits for him here and there and the game might have turned out different. But he did everything we asked of him today."
Palmer struck out Grow to open the sixth before reaching his pitch limit and being relieved by Brown, who struck out both batters he faced.
Queen Anne's stranded six, two in scoring position.
NORTH DORCHESTER 14 CAMBRIDGE-SD 4
SHILOH — Manny Reyes hit an RBI triple and Blake Bramble smacked a game-ending two-run triple in the sixth to lead the Eagles (6-5).
John Boyle earned the win, giving up three hits and striking out six in three innings. Brock Warrell threw three innings of relief.
Wes Windsor was 2 for 2 with four RBIs and Boyle singled and knocked in three runs.
SOFTBALL
COLONEL 7 NORTH CAROLINE 0
AMERICAN CORNER — Makayla Newcomb allowed six hits in a complete-game effort, striking out eight and walking none, as Colonel Richardson blanked its county rival.
Montana Davis had two hits and two RBIs for the Colonels (9-4) and Kylie Rhinehardt had two hits and one RBI. Sadie Prettyman added two hits, and Eileen Johnson (two RBIs), Kendall Sann (RBI) and Clarissa Peugh (RBI) had one hit apiece.
QUEEN ANNE'S 11 ST. MICHAELS 0
ST. MICHAELS — Hannah Martin tossed a two-hitter, striking out three and walking two over five innings, to lead the Lions.
Abbie Denes and Caroline Taylor had three hits for Queen Anne's County, and Autumn Huber and Hannah Martin each collected multiple hits.
EASTON 18 KENT ISLAND 9
STEVENSVILLE — Mayah Wilkins went 5 for 6 and drove in three runs and winning pitcher Sammy Townsend also had five hits as part of the Warriors' 22-hit attack Monday.
Townsend struck out five and walked three. Isabelle Ludwig drove in three runs for Easton and Olivia Orrell and Lyla Roe had multiple-hit games.
Avery Eaton had three RBIs for Kent Island. Hayven Applefeld, Bri Kurtz and Lizzie McConnell each had three hits for the Buccaneers.
GIRLS LACROSSE
EASTON 16 KENT ISLAND 9
EASTON — Emily Currie scored six goals Monday, and Miranda Stup and Dakota Lhotsky each had hat tricks as the Warriors posted their fifth win in six games.
Myka Motovidlak scored twice for Easton (5-2, 2-1), and Addie Knox and Anna Crist added one goal apiece. Zelia Proa finished with eight saves.

title: Lions closer to finish line
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions closer to finish line

 April 23, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 590
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — One word has been on the collective minds of Queen Anne's County High's softball team all season. Finish."Our motto has been finish all year long," Lions head coach Aaron Stewart said. "We didn't finish last year. Coming into the season this year, one of my coaches just came up to me and said, 'You know the word of the year has to be finish.' And we're finishing right now."
Queen Anne's took a big step in putting itself in a position to finish atop the North Bayside Tuesday afternoon, using a nine-hit attack to back the pitching of Emily Hirschbock in a 6-1 victory over defending division champion North Dorchester.
The Lions (12-1 overall) moved into first place in the North at 4-1 and now hold the tiebreaker over the Eagles (11-2, 4-1) after beating them in their only head-to-head meeting of the season. Colonel Richardson (10-4, 4-2), which defeated Kent County by forfeit Tuesday, North Dorchester and Easton (6-4, 4-1) remain in contention but need help to overtake the Lions.
"The bats definitely came back today," said Stewart, who was puzzled after his team was limited to just five hits in last Tuesday's 4-1 loss to Colonel Richardson. "We hit the ball well. Opposite field, which is even better. I like to see opposite-field hitting. We practice that over and over and over again, to take that outside pitch and drive it to right field. And we executed it today."
The Lions did just that in the third inning, breaking a scoreless tie with three consecutive two-out, opposite-field hits for a 3-0 lead.
Morgan Gottleib worked a one-out walk against North Dorchester ace Emilee Cohee (5-2) and was advanced to second on Emily Hirschbock's sacrifice bunt. Cam Jacobi lined a single into right field to score Gottleib. Caroline Taylor (3 for 4) drilled a 1-0 offering into the right field corner for a double. Autumn Huber then drove another Cohee delivery the other way for a two-run triple.
North Dorchester scratched a run across in the top of the fourth. Maggie Hubbard (2 for 3) hit a leadoff single and scored four batters later, when freshman Journey Pearson lined a shot to center that Jacobi just missed making a spectacular leaping catch on for the third out of the inning.
That would be the lone run allowed by Hirschbock (7-0) who finished with a complete-game five-hitter, striking out four and walking four.
"I was just kind of thinking to attack every pitch," said Hirschbock, who retired nine of the last 11 batters she faced. "It's been a big thing for me to attack specifically the first batter. I feel like I did that pretty well tonight. I'm proud of myself for that.
"It's always nice pitching with the lead," Hirschbock said with a big smile. "My hitters hit and it was awesome."
Queen Anne's extended its lead in the fifth. Jacobi reached on a one-out error. Taylor dropped a bunt that Cohee fielded, but had to hold onto with no one covering first. Huber walked to load the bases. Abbie Denes singled to left field to plate Jacobi for a 4-1 lead. Cohee notched her seventh and final strikeout before Emily Rendulic singled to score Taylor and Huber for a 6-1 cushion.
"Tough day," North Dorchester head coach Carol Hubbard said. "They out-hit us. We had a few unfortunate things on the base paths. Not making excuses. They made the plays they had to make."
Maddie Nagel relieved Cohee, got an inning-ending strikeout, then held the Lions scoreless in the sixth despite yielding singles to Jacobi and Taylor.

title: La Plata man selected as judge for Westminster dog show
author: Matt Wynn mwynn@somdnews.com
content:
La Plata man selected as judge for Westminster dog show

 April 23, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Matt Wynn mwynn@somdnews.com | Section: State News 
 
 484
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The Westminster Kennel Club has selected a La Plata man as a judge for the 148th annual Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show."I've always had dogs. They developed into a huge part of my life and became a major hobby for me," Richard Todd Jackson, 54, told Southern Maryland News. "Everything kind of exploded while I was in college."
Jackson, like many freshmen, said he hated living in dorms and moved off-campus. His parents told him he would have to pay half the rent, so he found a job as a kennel assistant.
His work at the Tsang-Po Kennels kindled his lifelong passion for chow chows, leading him to achieve over 50 championships and grand championships.
"I've had chow chows ever since," Jackson said. "I left to go off to college with no dogs, and I came home with six dogs."
As he was from Miami, he had to make special accommodations so his chow chows, which are an arctic dog, would be comfortable in the climate. He formed a makeshift kennel on his air-conditioned patio to keep his dogs cool in the long, hot Florida summers.
"I started judging my own breed, which is chow chows, and I've had quite a bit of success. I still show my dogs," Jackson said. "I don't get a chance to do it as much as I would like to because of avoiding conflicts of interest as a judge."
Jackson said his claim to fame came from his smooth-coated chow chows, which have a rougher, shorter, more bristly coat.
The Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show invited Jackson nearly a year and a half ago to serve on the panel, but he was sworn to secrecy until they made their announcement.
He is among 43 other judges for this year's show, being selected out of what he estimates to be at least 2,000 others.
He is listed on the Westminster Kennel Club's website as a toy breed judge for this year, examining affenpinschers, Biewer terriers and papillons.
"It's an honor to be invited to judge at what is one of the most revered dog shows in the world. The Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show is second only to the Kentucky Derby as one of the oldest sporting events in the United States," Jackson said, reflecting on his appointment. "Being chosen to judge is a dream to which most dog show judges aspire. To do so as one of the few people of color ever to attain this role adds a profound sense of responsibility, pride, and history."
The show will return for the second year to the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing Meadows–Corona Park, N.Y., on May 11, 13 and 14.
Beyond his contributions to the dog sport, according to a release from the Westminster Kennel Club, Jackson has been involved in real estate development and asset management, focusing on providing affordable housing to seniors and military families in the Mid-Atlantic region for over 25 years.

title: Lions regain form with bounce-back win
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions regain form with bounce-back win

 April 20, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1468
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Yes, its opponent was different.But so was its execution on both ends of the field.
"I think we were more cohesive and we played a lot more calmly," Lions senior defender Faith Novak said. "Still intense. But more calm to the point where we could communicate, stay in our zones, and really just work more as a unit than individual defense."
That was apparent early Friday night, as Queen Anne's County High's girls lacrosse team — three days after losing to Stephen Decatur — held a red-hot North Caroline team to its lowest goal total of the season during a convincing 15-4 victory on senior night at Lions Stadium.
"It's Queen Anne's. They are a powerhouse," North Caroline head coach Mandie Shockley said after the two-time defending Bayside Conference champions had ended her team's five-game winning streak. "We knew what to expect. They just outplayed us."
It was the Lions who had their five-game win streak ended Tuesday night as Decatur earned a 10-7 victory over Queen Anne's. Head coach Kesley Fitzgerald's bunch certainly appeared to have shaken off that rare conference loss Friday, as they spotted the Bulldogs the game's first goal then proceeded to score the next 12.
"We take a lot of pride in our preparation and I feel at practice (Wednesday and Thursday) we were all working to fix our flaws," Novak said. "And I think that really showed how much we worked to fix what we needed to work on. Like our transition looked a lot better. We were more comfortable with it. We were more comfortable with taking pressure, and I feel that led us to the win."
The Bulldogs (5-2 overall, 1-1 North Bayside), who averaged 17.4 goals an outing during their five-game win streak, took a 1-0 lead 4:23 into the game, when Claire Blue scored on a free-position opportunity.
It would be almost another 32 minutes of play before North Caroline put another shot past Queen Anne's goalie Maddie George (five saves), as Reece Bisesi scored 30 seconds into the fourth quarter, ending the Lions' streak of 12 consecutive goals.
"The draw," Shockley said. "Every other game we've played we've dominated the draw and we just could not get it. I think we got five, maybe six. And Queen Anne's is a team, they don't drop the ball. They definitely dominated the draw (winning 13). It was hard for us to get it back. We had a few, but we just had a lot of trouble getting to the net. They played hard."
The Lions (6-2, 2-0) also played with a longtime trademark of Fitzgerald's teams — patience.
"More calm. More patience," Fitzgerald said. "There were a few times where we still looked for that first push on the shot or pass."
But those times were far outnumbered by Queen Anne's Baillie Pinder (four goals, four assists) and RJ Ensor (three goals, four assists) waiting and finding teammates either cutting toward the goal or finding a small opening in Caroline's defense.
"Off-ballers were working a lot better tonight seeing things," said Fitzgerald, whose team has now won six of seven. "More communication. More composure. I think a turning point was they realized, we take it in, get your cut, and if you don't like what you see, pull it back out and then find something else."
After being held to just one first-quarter goal — that coming with 3:20 left in the opening period when Riley Klepper (game-high five goals) converted a Pinder dish to tie the game at 1-1, Queen Anne's blew open the game, outscoring the Bulldogs 7-0 in the second quarter and 4-0 in the third.
"We went to practice and we knew we had work to do," Pinder said. "I think this time we had a lot more patience and trust in ourselves with the ball. And we just wanted to come out and prove ourselves after the last game. Especially in the second half on offense. I could feel us a lot more calm. And we knew what we were going to do. Ensor ignited the Lions' 8-0 second quarter when she set up the first of Pinder's four goals 31 seconds into the period. Less than 2 minutes later, Ensor juked defenders and beat North Caroline goalie Ashleigh Lawry (eight saves) for a 3-1 lead.
North Caroline called time. Queen Anne's intercepted a Bulldog clearing attempt, got the ball quickly to Pinder, who neatly tucked in her second goal for a 5-1 lead. Klepper converted a pair of passes from Pinder for goals and another off an Ensor feed for an 8-1 halftime lead.
Madi Brown scored on a free-position opportunity before Ensor sandwiched a pair of scores around another Pinder goal — the second off a Kaitlyn Horney pass.
North Caroline played even with the Lions in the fourth, as Bisesi scored twice and Riley Walstrum once. Pinder, Kaisa Hickson and Brown added goals for Queen Anne's.
"Obviously their goalie is a good goalie," Shockley said of Brown. "Maybe not our best day on that side, but it happens."

Emily Currie scored twice for Easton (4-2) and Myka Motovidlak added a goal. Warrior goalies Haiden Hulliger and Zelia Proa each made four saves.
SSPP 23, GUNSTON 5
CENTREVILLE — Sophomore Caroline Ewing had five goals and set up three others, and senior Morgan Quade notched a hat trick and doled out seven assists Thursday as the Sabres extended their Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference win streak to 24.
Freshman Emery Zimmerman finished with three goals and three assists for Sts. Peter & Paul (8-1, 4-0). Sophomores Eryn Callahan (three assists) and Avery McCall, and freshmen Kate Sweeney (assist) and Julia Spero scored two goals apiece. Eden Zimmerman (three assists), Ashley Handy, Samantha Murphy and Emma Hainey each scored one goal.
BASEBALL
ST. MICHAELS 13 POCOMOKE 0
ST. MICHAELS — Bobby Fink tossed four innings of one-hit ball, striking out six and walking none Thursday as the Saints improved to 11-0.
St. Michaels' Jacob Bealefeld doubled, drove in three runs and was hit by a pitch three times. Brock Grow (1 for 1) scored three runs and was hit twice, and Ethan Royer was 1 for 1 with two runs and two RBIs. Eli Wallace pitched an inning of one-hit relief, fanning one.
QUEEN ANNE'S 14 J.M. BENNETT 4
SALISBURY — Evan Dickey pitched a complete-game four-hitter, striking out seven, and Colin Siwald went 3 for 4 with three RBIs Thursday to pace the Lions.
Jacob Clough was 3 for 4 with two RBIs, Noah Cramer collected three hits, and Bobby McCarthy drove in four runs for Queen Anne's County (9-2).
SOFTBALL
QUEEN ANNE'S 11 J.M. BENNETT 0
SALISBURY — Senior Autumn Huber knocked in four runs with three doubles as the Lions rebounded from their first loss of the season with a shutout of the Clippers.
Emily Hirschbock yielded four hits and no runs over five innings to earn the win for Queen Anne's (10-1), striking out six and walking just two. Caroline Taylor, Camaryn Jacobi and Hannah Martin each had multiple hits for the Lions.
EASTON 16, WICOMICO 2
SALISBURY — Sammy Townsend swatted a pair of home runs and also singled, driving in five, as the Warriors improved to 5-4 on Thursday.
Townsend also earned the win for Easton, allowing six hits and two runs over six innings. She struck out 11 and walked none. Leilani Brooks, Olivia Orrell and Gemma Vogel each smacked run-producing doubles, and Kaylee Verley drilled a two-run double. Isabelle Ludwig (double), Vogel and Brynlee Buchkoski each had multiple-hit games for the Warriors.
COL. RICHARDSON 17 WASHINGTON 0
AMERICAN CORNER — Eileen Johnson and Kylie Rhinehardt each had two hits, and Makayla Newcomb tossed three innings of no-hit ball, fanning five to lead the Colonels (8-4).
Rhinehardt pitched two scoreless innings of relief, striking out six, to complete the no-hitter.
Clarissa Peugh doubled for Colonel and Alaina Hall (RBI) and Tyla Dickerson each had a hit.
ST. MICHAELS 12 POCOMOKE 2
ST. MICHAELS — Lilly Haddaway went 4 for 4 with four RBIs and two runs as the Saints defeated the Warriors, raising their record to 5-6.
Myla Ramey earned the win, giving up two earned runs and four hits over three innings. Ramey struck out four and walked two. Mercy Haddaway worked two innings of scoreless relief, allowing one hit, a walk and striking out two.
Madi White was 2 for 3 with a double and two RBIs, Mercy Haddaway (double) and Gabby Pickens each went 2 for 3, and Katie Jenkins was 2 for 4 with a triple and double.

title: Mardela blanks ND in clash of unbeatens
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Mardela blanks ND in clash of unbeatens

 April 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 691
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SHILOH — This was act one in a potential three-part series.If acts two and three do materialize, North Dorchester High head softball coach Carol Hubbard hopes they go a lot better than this one.
Mardela cranked out 14 hits and sophomore pitcher Hayden Adkins hurled a complete-game one-hitter for her sixth shutout of the season Thursday, as the Warriors rolled to a 10-0 victory over the Eagles in a battle of unbeatens.
"Definitely an off-day," Hubbard said after the Eagles committed an uncharacteristic six errors. "We knew going in we're both tough teams. We both have strong pitching. We both typically put the bat on the ball. Tonight they outplayed us. No other way to say it. We had errors in the field. We didn't put the bat on the ball nearly as well as we're capable of. It just wasn't our day."
Mardela (12-0) took a 2-0 lead in the first inning against Eagles ace Emilee Cohee (5-1). Lexie Guy led off by blooping a single into center field. Julia Wisk advanced her with a sacrifice bunt. Camryn Dorr reached on an error that pushed Guy to third. Ava Twilley hit a comebacker to the mound that Cohee fielded. Knowing she didn't have time to get Guy at the plate, Cohee wisely threw for first for the second out. Karsyn Shockley then smacked a 2-2 pitch to the right-field fence for a double, plating Dorr. Cohee got Elana Donalds to ground out to second, ending the inning.
Cohee retired the first two batters of the second inning. Samantha Witte then hit a towering pop-up that landed between second baseman Emily Boyle and right fielder Journey Pearson. Witte raced to second on the play, stole third and scored on Guy's single to left field for a 3-0 lead.
"Eight of our nine in the lineup are batting .390 or above," said Mardela head coach Kory Shiles, whose team defeated North Dorchester in last year's Bayside Conference championship — the last team to defeat the defending Class 1A state champion Eagles. "We have five" — Twilley, Wisk, Dorr, Donalds, Abby Campbell — "that are batting over .500. That to go with our phenomenal pitching ..."
Phenomenal indeed.
Coming into Thursday's game the Warriors had yielded just two runs in regular-season play — that to Colonel Richardson. Adkins (7-0) struck out eight and walked two. Then there's Twilley who has only given up one hit all season.
"Mardela played a great game," Hubbard said. "They made the plays when we put the ball in play. And Hayden pitched a great game."
North Dorchester got its only hit in the third, when Mackenzie Lewis beat out a spinning infield single up the third-base line. Cohee followed with a walk, but Adkins squelched the rally there, getting Kinsley Peters to ground out to short.
The closest the Eagles came to a second hit came in the fourth when Maggie Hubbard scorched a hard grounder went off first baseman Shockley that Shiles called an error. Adkins retired 11 of the final 12 batters she faced, surrendering a leadofff walk to Maddie Nagel in the seventh. Nagel, who was hit on the ankle with ball four, was lifted for a courtesy runner, who was thrown out trying to steal second.
Mardela extended its lead to 4-0 in the fourth. Guy and Wisk hit back-to-back two-out singles before Dorr singled to right, scoring Guy.
The Warriors put together another two-out rally in the fifth, but Cohee got a called third strike on Witte to end the inning.
"I thought Emilee pitched well," Hubbard said, whose starter gave up 11 hits, the last, an RBI double by Dorr that pushed Mardela's lead to 5-0 in the sixth and ended Cohee's day on the mound. "She gave up one walk. Not a bad performance. Can't ask a whole lot more out of your pitcher than that."
Twilley greeted reliever Jewels Vroman with an RBI single. The Warriors tacked on two more runs — both scoring on errors.
"I got a feeling we'll see them one more time, if not two more times," Shiles said of a potential rematch with the Eagles in the Bayside Conference championship and the Class 1A East Region I final.
