title: Calvert middle schooler gets chance to golf at Masters
author: Ted Black tblack@somdnews.com
content:
Calvert middle schooler gets chance to golf at Masters

 April 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Ted Black tblack@somdnews.com | Section: State News 
 
 527
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Golfers of all levels from across the country aspire to compete in the Masters Tournament each April in Augusta, Ga., and for one Calvert County middle school student the dream became a reality, at least to a certain extent.Chesapeake Beach resident Luke Gladfelter earned the unique opportunity to compete in a drive, chip and putt competition for male and female golfers ages 7 to 15 and divided by gender. The three-pronged event at the Masters tests the talents and levels of consistency of youngsters in the key aspects of the game.
The Windy Hill Middle School seventh grader finished seventh in the National Drive, Chip & Putt Competition at Augusta National Golf Club in Georgia on April 7. The Chesapeake Beach resident tied for second in the putting competition of the event, which was part of the Masters held last week, and placed seventh overall in his age group.
The competition conducted in conjunction with the USGA, the Masters Tournament and the PGA of America, included 80 golfers from 31 different U.S. states, Canada and Australia. It took place several days prior to the start of the 88th Masters Tournament at Augusta National in Georgia which ran from April 11-14.
"I've always dreamed of being able to play at Augusta," Gladfelter said. "Now I get the chance to live out my dream. When I started playing golf, I learned a lot from my dad [Mark Gladfelter] and then I started playing in the Calvert County league. I played other sports, too. But I stuck with golf."
Prior to competing in the opening leg of the drive, chip and putt event, Gladfelter honed his skills in the Junior Tour events in Southern Maryland that thrived in the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic. Established high school golfers Shelby Herbert (La Plata High) and Aspen Bikowski (North Point High) also competed in those events, which were initially not divided by gender.
Gladfelter's climb to the national finals at Augusta began on June 14 when he captured the first local leg of the event at the University of Maryland as an alternate after three others defected. Two months later at River Bend in Great Falls, Virginia, Gladfelter finished second with 142 points in an event in which the top two finishers in each age group advanced to the next round.
On Sep. 16, 2023, in the Mid-Atlantic Regional Tournament at Aronimink Golf Club just outside of Philadelphia, Gladfelter scored 156 points and took first place in one of 10 regional events nationwide in which only the winner in each group would advance to the national finals.
"Luke had a really good day driving and chipping that day, and he also got points for his putting," said Mark Gladfelter, an assistant principal at Northern High School where his two oldest sons, Jack Gladfelter and Sean Gladfelter, are current students. "I was following along the scores and Luke was way out in front after most of the kids had played. So when I was waiting on the last couple of scores to come in I knew he was in good shape."
The National Drive, Chip & Putt Tournament was telecast live on the Golf Channel on Sunday, April 7.

title: Colonels upend unbeaten Queen Anne's
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Colonels upend unbeaten Queen Anne's

 April 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 953
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Makayla Newcomb has pitched well this season.But Colonel Richardson High's softball team either couldn't deliver the big hit or make the big play defensively when it was needed.
Tuesday, the Colonels got both.
Aubrey Taylor ripped a two-run triple down the right-field line and Newcomb crafted a complete-game five-hitter, as the Colonels defeated Queen Anne's County, 4-1, dealing the Lions their first loss of the season.
"She's had a good year for us," Colonel Richardson head coach Brett Ireland said of Newcomb (7-4), who finished with 10 strikeouts and no walks. "All year we just couldn't make enough plays or one thing would go wrong and it sort of snowballed. But we got the clutch hit today. We've struggled with the runners in scoring position."
Colonel (7-4 overall, 2-2 North Bayside) took a 1-0 lead in the first inning, as Kylie Rhinehardt, Clarissa Peugh, Eileen Johnson and Tyla Dickerson each singled off Hannah Martin (6-1), with Dickerson's hit to center plating Rhinehardt.
Martin though prevented the big inning, retiring the next three batters to end the inning, then setting down the side in order in the second.
Martin issued her only walk of the game to Peugh to lead off the third. Johnson (2 for 3) singled to left. Peugh was forced at third when Dickerson bounced into a fielder's choice. Taylor (2 for 3) then laced a 1-0 offering down the right-field line, scoring Johnson and Dickerson. Taylor raced home on an overthrow to third.
"Mostly I was just looking for a hit to the right side because I knew it would score both the runs on first and second," Taylor said.
That's exactly what her coach was looking for as well.
"Aubrey stepped up today and gave us a big hit," Ireland said. "Runners on first and second, she hit a triple down the line. I was hoping someone would hit it down that far just because I could see the right fielder was in right-center a lot. That (right-field) line was open and once it got there both runs were able to score. And Aubrey made good hustle to third. And then there was an overthrow and (she) was able to get in there and score. That really gave us nice comfortable lead. I was wishing we could tack on more but we just couldn't do it."
Martin yielded only one more hit the rest of the way, retiring 13 of the final 15 batters she faced.
"I think Hannah pitched extremely well," Queen Anne's head coach Aaron Stewart said, whose pitcher allowed seven hits and struck out seven. "Four runs. Our average is eight, nine runs. We score eight, nine runs — we had that one bad inning — we win the game."
Newcomb held the Lions (9-1, 2-1) to their lowest run total of the season and retired the first nine batters she faced before Queen Anne's scored its lone run in the fourth.
"I had a little bit of pressure, but I just go on top of the hitters," Newcomb said. "Once I got three-up, three-down on the whole lineup the first time (I was good). My curveball was good. And just the fastball, spotting it."
Newcomb recorded five of her 10 strikeouts through the first three innings.
That streak ended in the fourth, when Cam Jacobi drove a leadoff double to the fence in left field. Caroline Taylor then hit a line drive that Peugh made a diving stop on at second base. Autumn Huber followed with another double to the left-field fence, scoring Jacobi to make it 4-1.
But Newcomb got Abbie Denes and Martin to fly out to end the inning.
"Makayla threw a great game today," Ireland said. "She hit her spots well. We know Queen Anne's has some good sticks and I thought she was able to throw her off-speed pitch for strikes and got a couple of big outs with that. I thought the second and third time through the lineup, the changeup was good enough to get us some outs. "
Queen Anne's threatened again in the fifth.
Emily Rendulic stroked a single just over the outstretched glove of Taylor at short. Newcomb got a called third strike on Morgan Gottleib. Emilie Smith then doubled into the left-field corner, moving Rendulic to third. But Newcomb stifled the rally there, notching a strikeout and before inducing an inning-ending pop-up.
"We couldn't hit the ball today," Stewart said. "That's what it pretty much came down to. We've hit the ball extremely, extremely well all year long and we just couldn't get the hit today. Looked like she (Newcomb) was throwing the good stuff and we couldn't hit the ball. We normally put up eight, nine runs every game and one run isn't going to win you games. But we move on."

Mackenzie Lewis and freshmen Kinsley Peters and Journey Pearson each had two hits for the Eagles (9-0, 3-0), who ended Easton's three-game win streak.

Bealefeld went 2 for 3 with a double and two runs scored, and Henry Mullikin (2 for 3) doubled and drove in two runs for St. Michaels (9-0, 4-0).

 ST. MICHAELS — The rough start to the season was one thing.Not making contact though may have troubled Ryan Brice even more. So Easton High's first-year head softball coach tried a different approach.
"I told them, 'We're not going to have any more double-digit strikeout games,'" Brice said. "I told them before each game we're going to line up in the on-deck circle and time the pitcher. I'm not sure, but I think today we only had one strikeout. So I'm going to keep on going with that approach."
That approach certainly worked Monday, as the Warriors churned out 17 hits, including four doubles, on the way to a 14-3 six-inning victory over St. Michaels that extended their win streak to three.
"It's very hard to beat a team like St. Michaels like this," Brice said of a Saints team that entered the game having won three of four, its lone loss coming to defending Class 1A state champion North Dorchester. "They are very well coached. They're very aggressive. They're a good team from top to bottom. So for us to come here and do what we did is huge."
Easton (4-3 overall, 3-0 North Bayside) pushed four runs across in the first inning. Mayah Wilkins (4 for 5) and Lyla Roe (3 for 5) reached on back-to-back singles. Olivia Orrell and Sammy Townsend followed with consecutive run-producing groundouts.
St. Michaels starting pitcher Angel Bock (2-3) looked like she might escape further damage when she worked the count to 1-2 on Laillah Janes. But Janes (2 for 5) singled to right and Gemma Vogel reached on an error before Brynlee Buchkoski (2 for 4) doubled down the left-field line to plate Janes and Vogel for a 4-0 lead.
Myla Ramey relieved Bock to start the second, but Easton stretched its lead to 6-0, scoring two runs on a throwing error.
"Just an off-day all around," St. Michaels head coach David Fisher said after his team slipped to 4-4, 1-2). "I really felt like we were focused and we were ready. We just didn't click. Couple mental errors. It wasn't even the Easton-St. Michaels hype. It was just lack of focus. And then all of a sudden pitching change and we got down early and just didn't pull ourself out."
Easton expanded its lead in the fourth, cranking out five runs on seven hits. Roe reached on an error and scored on Orrell's double down the left-field line to make it 7-0. After Townsend singled, Janes and Vogel delivered consecutive RBI singles for a 9-0 cushion. Roe was relieved by Townsend, who got Katie Jenkins to bounce into a fielder's choice. But Madi White (2 for 3) singled to center, scoring Ramey. Bock followed with a single to right that plated Jenkins before White scored on Lola Browning's sacrifice fly to left, drawing the Saints within 11-3. Townsend stopped the threat there, inducing Brooke Reilly into an inning-ending groundout.
"She pitched a great game," Brice said of Roe, who allowed two runs, three hits, three walks and struck out three over four innings. "I call her a dog for a reason. She's a tough one. Lyla Roe did an amazing job today."
The Warriors regained their 11-run edge in the sixth. Leigha Bosley lined a leadoff double to left. After a Wilkins single, Roe singled to right, scoring Bosley. Wilkins scored on a wild pitch before Townsend's groundout to short plated Roe for a 14-3 lead.

title: Easton gets in the zone, routs Rams
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Easton gets in the zone, routs Rams

 April 13, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 825
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SALISBURY — This is how last season started for Easton High's boys lacrosse team.The Warriors lost their season-opener to Salesianum of Delaware then proceeded to piece together a school-record 14-game winning streak that ended in the Class 2A state semifinals.
Easton head coach Dennis Keenan may have thought he was watching last season unfold all in one afternoon Friday, as the Warriors surrendered the game's first goal, started slow, then reeled off 12 consecutive goals en route to a convincing 14-2 win over Parkside for their third straight victory.
"We're starting slow so we got to work on that. It's my fault. I got to get them into a warmup or something. Or some kind of dance routine before the game," Keenan said with a smile. "Get 'em a boombox. Get Saturday Night Fever going or something just to get 'em going."
After Nate Pusey's goal staked the Rams (3-3) to a 1-0 lead with 1:41 elapsed, Easton (3-1) struggled against Parkside's zone defense. The Warriors finally broke through when Hudson Royer snapped a left-handed shot past Rams goalie Nicolas Pastusak with 3:50 remaining in the first quarter.
Easton's struggles continued, but its defense allowed Parkside little in offense, killing off two extra-man opportunities early in the second quarter. The Warriors nudged in front when Drew Schmidt got free in front of the goal and tucked a shot over Pastusak's shoulder for a 2-1 lead with 4:52 left before halftime. Ty Finlay then won the ensuing faceoff, sprinted downfield and scored 12 seconds later for a 3-1 lead Easton carried into the half.
"First time seeing the zone this year and the guys just had to work through it," Keenan said. "Once we saw the seams in the zone the guys were able to take advantage of it. They tried to dodge into the zone too much early. Once they were aware of it, they pulled it out and starting moving the ball more."
That was evident in the third quarter, as Easton, despite a brief, cold burst of rain and continuously strong gusting winds, began finding openings in Parkside's defense. Landon Chaney scored just 1:11 into the third quarter to make it 4-1. Only 37 seconds later, Tyler Rardin bulled through traffic and flicked the first of his game-high five goals into the net for a 5-1 lead.
"Defense played great all game," Rardin said. "Offense, we finally just started shooting the ball more and they started falling second half. I think it was just trying to figure out their zone on offense, trying to find open shots. I think we got a lot in the first half, but really started making them in the second."
Campbell Taliaferro set up Rardin's second strike with 4:21 left in the third. Less than a minute later, Blake Royer zipped a pass from behind the net to Charlie Kaminskas, who completed the nice give-and-score play for a 7-1 lead. Blake Royer capped the 5-0 third-quarter scoring spree with under 2 minutes remaining in the third, parking an overhand shot into the net for an 8-1 cushion.
"I think our offense is getting there," Warrior goalie Jack Kilbourne said. "They're starting to click."
The offense continued clicking and widening the lead in the fourth. Rardin sandwiched a pair of goals around a Schmidt score, and Taliaferro notched a goal, all within the first 5 minutes of the fourth for a 12-1 bulge.
Parkside ended a 39-minute, 25-second scoring drought with just under 7 minutes left in the game, when Tavian Dashiell slipped one past Kilbourne, who along with defensive mates Kyle Dyott, BT Todd and Edward Whelan held the Rams to their lowest scoring output of the season.
"I think we just kind of played as a whole unit," said Kilbourne, who finished with 11 saves. "And we really trusted our guys to push them in the right direction. I saw shots, I was able to make a save. They put me in a good position.
"I should have had it," Kilbourne said of Pusey's first-quarter goal. "But you can't have 'em all. I think we're moving in the right direction. And I think we're only going to get better from here."
Easton closed the scoring with goals from Jackson Wieland and Rardin in the final 6 minutes.

Stella Kabler, Dakota Lhotsky, Addie Knox and Emily Currie each recorded hat tricks for Easton, and Miranda Stup and Anna Crist added one goal apiece. Zelia Proa made five saves and Haiden Hulliger stopped eight shots.

title: Colonel strikes early, hangs on late
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Colonel strikes early, hangs on late

 April 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1096
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Perhaps one of the biggest reasons behind Daniel Hesson's success on the mound the past three seasons has been his practical approach."I felt like I had decent stuff," Colonel Richardson High's senior left-hander said. "Missed a couple locations. But you know, that's baseball. Sometimes you miss a spot, sometimes you put one where you want to put it. And other stuff happens. There's not much you can do about it."
Hesson tried to do as much as he could Thursday afternoon, limiting Easton to four runs over six-plus innings before the Warriors pieced together a late rally that fell short in an 11-8 loss to the Colonels.
"We got a saying: 'Winners find a way,'" Colonel first-year head coach Garrett Nepert said after his team's fourth straight win. "We found a way. It wasn't pretty, but winners find a way. So that's what we're kind of going with to make ourselves feel better today."
The Colonels (8-1 overall, 2-0 North Bayside) were feeling pretty good about themselves after sending 13 batters to the plate in a nine-run first inning that featured eight walks, Jordan Regulski's three-run double, and Hesson's RBI two-bagger.
Hesson (2-1) yielded three runs and six hits over 6 1/3 innings, striking out five and walking two. And though he surrendered Dustin Blue's leadoff homer to left-center field in the second inning, and Mikey O'Connor's two-out, two-run double in the fourth, he avoided the big inning for the most part.
"I was hitting locations early," Hesson said. "Missed a couple spots early. But really just movement on the changeup and everything like that was working well today."
O'Connor (0-1), Easton's starting pitcher, didn't get out of the first inning and was relieved by Pax Echternach. The Warriors' first reliever faced two men, including Regulski (2 for 3) who hit his bases-clearing double. Echternach was relieved by Cullen Murphy, who quieted the Colonels until the fourth, when Gavin Whitby (2 for 2) hit an RBI single and courtesy runner EJ Jones scored on a pop-out to first.
Down 11-3, Easton (4-4, 0-1), playing its fifth game in six days, had a potential rally going in the fifth, when Finn McGuckin and Dylan Cassell (2 for 3, RBI) led off with back-to-back singles. That rally was squelched though, when Josh Dressler hit a rope to short that Regulski lunged forward to catch. Colonel's shortstop, who has verbally committed to Wake Forest, got to his feet, stepped on second and threw to first to complete a triple play.
But Easton wasn't quite finished.
"We felt very comfortable today and that kind of came back and bit us," Hesson said. "They made it close in the very end. We got too comfortable. We have stuff to work on as a team. Me as well. This isn't our final form. We just got to get better as a team."
Hesson was relieved after allowing a one-out single to Carter Mooney in the home seventh. Reliever Jack Walls walked the first three batters he faced before Kayden Webb stung a two-run single to center, drawing Easton within 11-6. CJ Dugan's sacrifice fly trimmed Colonel's lead to 11-7. Blue walked before Colin Mooney singled to score Webb to make it 11-8. But Walls extinguished the rally there, getting a called third strike on O'Connor to end the game.
"At the end we didn't play our best baseball," Nepert said. "We have to continue to coach no matter what the lead is. Early on we kind of stuck to a good approach. Kind of went away from that later on in the game. But when you get a nine-run lead you get a little bit of a cushion which is a great thing."
Though his team's pitching was thin, Easton head coach Albert Pritchett liked how his team battled despite the early deficit.
"We probably had a few too many walks," said Pritchett, whose team issued 13. "But like the team we've always had in Easton, we never gave up. We had a hole. Cullen Murphy and Al Rhodes came in and held down things, and our offense chipped away. We got Hesson out of the game and got to the next pitcher and scored a few runs to make it competitive. Had a couple extra errors I would have liked to have got ridden of. But we're hitting the ball. I don't think this team thinks it's ever over."
ST. MICHAELS 16 KENT ISLAND 8
STEVENSVILLE — Jacob Bealefeld (2 for 2) homered, Connor Wheeler (2 for 4) doubled, and Will Sherwood (2 for 4) stole three bases as the Saints remained undefeated.
Anthony Massaro earned the win, allowing four runs (two earned) and eight hits over four innings. Brock Grow pitched three innings for the save.
Grow also went 2 for 2 with a pair of walks, and Bobby Fink has an two-run double for St. Michaels (7-0).
SOFTBALL
ST. MICHAELS 8 KENT ISLAND 7
STEVENSVILLE — Angel Bock picked up the win, allowing seven runs on 10 hits over seven innings Thursday to lead the Saints.
Bock, who struck out seven and walked just one, was 2 for 4 at the plate. Katie Jenkins also went 2 for 4 and Myla Ramey, Mercy Haddaway and Brianna Crow each had hits. Madi White drove in a pair of runs.
QUEEN ANNE'S 7 NORTH CAROLINE 6
CENTREVILLE — Autumn Huber drove in a pair of runs and Caroline Taylor went 3 for 4 Thursday as the Lions rallied from a five-run deficit to edge the Bulldogs.
Emily Hirschbock earned the win, allowing one hit and one run over 4 2/3 innings.
Queen Anne's scored five runs on four hits in the bottom of the third inning, with Mikayla Livingston and Emilie Smith hitting RBI singles.
BOYS LACROSSE
EASTON 16 CAMBRIDGE-SD 5
EASTON — Drew Schmidt and Tyler Rardin each had three goals and two assists Wednesday to lead the Warriors.
Campbell Taliaferro and Jackson Wieland had two goals and an assist apiece for Easton (2-1) and Charlie Kaminskas had a pair of goals. Hudson Royer and Sabin Long finished with one goal and one assist each, and Logan Friend and Luke Stanco netted one goal apiece. Easton's Angel Fernandez won five faceoffs and goalie Jack Kilbourne made three saves.
GIRLS LACROSSE
SSPP 24 SALISBURY SCHOOL 6
EASTON — Senior Morgan Quade totaled five goals and seven assists, and freshman Emery Zimmerman finished with four goals and three assists Wednesday as the Sabres improved to 5-1.
Caroline Ewing had four goals and one assist for Saints Peter and Paul, and Eryn Callahan (four assists), Kendall Kroniser (two assists), Avery McCall (assist) and Eden Zimmerman each had two goals. Emma Hainey, Samantha Murphy and Julia Spero added one goal apiece for the Sabres.

title: FINAL PUSH
author: Bill Haufe
content:
FINAL PUSH

 May 25, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 959
 Words 

 Read News Document

 COLUMBIA — North Caroline High's Josh Huster said he was coming back, and he was right. He just wished he could have taken his return trip one step further.Easton High's Jake Hershey took a step further than a year ago, but fell shy of his desired destination. And Cooper Baum, Miles Fox, Alexandria Rockwell and Lila Moore went where no player had ever gone before in the history of St. Michaels High's tennis program — the state finals.
That's how the high school tennis season ended for the North Bayside's top hopefuls Saturday during the Class 2A and 1A state championships at the Wilde Lake Tennis Club.
"Not bad for small North Caroline," said Huster, who made his second consecutive state final after last year teaming with Rebecca White to win the Class 2A mixed doubles title, giving North Caroline its first state tennis championship of any kind. "Unfortunately, we didn't win. But I thought we put up a pretty good fight."
During an interview to recap last year's championship run, Huster calmly declared he and Jesse Link would be in states in 2024. Huster backed that claim, as he and Link won the 2A East Region I boys doubles title, then defeated Eastern Tech's Ryan Elmendorf and Lawson Johnson, 6-4, 6-0 in Friday's quarterfinals before ousting Easton's Clay Nagel and Kai Ferraris, 6-4, 6-1 in the semis later in the day.
"We just started slow," Huster said of the quarterfinal and semifinal victories. "And I felt like today we did the same."
But second-seeded Huster and Link could not overcome that slow start as No. 1 seed Jeeva Padmanabhan and William Chen of Poolesville earned a 6-1, 6-2 victory in the final.
"They were a great team," Huster said of the champs. "I don't think they outplayed us. They've probably been playing longer than us; more match experience. We played pretty well together. We only lost twice all season. We were in most every game (today). Credit to them."
Poolesville ended a second North Bayside title bid, when top seed Andy Wu defeated Easton's Hershey, 6-2, 6-0, in the 2A boys singles final.
"He's just a good player," Hershey said of Wu. "I've seen him at tournaments before. He just got the better of me today. He's strong in every aspect of his game. Just a really steady player."
Despite a nasty blister in the middle of his racquet hand, Hershey last week helped Easton win the 2A East Region II title. Third at states a year ago, the Warrior junior extended his undefeated season to 17-0 on Friday, when he beat Hereford's Richard Wang, 6-1, 6-3 in the quarterfinals, then bounced the No. 2 seed, La Plata's King Herald Nacua, 6-4, 7-6 (3) in a rematch of last year's semifinals.
"First match I was pretty happy with," Hershey said. "Couple moments I wanted to take back. And then second match was definitely a grind. Played the same dude I played last year in the semis. Different result this year."
The difference?
"Twenty-hour weeks every single week this summer training," Hershey said. "Traveling all over the Eastern seaboard playing. Really just hours and hours."
But those long hours of work could not carry Hershey past Wu.
"It's not over yet," Hershey said of his high school career. "One more (year)."
St. Michaels had never advanced a player or team to the finals at states until this year, when it had a boys and girls doubles team reach the 1A championship match.
"They have really just done everything that we've asked them to all season long," St. Michaels head coach Jordan Miller said of his two doubles teams. "They have worked their butts off the entire season. Postseason played every match we asked them to and did all the right things. They came out today and they competed. They put it all on the line. They didn't get the results they wanted, but they absolutely showed they belonged to be here."
Baum and Fox didn't drop a game in the boys doubles quarterfinals, routing Patuxent's Brian Platz and Daniel Segar, 6-0, 6-0. The No. 2 seed then defeated Southern Garrett's Ben Nazelrod and Shane Sisler, 6-1, 6-2, before falling 6-3, 6-2 in Saturday's final to top-seeded Arjun Mistry and Hayden Spence of Liberty.
Teammates Rockwell and Moore followed a similar path in the 1A girls doubles bracket. Seeded second, Rockwell and Moore beat Loch Raven's Christine Onananga and Angel Ibeadogbulen, 6-0, 6-4, in Friday's quarterfinal round before earning a 6-3, 6-1 semifinal win over Allegany's Maya Hare and Danica Knight. And though Rockwell and Moore battled, they couldn't beat South Carroll's Caroline Aliftiras and Audrey Lillycrop in the final, losing 6-3, 6-1.
"That's going to be the next step we're going to have to take is our players are going to have to start playing tournaments," Miller said. "That's what we're going toward.
"They were the two seed coming in and held their to final," Miller said of both his doubles teams. "And we're losing one senior. Everybody else is coming back. So we're in a good spot."
Notes: Easton's Nagel and Ferraris lost 6-4, 6-3 to McDonough's Noah Cusack and Chris Jozwick in the consolation match for 2A boys doubles. … Losing in the quarterfinals of the 2A tournament were Queen Anne's Tyler Olah (boys singles), Kent Island's Jamie Tranquill and Queen Anne's Lucy Taylor and Meg Taylor (girls doubles). … Cambridge-South Dorchester's Amy Wanex lost in the 1A girls singles semifinals before falling 7-6 (4), 6-3 to Fort Hill's Jovie Breitfeller in the consolation match. … St. Michaels' Tom Weller lost in the quarterfinals to eventual 1A boys singles champ Hunter Liao of Boonsboro. … Falling in the first round in the 1A brackets were North Dorchester's AJ Fehsenfeld (boys singles), Kent County's Nina Fahrman (girls singles) and North Dorchester's Maddie Tobat and Jules Tobat (girls doubles).

title: CHAMPS
author: Bill Haufe
content:
CHAMPS

 May 23, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Champs 
 
 1036
 Words 

 Read News Document

 LANDOVER — Clint Falduto knew last summer, predicting Cambridge-South Dorchester High's boys outdoor track and field team would win a state title.The Vikings' co-head coach knew for certain Thursday, when his 4x100 relay took runner-up honors, clinching the program's first-ever state title outdoors with one event remaining in the Class 1A state championships.
But co-head coach Lois Narr didn't know, and didn't want to know until an official verdict was announced.
"I didn't look," said Narr, who at any time could have asked Falduto, or checked the AthleticLive app on her phone to see how her team was doing. "I didn't look the whole time. I didn't want to know. All I wanted to know is every kid got a chance to do their best. And he (Falduto) kept trying to tell me and I'm like, 'Don't tell me until we know. I don't want to hear it. I don't want to be anxious. I don't want to know.' And when he told me I was just crying."
A meet that started with light rain ended with Cambridge-SD hoisting the Class 1A state championship trophy under a beaming sun in the infield of Marvin F. Wilson Stadium at the Prince George's Sports and Learning Complex.
"This is the best thing ever, man," said Cambridge-SD's Tori Willis Jr., who won the boys 300-meter intermediate hurdles in a 1A meet-record time of 38.68 seconds. "We've been doing this since two years ago when we first started. It was just a few of us, we added on, and got better and better each year. It feels like Avengers' Endgame. We finally got Thanos. We finally got Catoctin."
Cambridge-SD totaled 80½ points to defeat runner-up Catoctin (72) and third-place Western Tech (58).
The Vikings' victory was the first for a Bayside Conference school since James M. Bennett's girls won in 2004, and the first for a Bayside boys' team since Wicomico in 1988.
"They're the best," said Narr, fighting back tears. "Before we got off the bus I said to them, 'This is the finest team we've ever had.' We've never taken second. We've never taken first. It was a team effort."
Leading that effort was Willis, who not only won his second straight 300 hurdles title, but placed fourth in the 100 meters (10.98), and led a 3-4-5 Viking finish in the 110 high hurdles with a time of 14.69. Antonio Blueford (14.76) was fourth and Jayden Smith fifth in 14.86. Willis capped his day by anchoring the 4x100 relay (43.27) of Jakuez Snead, Kay'ion Marine and Teshar Drummond, breaking into a huge grin after crossing the finish line, knowing the Vikings had clinched the title.
"My main goal was just to get out very fast and just try to keep as long as possible to get the win," Willis said of the 300 hurdles, which, despite setting a new 1A state meet record, was not a personal-record.
While Falduto admitted he was hoping for a better finish in the 110 hurdles, he also noted the Vikings gained huge points from some unexpected sources, most notably Snead finishing fourth in the shot put (46-6), and Majestic Jones (6 feet) and William Jackson (5-10), finishing fifth and sixth, respectively in the high jump. Jackson also added four points with his fifth-place finish (12-6) in the pole vault.
"Just figuring out their best position of where we think they can succeed the most," Falduto said. "And we definitely put that team together this year. This year has just truly been incredible. Watching Tori break the (1A) state record, and just showing up in places we were not expected. Our boys just knew it meant every point. Even though we didn't place everywhere we wanted to, we still finished the races and got the points that were needed."
In addition to his fifth-place finish in the 110 hurdles, Smith delivered two more big efforts, taking third in the triple jump (43-¾) and fourth in the long jump (21-¾). Then there was Tekai Drummond, who settled into a rhythm in the 800 before putting on a big surge down the stretch to place second in 1:58.16.
"That was a big swing race," Narr said, noting Catoctin had three runners seeded in the top eight, but only had one finish in the top 11.
On Day 1 of the meet Wednesday, Cambridge-SD senior Kassidy Young won the girls 1A discus with a heave of 124-4 on her first attempt, beating her previous best by an impressive 12 feet.
"I wasn't expecting to PR by as much as I did," Young said who couldn't explain her first throw. "I don't even know. I just let it fly. It was a real shock. I walked up to my coach (Narr), and I couldn't even explain."
North Dorchester senior Vernon Price delivered what some may have considered a surprise, when he won the boys 1A high jump title Wednesday in his first year competing outdoors, clearing the bar at 6-6.
"I knew I could go for gold," Price said. "I wanted to go for No. 1 in the state of Maryland with 6-8. And I should have cleared but form, because it is my first year, I really haven't had a lot of time to practice.
A dual-sport athlete who also played baseball this season, Price was second in the triple jump (44-1¾) and third in the long jump (21-2).
Queen Anne's County junior Ben Marks dueled Century's Ryan Hartranft and Southern's Eric Penkala in the 2A boys 1,600 meters, finishing second with in a personal-record 4:14.03. Hartranft won in 4:13.00, while Penkala placed third in 4:15.24.
Marks came back to place second in the 800, clocking a 1:54.85 to Harford Tech's Alexander Wockenfuss, who won in 1:54.28.
Easton's Sumayah Wilkins took runner-up honors in the 2A girls high jump, clearing 5-4. Patuxent freshman Aiyana Smalley won at 5-6.
Colonel Richardson's Aydan Downie was second in the 1A boys long jump (22-4½), and Queen Anne's freshman JaDereon Thompson finished third in the 2A boys long jump (22-0).
Kent Island senior Gabrielle Bernhard was second in the 2A girls 300 hurdles (45.52), third in the pole vault (11-0) and fifth in the 100 hurdles (15.44). Cambridge-SD junior Le'Asia Todd was third in the 1A girls long jump (16-4¾), fifth in the triple jump (33-7¾), and sixth in high jump (4-8).

title: Lions can't find way past Glenelg
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions can't find way past Glenelg

 May 22, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 746
 Words 

 Read News Document

 OWINGS MILLS — It had faced tough defenses before this season.But usually Queen Anne's County High's girls lacrosse team solved the opposition's defensive scheme, finding enough openings and seams to carve a path to victory.
The Lions couldn't find a solution though late Tuesday afternoon, as Glenelg dominated possession and yielded Queen Anne's few offensive opportunities en route to a 13-3 victory in the Class 2A state championship at Stevenson University's Mustang Stadium.
"They were able to come out defensively and put on the pressure and hold it," Lions head coach Kesley Fitzgerald said of Glenelg.
The Gladiators (18-1) were also able to hold the ball. Glenelg consistently won draw controls, reached ground balls before the Lions, and seemed to have someone on the ball every time Queen Anne's (15-3) lost possession or had a pass miss connection.
"Lots of speed and explosiveness," Fitzgerald said of the Gladiators. "And when you don't have lots of possessions you have to make every single one count.
"In the beginning of the first quarter we were," said Fitzgerald, whose team fell behind 2-0 in the opening 61 seconds, then cut that deficit in half with 8:46 left in the first quarter. "We were working through some kinks on defense, and every time offense had it in the first quarter we were converting. And then it came down to the draw possessions, and just making sure we got the ball out safely. And we didn't do that as well as we have all season."
Glenelg took a lead in never surrendered 34 seconds into the game when Kayleigh White (two goals) swept in the from the left and put a shot past Lions goalie Maddie George. Just 27 seconds later, Kamryn Henson (three goals) gained possession at the top of the box, dodged two defenders and stuck a shot into the right side of the net for a 2-0 lead.
Queen Anne's, which entered the game on a 10-game winning streak in which it averaged 13 goals a game, didn't appear rattled, as it pulled within 2-1, when RJ Ensor set up Riley Klepper's goal. The Gladiators regained their two-goal cushion a little over a minute later, when Regan Kelleher (two goals, two assists) found Reilly Kelleher alone in front of the net for a goal. Maggie Metz (three goals) scored in transition, extending Glenelg's lead to 4-1 with 3:36 left in the opening quarter.
The Lions answered, as Baillie Pinder dished to Ensor to make it 4-2 with 52.4 seconds remaining in the first quarter.
But Queen Anne's wouldn't score again until Madison Brown's goal with 3:40 left on a running clock in the fourth period made it 13-3.
"Offensively, they were all moving," Fitzgerald said of Glenelg. "Great off-ball movement. That's a strong team."
A team that scored nine consecutive goals after Ensor's strike to build a 13-2 lead with 9:41 left in the contest.
Glenelg had six different goal scorers before Henson netted her second off an assist from Emmy Dello Russo with 58.8 seconds left in the first half, pushing the Gladiators' lead to 8-2 at halftime. Chloe Key, Dello Russo and Regan Kelleher also scored in the first half.
Fitzgerald rotated George in goal with Emma Dulin throughout the game, both making big saves to keep the score respectable.
"Both those girls did an amazing job," Fitzgerald said.
Glenelg tacked on three third-quarter goals, with Henson scoring once and Metz twice. Regan Kelleher and White scored one apiece in the fourth before Brown ended Queen Anne's scoring drought.
"I do know we have the makings of being right there with them," said Fitzgerald, whose team was bidding for its second state title in four years. "Wasn't our day today. Super proud of the team. They have nothing to hang their heads about. We got here. We deserved to be here. And we'll be back.
"Every year we start out and try to figure out what the roles are going to be," Fitzgerald continued. "This year we made those roles very apparent, very early; earlier than I ever have before. And that's what worked for us this year. Everybody fell into their role. I'm fortunate every year at Queen Anne's as their coach to just have amazing student-athletes."
BASEBALLBRUNSWICK 26, COL. RICHARDSON 6FREDERICK — Derrick Mitchell had a pair of hits for Colonel Richardson, which had its hopes of a third straight Class 1A state final appearance end in Tuesday's semifinal round at McCurdy Field.
Brayden Dadds, Caleb Rouser and Gavin Whitby each had one hit for the Colonels, who finished the season 20-3.

title: NHL will have a new champion this century
author: Bill Haufe
content:
NHL will have a new champion this century

 May 21, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 657
 Words 

 Read News Document

 No matter which team wins the Stanley Cup championship this year it will be a first this century.The Dallas Stars won the franchise's lone championship in 1999, months before the world worried computers would malfunction at the start of a new millennium. The New York Rangers haven't done it since their magical run in 1994 that ended a 54-year title drought.
The Edmonton Oilers have not done it since the last title of their dynasty in 1990, seven years before current star Connor McDavid was born. The Florida Panthers have never won the Cup since their inception in 1993, when hockey in the U.S. Sun Belt was just starting to become a reality.
"It's something that these all markets are starving for," said Mike Rupp, a NHL Network analyst whose three-point Game 7 performance in 2003 gave New Jersey its third championship. "I love seeing new blood in it."
New blood when it comes to a title but not unfamiliar with this stage of the playoffs. Florida and Dallas were each in their respective conference finals last year (Florida advanced to the Final, too), while New York and Edmonton are back after getting there in 2022.
Thirteen different teams have hoisted the Cup since 1999, including Chicago, Pittsburgh and Tampa Bay doing it three times, and New Jersey, Colorado and Los Angeles twice each.
The more things change ...
None of the remaining teams has had the same coach for more than the past two seasons.
Paul Maurice took over the Panthers and Peter DeBoer the Stars in the summer of 2022. Peter Laviolette got the Rangers' job less than a year ago. Kris Knoblauch was an early-season replacement for the Oilers in November.
Part of that is just the cyclical nature of coaching changes in hockey, though the high volume over the past 18 months has gotten the attention of the fraternity, with DeBoer calling it "insanity."
There's still value in experience, though, with Knoblauch the only first-time NHL head coach in the final four. He is eight wins away from being the fourth coach hired in-season to win the Cup that year.
Laviolette is in his sixth head coaching job. He coached Carolina to the Stanley Cup championship in 2006 and took Philadelphia in 2010 and Nashville in 2017 to the final. DeBoer has two trips to the final on his resume: 2012 with New Jersey and 2016 with San Jose. No one has coached more NHL regular-season and playoff games without winning the Cup than Maurice with 1,973.
... the more they stay the same
This isn't quite like the Tampa Bay Lightning going back to back in 2020 and '21 and reaching the final in '22, but these teams have all played a lot of playoff hockey in recent years.
Counting their bubble run to the Cup Final four years ago, the Stars have been in 79 playoff games dating to 2019.
"Dallas has been a good team for a long time, just never able to kind of get over the hump and had some really tough paths in the playoffs," Rupp said.
McDavid and the Oilers have played 54 postseason games since 2020, their first of five consecutive postseason appearances, with an asterisk on the expanded pandemic format.
The Panthers, who have played 52 over the past five playoffs, have usurped the Lightning as the best team in Florida, including knocking their cross-state rivals out in the first round this year. They're now co-Cup favorites along with Dallas, according to BetMGM Sportsbook.
The Rangers, with 40 games of playoff experience since 2020, are actually the longest shot on the board despite winning the Presidents' Trophy as the NHL's best team in the regular season. Since general manager Chris Drury took over, New York has gone from youth movement to powerhouse.
"The days of the rebuild of the Rangers, it wasn't all that long ago," Rupp said. "They were setting themselves up for some very lean years, and they turned it around a lot quicker, I think, than people thought."

title: Glenelg ends Bucs' three-peat bid
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Glenelg ends Bucs' three-peat bid

 May 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 Read News Document

 BURTONSVILLE — Yes, defense wins championships.It also ends title streaks.
Tim Iannarino and Chase Buscher each scored four goals, and Glenelg High held two-time defending Class 2A state champion Kent Island scoreless for almost the entire second half Saturday on the way to a 16-8 victory in a 2A state semifinal at Paint Branch High.
The third-seeded Gladiators (14-3) advance to Wednesday's 2A state championship game, where they will face No. 5 seed Hereford (13-2) at 8 p.m. at Stevenson University's Mustang Stadium in Baltimore.
"Hey, their defense was ready to play," Kent Island head coach Bobby Woolley said of Glenelg, which held the Buccaneers (12-5) to their lowest goal total since a 12-4 loss at Urbana on April 8. "Certainly they played with a lot of energy early, which set the tone for how they were going to play for the day. It was tough. They got big, athletic kids coming at you. And it made for a little bit tougher time for us on offense."
Mark Rees scored unassisted to give Kent Island a 1-0 lead less than 2 minutes into the game. But the Gladiators scored six of the game's next seven goals for a 6-2 lead 1:17 into the second quarter.
The Buccaneers looked to be putting together a comeback, when Aidan Henry scored on an extra-man opportunity with 9:42 left in the half, and Keegan Green (two goals) netted an unassisted goal at the 9-minute mark, shaving Glenelg's lead to 6-4.
But that's where the rally ended.
Tim Iannarino came from behind the net and snapped a shot past Bucs goalie Christian Lemme with 7:53 left in the half. Collin Szczepanski set up a crank from Chris Iannarino with 3:02 remaining. Glenelg won the ensuing faceoff and Shane Dubois raced down the sideline before feeding Buscher for a goal to make it 9-4 with under 3 minutes to go in the opening half.
Kent Island senior captain Tucker Claxton scored to make it 9-5 with 2:15 left in the first half.
But the Bucs, who came in riding an eight-game winning streak, wouldn't score again against Glenelg's man-to-man defense until Green's goal with 1:22 remaining in the game, going almost 35 minutes without a score.
"We watched film and their offense can really put the ball in the back of the net," Glenelg head coach Josh Hatmaker said of the Bucs. "And they score in bunches. That's always a concern. But I was confident in our kids and our goalie play. I thought team defense wise we played excellent today. That's what we pride ourselves on."
Conner Hammond's goal with 25 seconds to go before intermission gave Glenelg a 10-5 halftime lead. That lead was extended to 12-5 in the third quarter. Buscher took a pass from Chris Iannarino, and with his back to the goal, flipped a backward shot into the net for an 11-5 lead near the halfway point of the third period. Brandon Klopp converted a DuBois pass to make it 12-5 heading into the fourth.
"Offensively, I thought we could exploit some things with their defense," Hatmaker said. "And our kids really played as a whole unit, not just as an individual. That's how our system is based. I thought they were really successful at it."
Glenelg's offense continued to be successful in the fourth. Tim Iannarino's set up his brother's third goal then scored his fourth on an EMO. Szczepanski scored unassisted with 4:27 left in the game, and 32 seconds later, Hammond scored another EMO to make it 16-5.
"I think they came out super intense," Woolley said of Glenelg. "Kind of got some calls to go their way at some critical moments. That seemed to take some momentum (from us), that they gained; put us in a tough spot. Big mental game today. They threw some really heavy punches that we really didn't have the ultimate counter to."
Kent Island ended its near 35-minute scoring draught with 1:22 left in the game, when Owen Wynot set up Green's second goal. Wynot and Claxton each added an unassisted goal in the final 1:12.

title: Friars strike quick, top SSPP
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Friars strike quick, top SSPP

 May 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 ANNAPOLIS — Saints Peter and Paul High's boys lacrosse team swept Archbishop Curley during their two regular-season meetings this spring.The top-seeded Sabres met the Friars for a third time Friday at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium. Only this time, the two-time defending Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association B Conference champions showed just how much experience matters.
The Friars scored twice in the opening minute, taking control with a five-goal opening flurry, then tightened its grip even further during a dominating second quarter en route to a 18-9 victory over Sts. Peter & Paul and a third straight MIAA B Conference title.
"I guess we're too young and they couldn't handle where it was," Sabres head coach Todd Wolters said. "They (Curley) came out running. We came out walking. Again, they (SSPP) haven't been here. That's their third (title) in a row. They got a lot of seniors on that team and I think that showed. And again, they're a really good team."
Curley (12-7) wasted little time showing how good it is, as senior Carson Gianelli (three goals, assist) scored just 28 seconds into the game, then added a second 11 seconds later. Senior captain James Zingo (four goals) made it 3-0 with 7:08 left in the first quarter. Brandon Mejia (three goals) and Matt Ramirez scored in the closing minute for a 5-0 Curley lead.
Sts. Peter and Paul's Grant Messick (three goals) converted a Noah Zimmerman pass into the Sabres' first goal with 16.6 seconds left in the first quarter, but that was the only ball put past Friars goalie Ryan Cosey in the first quartr. Curley answered, Carson Gianelli setting up the first of Dominic Broadwater's three goals with just 5.6 seconds left in the opening period for a 6-1 Friars' lead.
"It was huge," Curley head coach Chris Ogle said of the opening quarter. "I think experience played a role in that. Our seniors, our leaders carried us through that first quarter."
That senior leadership continue to pace the Friars in the second quarter.
After Zingo's goal 8 seconds into the quarter made it 7-1, Messick responded with an unassisted strike for the Sabres 15-5).
But Curley's Cooper Granados, Carson Gianelli, Ramirez and Gavin Albright scored the game's next four goals in a little over 2 minutes. Albright and Mejia tacked on two more for a commanding 13-2 lead with 35.1 seconds left in the first half.
"Again, they've been here," Wolters said of Curley. "They know what it takes to win. They out-physicaled us. They out-hustled us. We'd turn it over, not with them doing anything."
Liam Durnbaugh (three goals) scored on an extra-man opportunity with 2.9 seconds left in the first half to make it 13-3 at the break.
Zingo made it 14-3 early in the third. But the Sabres scored consecutive goals for the first time when Vincent Dyer set up a Zimmerman goal and Durnbaugh scored unassisted to make it 14-5 with under 6 minutes left in the third.
Curley called time and came back with a pair of goals, Albright (three goals) bouncing a shot past Sabres goalie Hank Wolters and Mejia scoring while falling down to make it 16-5.
Sts. Peter & Paul, which won 9-6 at Curley on April 23 and 11-9 at home on May 10, continued battling, as JJ Rardin — a focal point for the Friars' defense — and Messick scored just 12 seconds apart, pulling the Sabres within 16-7 heading into the fourth.
"My defensive coaches did an outstanding job putting together a game plan that we've kind of had in our backpocket," Ogle said. "We had a feeling we were going to see the Sabres again, and the kids executed to perfection for us. We wanted to take Rardin out of the game. Our boys did an outstanding job with that. I also think we shot the ball better. We've been working on that and it really came to fruition today."
The teams played even in the fourth quarter, with Zimmerman scoring on an EMO and Durnbaugh scoring with a left-handed shot with a little over 6 minutes left. David Fritz and Zingo added goals for the Friars.
"I can't say anything but give them credit," Wolters said. "The second half we beat them (6-5). Not that that matters. Our kids could have given up when you're down by 10. To come back in the second half, and they were still shooting with a minute to go.
"The kids didn't give up," Coach Wolters continued. "We're young. We're going to be back next year. Then we'll come back with some experience."
GIRLS LACROSSE
QUEEN ANNE'S 6, STEPHEN DECATUR 4STEVENSVILLE — Junior RJ Ensor had a hat trick and set up a fourth goal Friday, as the sixth-seeded Lions defeated the No. 2 seed Seahawks in a Class 2A state semifinal at Kent Island High.
Queen Anne's will play fourth-seeded Glenelg for the state championship on Tuesday at 4 p.m. at Stevenson University's Mustang Stadium.
Baillie Pinder (assist), Riley Klepper and Kaisa Hickson each scored once for Queen Anne's.

title: Todd earns four titles; Vikes win boys crown
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Todd earns four titles; Vikes win boys crown

 May 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 919
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — Cambridge-South Dorchester High's girls track and field program has had a nice list of talented athletes, including a handful of state champions.Le'Asia Todd may have pushed her way to the top of that list.
Two days after winning the triple jump at the Class 1A East Region outdoor championships, Todd returned to Kent Island High on Thursday to win the long jump, high jump and 300-meter intermediate hurdle crowns during an impressive second day.
"I guess you have to say that she is the finest female track athlete we've ever had," said Dr. Lois Narr, Cambridge-SD's co-head coach. "We've never had a girl that I can think of who's won four open events at the regionals."
The defending Class 1A state champion, Todd won the triple jump during Day 1 on Tuesday, with a leap of 34 feet, 3 inches, finishing well ahead of Kent County's Zoe Angennieux, who was runner-up at 30-10.
The junior started her day Thursday by winning the long jump with an effort of 16-5. She brushed sand off her legs and moved over to high jump, where she cleared her first height, but then had to pause to run the 300 hurdles. Todd clocked a first-place time of 49.29 seconds in the hurdles, then returned to the high jump, where she won with a 4-8, clearing the height in fewer attempts than runner-up Angenieux.
"She's so talented," Narr said.
Cambridge-SD picked up a fifth title, when Kassidy Young won the shot put with a heave of 33-1, and also got big points from Al'Janae Jackson, who was runner-up in the 100 meters (13.06) and 200 (27.27) and the pole vault (7-9).
Washington won the girls team title with 124 points, followed by Cambridge-SD and Colonel Richardson, who finished tied for second with 89 points.
Colonel was led by its relays, as the 4x100 (Chaney Paul, Sadie Prettyman, Viergena Toussaint, Anijah Hammond) won in 52.99, and 4x400 (Addison Claytor, Paul, Prettyman, Landine Dorleans) finished first in 4:20.60. The Colonels' 4x200 relay of Hammond, Toussaint, Prettyman and Claytor were second (1:52.57).
Led by Jayden Smith, Tori Willis Jr., and Tekai Drummond, Cambridge-SD won the 1A boys title with 155½ points, easily outdistancing second-place Perryville (94½).
Smith led a 1-2-3 Viking finish in the 110 high hurdles, crossing the finish line in 14.701 to edge Willis (14.705) and Antonio Blueford (14.82). Smith went on to win the long jump (21-2½) and was fourth in the triple jump (42-4).
Willis won the 300 hurdles (39.28), was second in the 100 (10.68), and teamed with Jakuez Snead, Kay'ion Marine and Tekai Drummond to win the 4x100 relay in 43 seconds flat.
Tekai Drummond gave the Vikings a fourth individual title, when he won the 800 meters in 1:59.64. He also joined his brother Teshar Drummond, Zy'Meir Wilson and Preston Adkins to place second in the 4x800 relay (8:27.26).
Kent County senior Larry Steward, who won the Class 1A state indoor high jump title this past season, added another championship to his resume, clearing 6-4 to finish first at regionals. Teammate Gavin Larrimore won the shot put in 42-10 and was second in the discus (127-3). North Dorchester's Jase Todd won the discus with a throw of 128-5.
Harford Tech swept the 2A East titles, the boys totaling 151 points, while the girls finished with 171.
Kent Island girls were second with 89 points, as sophomore Lacey Dauses won the 800 (2:23.28), while senior Gabrielle Bernhard delivered another strong performance in her final meet on her home track, placing second in the 100 hurdles (15.55), 300 hurdles (45.81) and pole vault (10-10). Bernhard also teamed with Kendra Coffey, Reese Heyliger and Dauses to take second in the 4x400 relay (4:12.02).
Easton senior Sumayah Wilkins won the high jump, clearing the bar in a personal-record 5-6.
"I had a little hiccup with 5-2," said Wilkins, who got over the height on her third attempt.
Wilkins then went to 5-6, and again needed a third attempt before cleanly slipping over the bar to win the title.
"I was looking at the heat sheets and some girls were jumping 5-3," said Wilkins, who was seeded first. "I was seeded the highest, but I said, 'That doesn't mean anything. They could come here and finish on top. So I'm going to come here and just do my best.'"
North Caroline's 4x800 relay of Linda Ridgelll, Brooke Sullivan, Seanna Rupp and Morgan Knott proved best in the region, winning in 10:05.91.
Kent Island's boys finished third in the team competition, getting a boost from Evan Newcomer. A senior, Newcomer missed the bulk of the indoor season while recovering from a foot injury, but looked in fine form Thursday, winning 400 in a school-record 49.52 and the 200 (21.99). Newcomer then anchored the Bucs' 4x400 relay to victory in the meet's final event, as he, Isaiah Diaz, Caleb Heater and Trey Donnelly won in 3:30.56, punctuating head coach Justin Holland's final meet on his home track.
"Mentally-wise I knew he'd be there," Holland said of Newcomer. "I didn't know if he was ever going to get as fast as he is currently. I didn't know if he was going to get all that back."
Kent Island also got victories from Jack Middleton in the high jump (6-0) and Josh Fuller in the shot put (45-4½).
Queen Anne's middle-distance standout Ben Marks won the 1,600 in 4:21.32, then came back to finish second in the 800 (1:55.61), getting edged by Harford Tech's Alex Wockenfuss (1:55.28). Queen Anne's freshman teammate Ja'Dereon Thompson won the long jump in 21-9.
Easton's Jed Smith was third in the 1,600 (4:34.09) and 3,200 (10:15.08).

title: Lions rally for first Bayside title; Caroline boys defend throne
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions rally for first Bayside title; Caroline boys defend throne

 May 15, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 838
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Queen Anne's County High's No. 3 girls doubles team of Sydney Pinder and Kara Ringold were down 4-1 when head coach Dee Fisher approached."I asked them, 'Hey, are you guys having fun?'" Fisher said. "And they were like, 'No. We're not.' I was like, 'You guys need to go out there and have fun and relax.' Just the things you can say to kids, and nothing tennis related, and it just made them relax."
Pinder and Ringold rallied to win, then watched Hayden Legg rally for a clinching victory at No. 3 singles Tuesday, May 7, helping Queen Anne's defeat Stephen Decatur, 4-3, at Washington College for its first Bayside Conference championship in girls tennis.
While the Lions were winning their first title, North Caroline's boys were winning a second straight conference crown, topping James M. Bennett, 4-3, to cap a perfect 15-0 season.
"We lost one match last season," Bulldogs second-year boys head coach James Donelan said. "It was their goal to go undefeated this year. And we were able to do that, which was huge.
We had a couple of close matches at the end of the season that just took some real grit to pull out and some real mental toughness from our boys," Donelan said of a 4-3 win at St. Michaels on April 24 and a 4-3 victory over Easton in the regular-season finale May 1. "It was really impressive to watch. Their growth and their ability to face adversity, face everybody coming at you, giving you their best every single night and just finding a way to win."
The Bulldogs did that again against the South champion Clippers.
North Caroline's No. 1 singles team of Josh Huster and Jesse Link defeated Cypress Schnatterly and Joe Chen, 9-7, while Ryan Canter and Hayden Kent beat Bennett's Daniel Ryu and Mason Layne, 8-4, in second doubles. But the Clippers avoided a double sweep, when Shafay Qaiser and Rishi Kandagatla earned an 8-5 win over Gavin O'Brien and Yossin Roblero-Velasquez at No. 3.
It remained close, as Bennett's Chen defeated Link, 8-5, at second singles, and Ryu outlasted Canter, 9-7 at No. 3. But Roblero-Velasquez rolled to an 8-1 victory over Landon Blumenthal at No. 4. Huster, who last year teamed with Rebecca White to win the Class 2A state mixed doubles title — North Caroline's first-ever state tennis title of any kind — clinched the victory against Bennett and the perfect record with an 8-3 victory over Schnatterly at No. 1.
"Going into this season, after the success that we had last year, we were definitely very confident," Donelan said. "We knew it wasn't going to be handed to us. We knew that everybody was going to be putting a target on our back, and that they knew we only graduated one senior and then all these boys were returning."
Unlike Donelan, Fisher entered the season thinking rebuild after graduating nine seniors from a year ago. Instead, the Lions went unbeaten in the North and 13-1 overall, with the lone loss coming against Decatur.
And while Queen Anne's drew a rematch with the Seahawks for the Bayside championship, Fisher didn't want his team deviating from its usual approach.
"Just treat it like a regular match and have fun," Fisher said to his team.
The Lions' No. 1 doubles team of Lucy Taylor and younger sister Meg Taylor lost 8-6 to Decatur's Ana Pena and Emily Ferguson. But Queen Anne's Hayden Legg and Marylee Kline beat Brooke Berquist and Kalli Nordstrom, 8-2, at No. 2, while Pinder and Ringold erased their 4-1 deficit en route to an 8-6 victory over Anika Karl and Emmie Weber at No. 3.
The Seahawks moved to a 3-2 lead, when Pena defeated Lucy Taylor, 8-2 at first singles, and Ferguson earned an 8-2 win over Meg Taylor at No. 2. Kline tied the match at 3-3 with her 8-6 win over Nordstrom at No. 4.
That left No. 3 singles, where Karl built a 4-1 lead on Legg. Again Fisher spoke with his player.
"I was like, 'Come on Hayden. You can play better,'" Fisher said. "'Focus. Take your time.' And basically she just started turning it around."
Legg did turn it around, rallying for an 8-6 title-clinching victory.
"I was like, 'It's going to be tough,'" Fisher said. "She's like the most chill person. She just kept coming back and coming back."
Yet after Legg had completed her comeback to seal the title, nobody from Queen Anne's stormed the court or hoisted their teammate onto their shoulders for a victory lap.
"Nobody got excited," Fisher said. "We just all like took it all in, like, 'Good job Hayden.'" Fisher said. "I think that's just the mentality of our team. We treat it like a regular match. We just do what we do.
"It felt even better because we lost to Decatur during the regular season," Fisher said. "Hey we fixed our wrongs, made some corrections and won it."
What Fisher wasn't expecting came next.
"They were like, 'Come here coach Fisher and take a picture,'" Fisher said. "And then they started spraying me with silly string. It was fun."

title: Rardin scores five goals in return as top-seeded Sabres grind way past Falcons for spot in MIAA B Conference championship
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Rardin scores five goals in return as top-seeded Sabres grind way past Falcons for spot in MIAA B Conference championship

 May 14, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 881
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — It was the No. 1 seed.It had won 11 of its last 12 games, and had already twice beaten its opponent.
But none of that matter to Saints Peter and Paul High boys head lacrosse coach Todd Wolters after the first half of Tuesday's Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association B Conference semifinal.
After mustering just one first-quarter goal and carrying a four-goal cushion into halftime, Wolters made clear to his team he wasn't happy.
"Coach pulled us over at halftime and told us that this could be the end of our season," sophomore face-off man Grant Messick said. "'We could be done here.' But none of us want that. I think he kind of brought that out of us, just saying we could be going to Navy this Friday to win a championship that hasn't been done in a decade."
The Sabres responded, outscoring No. 4 Gerstell Academy by three goals in a decisive third quarter, catapulting them to a 13-8 victory on a dreary Tuesday afternoon.
Sts. Peter & Paul (15-4) advances to Friday's MIAA B Conference championship game where it will meet second-seed and two-time defending champion Archbishop Curley (11-7) at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium at 5 p.m. The Sabres defeated Curley twice during the regular season.
"They were taking a team lightly, like they've already won," said Wolters, whose team won 7-6 at Gerstell on April 12, then routed the Falcons 16-3 on their home turf April 30. "And they've done that before. We just lose focus."
In his first game back from injury, JJ Rardin (five goals) gave the Sabres a 1-0 lead with 2:22 left in the first quarter, when he scored off an assist from Andrew Steinhardt.
Gerstell (6-10) tied the score on Bronson Peters' goal less than 2 minutes into the second quarter. Rardin gained possession out in front of the net and fired his second goal just under the crossbar to make it 2-1 just 18 seconds later. But the Falcons came right back with Ryan Ellis beating Sabres goalie Hank Wolters (11 saves) to make it 2-all.
Davis Kimminau whipped a shot in from the right side, and less than two minutes later, set up Vincent Dyer's goal to nudge Sts. Peter & Paul to a 4-2 lead. But Peters (four goals) scored at the midway point of the second quarter to make it a one-goal game again.
"They came out and they didn't want their season to end," Messick said of Gerstell. "They came out with nothing to lose. We're the one seed. They come out and they beat us, then it's a huge upset. And if they don't it's not what they were expected to do. So I think they had that mentality while we came out thinking, 'Well, we smoked them before. We're going to roll them this time.' But they didn't. They came out and they fought really hard."
The Sabres scored the last three goals of the half, as Liam Durnbaugh, Noah Zimmerman and Rardin each tallied to make it 7-3 at the break.
"Our guys were in it," Gerstell head coach Ryan Drenner said. "We stayed in the fight the entire game. That was the biggest difference. We were here a couple weeks ago April 30. Very lopsided. We try to learn a lesson from every game regardless of the outcome of the game. And so for that one it was we had to come up with a better plan of how to travel down here and be ready to go from the jump. So we changed how we warm up just to be a little bit more alert from the start. I thought our guys did that today and we played four quarters of a great lacrosse game."
Gerstell cut its deficit to 7-4 just 19 seconds into the third quarter on a goal by Peters. Zimmerman scored for the Sabres, but Matthew Schols answered for the Falcons.
Sts. Peter & Paul took control the remainder of the quarter, getting one goal each from Steinhardt (four assists) and Kimminau, and two more from Rardin for a 12-5 lead heading into the fourth quarter.
"We know how good we are," Wolters said. "The third quarter we go and we really just started opening it up. And then in the fourth quarter we thought it was done."

title: Bucs survive Easton rally
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Bucs survive Easton rally

 May 14, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1174
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — The bus carrying the Kent Island High boys lacrosse team had already left by the time Easton head coach Dennis Keenan emerged from the storage shed that serves as his team's quasi locker room."There's a reason why they're reigning champs," Keenan said of the Buccaneers.
One of the biggest reasons Monday was Kent Island didn't give Drew Schmidt any room or angle to shoot in the dramatic closing seconds, the senior attackman's last shot of his high school career bouncing left of the mark, as the Bucs hung on for a 12-11 victory in the Class 2A East Region I final.
"I thought we played our hearts out," said Keenan, whose team finished the season 11-3. "It was a great game. They're a great team. Coach (Bobby) Woolley does a great job. They'll be a tough out for anybody else."
The two-time defending Class 2A state champion, Kent Island (11-4) is seeded seventh for the state playoffs, and will play at No. 2 Stephen Decatur (12-3) on Wednesday at 7 p.m. in a quarterfinal. The Seahawks defeated the Bucs, 14-11, on April 19 in their one regular-season meeting. Since then Kent Island has won seven straight, including a 20-14 victory over Decatur in the Bayside Conference championship on May 6.
"A little bit more interesting than we would like," said Woolley, whose team held a five-goal lead on Easton with 5:24 remaining in the third quarter. "Two good teams going at it. And there's only one ball and you've got a lot of energy going around. It's tough to maintain full control when a bunch of adolescent boys are getting after it."
Kent Island looked to be in control when Micah Quinn (two goals) snapped a shot over the head of Easton goalie Jack Kilbourne (14 saves) a little past the midway point of the third quarter for an 11-6 Buccaneers' lead.
But the Warriors, despite losing senior midfield standout Hudson Royer to a game-ending leg injury with 7:23 left in the second quarter, began slowly closing that gap.
Senior Tyler Rardin (team-high four goals) rolled right and parked a rocket past Bucs goalie Christian Lemme (nine saves) with 26.3 seconds left in the third to draw Easton within 11-7.
Kilbourne made a huge stop on Owen Wynot (three goals) with Kent Island on an extra-man opportunity early in the fourth. Rardin cranked his second goal into the lower left corner with 9:13 left, trimming the Bucs' lead to 11-8.
Rardin hit the left pipe during an Easton EMO, but Schmidt gain possession and fed Blake Royer for a goal that pulled Easton within two with 8:38 left.
Kent Island, which got outstanding face-off work from Quinn McFaden, who won 18 of 24 draws, won the ensuing face-off but turned the ball over. The Warriors raced down field, and again Schmidt dished to Blake Royer for a goal, bringing Easton within 11-10 with 8 minutes left.
"I definitely got a little nervous," Kent Island senior midfielder Tucker Claxton said. "But we're well conditioned enough to pull it out."
Just 52 seconds after their once five-goal cushion had dwindled to one, the Bucs got back on the board, as Henry Aidan set up Keegan Green (team-high four goals) for a goal and a 12-10 lead.
But Rardin answered. Moving left to right, the senior attackman sliced the Bucs defense and whipped a shot over his left shoulder into the net to make it 12-11 with 6:18 left.
Kilbourne made yet another big stop with just over 5 minutes left, this time foiling Mark Rees (two assists).
"Jack was awesome tonight," Keenan said. "I think we only gave up three goals in the second half."
Still holding its one-goal edge, Kent Island had a chance to kill the majority of the remaining clock, when Easton was hit for a one-minute unnecessary roughness flag with 1:43 left. But the Warriors regained possession on a Bucs turnover.
Easton called time with 1:16 left. Play resumed, with Schmidt holding the ball until both teams were even with 43 seconds left. Schmidt began looking for an opening on the left side. But Kent Island's defense gave him little space and with the Warrior sideline counting down the final seconds, Schmidt fired a shot that Lemme watched bounce wide left to end the game, starting the Buccaneers' celebration.
"I'm super proud of this team," said Hudson Royer, who watched the remainder of the game from the sideline. "I'm super proud of Drew, stepping up as a big part of this team. He's a big part of the reason we were so in this game."
Schmidt and Hudson Royer are both headed to the University of Lynchburg to continue their playing careers.
"I'm just proud of all our guys that stepped up," Schmidt said. "Even when our captain (Royer), one of our best players, went down, we still stepped up and fought back. And we lost by one. We easily could have won that game."
Goals by Claxton and Green staked the Buccaneers to a 2-0 lead a little over 3 minutes into the game. Hudson Royer scored Easton's first goal with 5:31 left in the first quarter, but limped off the field.
Play continued to see-saw. Wynot converted a Gavan Henry feed for a 3-1 led just 6 seconds after Royer's strike. Schmidt and Rardin scored 1:23 apart to forge the game's only tie at 3-all with 2:07 left in the opening quarter.
But Rees scored off a failed Easton clear with 50.8 seconds left in the first quarter, giving Kent Island a lead it never relinquished the rest of the way.
The Bucs outscored Easton, 5-3, in the second quarter on a pair of Wynot goals and one each from Green, Quinn, and Aidan, who scored short-handed midway through the quarter.
"In that first half we executed just how we thought," Claxton said. "We took our foot off the gas a little bit, which looking forward we may try to push out a little bit more. First half executed well. But we had the lead and we were trying to take the time off (in the second half)."
Campbell Taliaferro scored twice in the second quarter for Easton, the second off a Blake Royer assist with just under a minute left in the first half to get the Warriors within 9-6 at the break.
But Kent Island extended its lead to 11-6 on goals from Green and Quinn before Easton's late push.
"I think the game plan was right until they realized the urgency was on their offense," Woolley said. "We played really stout. We made a couple kind of bonehead mistakes that in any game we wouldn't make honestly. And after that we just had to grind out three quarters and finish it out.
"One goal is the margin of victory," Woolley continued. "That's all you need this time of year. It's a full-team effort. I think we did a real nice job with the face-off dot, which helped us get possessions when it mattered. It goes a long way for the cadence of the team. We made some mistakes in the clearing game. But at the end of the day, a win's a win."

Saints grind way into final

 May 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)
