title: Mautz' first goal proves to be game-winner for Saints
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Mautz' first goal proves to be game-winner for Saints

 September 25, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 708
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — Johnny Mautz hadn't played high school soccer before this season.Judging by the celebration he triggered midway through Tuesday night's second half, his St. Michaels High teammates are elated he decided to give the game a go this season.
Ethan Royer crossed a ball that Mautz converted into what proved to be the game-winning goal, as the Saints rallied from a halftime deficit to notch a 3-2 victory over Class 1A rival and previously unbeaten Colonel Richardson.
"I was playing baseball for awhile but I just stopped playing last year," said Mautz, a standout on the Saints' basketball team. "I never played soccer 'cause I didn't want to play three sports. But I said I might as well come out because I was only playing one sport (basketball). And then the rest is history."
There was also a touch of history attached to Mautz' score.
"That was his first goal of the year," St. Michaels head coach Pat Hambleton said of Mautz. "He's hit the post six times."
That strike with 21 minutes, 9 seconds remaining not only capped a three-goal, second-half surge, giving St. Michaels a 3-1 lead, but it also afforded the Saints (3-2 overall, 2-1 North Bayside) the breathing room they needed to weather Colonels' late-game push.
Not quite 4 minutes after having a goal erased by an offsides call, Colonel (4-1, 2-1) took a 1-0 lead on Aydan Downie's unassisted tally with 9:42 left in the first half.
St. Michaels' best chance to pull even came with just under 2 minutes to go in the first half, when Miles Fox put a shot right on Colonel keeper Cohen Carels, who made a midsection stop.
The Saints pulled even though just 1:26 into the second half, when Sherwin Mendez parked a direct kick into the back of the net for a 1-all tie.
"I think their free kick a minute and a half into the second half definitely gave them some momentum," Colonel head coach Dillon Shaheen said. "And they took that and ran with it."
Not quite 10 minutes later, Fox got deep on the left wing and steered a crossing pass that Connor Wheeler banged into the net for a 2-1 St. Michaels lead.
"Their sweeper was playing a little too far back I noticed," Hambleton said. "He was solely intercepting through balls, so I just made a small adjustment, where once he left for that through ball, I had a forward there, and it happened to be Connor. So he left, peeled off to Miles. Miles received and played that ball across, and it was wide open in the front of the net. It was just a good momentum boost that we needed to start the half."
Less than 8 minutes later, Royer slid a pass from the left side through the crease to the right post and a waiting Mautz for a 3-1 lead.
"I've been working on staying back post so that I can get whatever comes my way," Mautz said. "And Ethan played me a beautiful ball and I was just right there for the lefty finish."
Colonel wasn't quite finished though.
With 15:06 remaining, St. Michaels was called for a handball in the box. Colonel's Angel Castro Rios calmly deposited the penalty kick to the left of St. Michaels keeper Lucas Greenwood to make it a one-goal difference.
With Colonel continuing to push into the Saints' end, Hambleton dropped his team into defensive mode. St. Michaels foiled rushes and generally got in the way over the final 12 minutes, with Colonel's best chance for the equalizer coming with 6:37 left, when Greenwood smothered a loose ball near the left post in front of a charging Downie.
"Energy. They definitely came out a little more ready than we were, and we talked to them about that at halftime," Shaheen said. "I think they wanted the ball more it seemed. We match up pretty well with them, and they know they match up well with us. What it usually comes down to is which ever team plays harder, and they were definitely that team."
NORTH CAROLINE 8 CAMBRIDGE-SD 0
CAMBRIDGE — Omar Marroquin had a hat trick as the Bulldogs earned their first win of the season.
North Caroline (1-4, 1-2) also got goals from Mason Shilling, Adrian Lopez Rivera, Brayden Boarts, Karson Hollingworth and Jimmy Cohoon.

title: Warriors survive Bulldogs' rally
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors survive Bulldogs' rally

 September 20, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 836
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — It didn't matter that North Caroline High's football team had lost its first two games this season.The Bulldogs just scared Easton head coach Matt Griffith. And in a furious fourth-quarter span of just over four minutes they showed why, shaving a 28-point Warrior lead to just seven.
That's when Mikey O'Connor took over. Easton's senior quarterback ran for a pair of first downs and threw for another in the final 2:52 Friday night to finally secure a 28-21 victory that pushed the Warriors' record to 3-0.
"They got great athletes all over the field," Griffith said of North Caroline. "They've struggled early on, but you saw exactly how explosive they can be, and how quick they can be explosive. That's what I was worried about. Sometimes you can do all the right things, but sometimes really good athletes can make plays. And that's a lot of what happened in the last five minutes of the twilight zone that we're calling it."
O'Connor hit Diontaye Copper for a 35-yard touchdown pass 1:41 into the third quarter, and Dominic Stanco tacked on the point-after kick for a 28-0 Easton lead.
The Warriors had not allowed a point all season until North Caroline's Tyson Weber scored on a 16-yard run with just under seven minutes left in the game, drawing the Bulldogs (0-3) within 28-7. Mason Shilling added the extra point.
Easton went three-and-out on its next possession, with O'Connor booting a quick kick to North Caroline's 27. Bulldog senior quarterback Corey Bunce hit Derek Jones for 13 yards, then connected with Zymear Smith for a 33-yard pickup. Weber scored on a 27-yard touchdown run on the next play and Shilling again converted the PAT, narrowing Easton's lead to 28-14 with 3:57 left.
North Caroline recovered the ensuing onsides kick at the Warrior 47. Bunce hit Jones for a 20-yard gain. Easton's Tymiere Thomas sacked Bunce for a 5-yard loss. But the Bulldogs' quarterback fired toward the end zone on the next play, and watched the ball deflect into the hands of Jones for a 33-yard touchdown. Shilling's point-after kick made it 28-21 with 2:52 remaining.
"Hell of a comeback," North Caroline head coach Nic McMorris said. "I'm so proud of the resilience of our guys. It was the first time that we recognized this team.
"They're a great team," McMorris added of Easton. "They have such a dynamic offense. But we were moving the ball and just kept shooting ourselves in the foot. And then we just started playing inspired football."
North Caroline drove from its 38 to the Easton 12 when it fumbled the ball away late in the first quarter. But the Bulldogs regained possession four plays later when O'Connor's pass was deflected and intercepted by Smith. Again Caroline moved the ball, marching 32 yards to the Warrior 8. But the Bulldogs again fumbled, with Easton recovering at the 1.
Easton's next drive ended with a fumble, giving North Caroline possession at the Warrior 25. But North Caroline went no where on three plays. Shilling came on to attempt a 40-yard field goal, but slipped on his approach, the kick falling well short.
The Warriors, who took a 7-0 lead on O'Connor's 3-yard touchdown run and Stanco's PAT with 3:54 left in the first quarter, stretched their lead to 14-0 with 2:11 left in the first half, when Jordan Horsey slammed in from five yards out. Stanco again made the extra point.
Easton took advantage of a short Caroline punt, as O'Connor hit Carter Mooney for 18 yards, and Copper for 17 yards before scoring on a 2-yard run for a 21-0 halftime lead.
"We came out with a game plan and we executed very well," Griffith said. "I think we did a lot of really good things early, even with two turnovers. Those are our first two turnovers of the year. We were able to bounce back."
So was North Caroline.
"No excuses," Griffith said. "Caroline's a good football team. They're a very good football team for being 0-3."
It's one-time 28-point cushion reduced to just seven, Dustin Blue recovered the onsides kick for Easton after North Caroline had gotten within 28-21.
O'Connor ran for three yards before Caroline called time. O'Connor then ran for eight yards and a first down. North Caroline stuffed Easton's quarterback for no gain on the next play and again burned a timeout. O'Connor then fired an 11-yard dart to Carter Mooney for a first down, then found room around left end for a 22-yard pickup and a first down that clinched the win. O'Connor took a knee on the next two plays to bleed the final minute.
'We got up and then we just kind of let off," O'Connor said. "And we just can't do that against a great team like this. Great first half. Then the second half we slipped off. But we need to play two halves of football."
Griffith agreed but applauded his quarterback.
"He did a phenomenal job," Griffith said of O'Connor. "And he took control at the end of the game to make sure we were able to seal the victory."

title: Queen Anne's takes aim at fifth straight North Bayside title and more
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Queen Anne's takes aim at fifth straight North Bayside title and more

 September 19, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1297
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Queen Anne's County High's girls soccer program has compiled an impressive resume during Mike Kern's 23 seasons as head coach.The Lions have won 14 North Bayside titles and two Bayside Conference championships. They've reached 11 regional finals, winning twice, and have advanced to the state finals once.
But as Queen Anne's has worked through preseason tryouts, scrimmages and into the regular season's early weeks, Kern sees a team that could be among his finest from front to back.
"This might be our most talented team we've ever had in my opinion," said Kern, who has never had a losing record as he enters his 24th season as head coach. "Every single one of them has played travel for years. There's a lot of times we'd get good athletes that played lacrosse or something else, and just played soccer to stay in shape. But this year we have soccer players. And for most of the girls, their first sport is soccer. I think that's the difference from years past."
Despite that talent, which includes all-state first-team selection and returning North Bayside Player of the Year Olivia Ryan, Kern knows there is one main obstacle in his team's path to a fifth consecutive North title — the 2020 COVID-shortened season excluded — and a potential regional title — Kent Island.
Though Queen Anne's shut out the Bucs 3-0 during the regular season last year, it lost 3-2 in double overtime in the Class 2A East Region II title game.
The Lions blanked Kent Island, 1-0, already this season, but have a second date with their county rival Oct. 16 which will likely decided the division crown, and then could have a third encounter come the postseason.
"I'm excited. I really am," Kern said of the season. "We should go far. But we've got to get through Kent Island."
Here's a look at this year's teams.
CAMBRIDGE-SDHead Coach: Sarah Alpaugh.
Who's Where: Goalie: Akizhae Hammond (Jr.); Backs: Monti Jackson (So.); Skyla Ali (So.); Mimi Exume (So.); Sophia Diaz (Fr.); Midfield: Lainey Jones (Sr.); Olivia Fischer (Fr.); Kamryn Bourne (So.); Lilly Moxey (Fr.); Forwards: Laila Insley (Sr.); Madalyn Spicer (Jr.); Jade Bryant (Jr.); Kennedy Bourne (So.).
Outlook: The Vikings graduated their entire defensive unit from a year ago, so one of Alpaugh's focuses will be hoping a young cast of replacements can stick together and gain experience to form a strong foundation for the future.
Jones is a four-year starter that anchors a midfield, which hopes to regain the services of returning starter Kamryn Bourne, who was injured in the season's second game. Alpaugh, who begins her third year, calls Insley a key component, and coupled with the speedy Bryant, could provide a nice one-two punch at the top.
COL. RICHARDSONHead Coach: Beth Carmen.
Who's Where: Goalie: Cloee Welzel (So.); Backs: Olivia McGregor (So.); Kallie Peele (Sr.); Violet Cheezum (Jr.); Adan Alvi (Sr.); Agatha Divjak (Fr.); Lila Schriefer (Jr.); Vanessa Odidika (Sr.); Midfield: Brynne Harper (So.); Doranelli Tomas-Ortiz (So.); Forwards: Ryleigh Hall (So.); Sadie Prettyman (So.).
Outlook: The Colonels got clobbered by Snow Hill a year ago, 8-0. They met the Eagles in this year's opener and scored the game's first goal in an eventual 4-2 loss.
"I have really seen a lot of improvement from last year," said Carmen, who is in her second year as head coach. "I've actually had one of the refs come over to me and say this is one of the best looking Colonel girls soccer teams that he's seen in a long time."
Carmen will rotate players between defense and midfield, and attack and midfield in hopes of finding a consistent combination. After falling to the Eagles in the opener, Colonel bounced back with wins over Cambridge-SD and North Dorchester.
"This is a really great group of kids," Carmen said. "They work well together and they communicate well."
EASTONHead Coach: Ellie Kilmon.
Who's Where: Goalie Zelia Proa (So.); Backs: Dakota Lhotsky (Jr.); Sam Murphy (Sr.); Bella Swann (Sr.); Finley Golden (So.); Stella Petrichenko (So.); Midfield: Addie Schindler (Fr.); Laillah Janes (Sr.); Addie Chandler (Sr.); Anna Quidley (Sr.); Megan Wright (Fr.); Angie Martinez (Jr.); Forward: Miranda Stup (Jr.).
Outlook: Kilmon isn't making any predictions whether the Warriors can battle Queen Anne's and Kent Island for division supremacy.
"I never know until we play," Kilmon said. "It really depends on how the girls show up and play."
Center backs Lhotsky and Murphy look to provide a solid defensive core.
"I'm excited for the year," Kilmon said. "I think we have a good amount of returners and we just have a nice team dynamics that's building so I'm excited to seem them grow together."
KENT COUNTYHead Coach: Ben Joiner.
Who's Where: Goalie: Sophia Cousineau (So.); Backs: Mary Jane Joiner (Jr.); Paige Miller (Sr.); Savanna Reynolds (Jr.); Reese Strong (Fr.); Midfield: Delilah Markovic (Jr.); Jane Cleary (So.); Emy Karlik (Fr.); Bella Hinefelt (So.); Forwards: Zuleika Nava (Jr.); Sabrina Tee (Fr.); Madison Garcia (Fr.); Morgan Kendall (Sr.); Kayla Aguilar (Fr.); Ashlynn Elborn (Fr.); Amelia Plummer (Fr.).
Outlook: A 1995 Kent County graduate, Joiner takes over as head coach and has watched his young team get off to a 2-1 start.
"We really got a lot of positive momentum going with the number of girls that have joined the team this year," said Joiner, who praised the work of assistant Joel Tolbert in helping develop the team. "We're super young. We're really relying on the leadership of our seniors and juniors to elevate the team."
Joiner said an emphasis has been placed on defense in preparation for the 2A schools on the schedule, but has been encouraged by his team's play against 1A rivals.
NORTH CAROLINEHead Coach: Jenna Riordan.
Who's Where: Goalie: Rylee Gowen (Jr.); Amber Biars (Jr.); Backs: Sarah Brown (Sr.); Natalie Newman (Jr.); Izzy Knott (Sr.); Midfield: Emma Hansley (So.); Megan Rogers (Sr.); Madison McNinch (Jr.); Paisley Garland (Jr.); Linda Ridgell (Jr.); Forwards: Irma Sanchez (Jr.); Seanna Rupp (Sr.).
Outlook: The Bulldogs opened the season by defeating Parkside — gaining a measure of revenge on the Rams, who knocked them out of the playoffs in last year's 2A East Region I title game — but then lost by a goal to Easton before getting humbled by Stephen Decatur.
"We have had a rough start to our season so far, but I'm hoping to get a couple wins under our belts the next two weeks," Riordan said. "That ought to help our record."
Riordan also hopes a few wins help her team's confidence as it transitions from a 4-4-2 scheme to a 3-5-2 alignment.
"We're still adjusting and learning our positions," said Riordan, who begins her sixth season. "I've always said that we play up to the teams that are above us, so I do think we'll play (Queen Anne's and Kent Island) a really good game."
QUEEN ANNE'SHead Coach: Mike Kern.
Who's Where: Goalie: Bea Holthaus (So.); Backs: Shannon Rath (Jr.); Hayden Legg (Sr.); Finley Patchett (So.); Kathryn Baer (Sr.); Abby Robinson (So.); Midfield: Chloe Sharp (Sr.); Olivia Ryan (Sr.); Morgan Scott (Sr.); Kara Ringold (Jr.); Forwards: Madi Horney (So.); Riley Klepper (Sr.); Taylor Napier (So.).
Outlook: The most notable graduation loss for the Lions was back Elizabeth Oldfield. But this could be one of the best defensive units Kern and longtime assistant Jeff Anthony have ever had in Centreville.
Kern also noted Scott and Ringold may be the two best outside midfielders Queen Anne's has had since the days of former standout Kesley Dean. Add to the mix Ryan, the all-state pick and the Lions' leading scorer from last year is back, along with a group of nine sophomores, several of which played together on a travel team coached by Kern.
Despite all that, Kent Island remains the primary hurdle in the North, while James M. Bennett or Stephen Decatur — which defeated the Lions in overtime to open the season — are angling toward the South Bayside crown and a possible conference championship showdown.

title: Suggs among Hall nominees
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Suggs among Hall nominees

 September 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 848
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Two-time Super Bowl MVP Eli Manning, former Defensive Players of the Year Luke Kuechly and Terrell Suggs, and postseason kicking hero Adam Vinatieri are among the players nominated for the 2025 Pro Football Hall of Fame class in their first year of eligibility.The Hall announced 167 modern era candidates for the class on Wednesday that included 16 players who became eligible this year, including two-time All-Pro guard Marshal Yanda.
A screening committee will reduce the list of nominees to 50 players next month. Then the full 50-person selection committee will cut the list down to 25 semifinalists and then 15 finalists for the annual meeting before the Super Bowl that will produce the new class. Players must get 80% of votes to get in with between three and five players getting in as modern era candidates.
There will also be three senior candidates, grouped with one coach and contributor with at least one and no more than three of those finalists getting in based on voting.
The other first-year candidates are offensive linemen Travis Frederick, Ryan Kalil and Joe Staley; running backs Darren Sproles and Marshawn Lynch; receiver Demaryius Thomas; tight ends Vernon Davis and Delanie Walker; and defensive backs Antoine Bethea, Aqib Talib and Earl Thomas.
There are also 10 players back under consideration who were finalists a year ago with tight end Antonio Gates, receivers Torry Holt and Reggie Wayne; offensive linemen Willie Anderson and Jahri Evans; defensive backs Darren Woodson, Eric Allen and Rodney Harrison; defensive lineman Jared Allen; and running back Fred Taylor back on the list.
Manning will look to follow his brother Peyton into the Hall following a standout career with the New York Giants. Manning was picked first overall in the 2004 draft and spent his entire career in New York. He led the Giants to an upset win over the undefeated New England Patriots in the Super Bowl following the 2007 season, throwing a game-winning TD pass to Plaxico Burress in the final minute.
He led another late TD drive to upset Tom Brady and the Patriots four years later. Manning is one of 13 QBs to win multiple Super Bowls with eight of the nine who are eligible for the Hall getting inducted.
Only Jim Plunkett has not been inducted along with more recent players such as Brady, Ben Roethlisberger and Patrick Mahomes, who aren't eligible.
Manning was a four-time Pro Bowler but never made All-Pro or led the league in a major statistical category in a season but finished his career with 57,023 yards passing and 366 TDs.
His best moments were in those two postseason runs. Manning joined Brady (five), Mahomes (three), Joe Montana (three), Bart Starr (two) and Terry Bradshaw (two) as the only multiple winners of Super Bowl MVP awards.
Kuechly and Suggs were among the top defensive players of their era with Kuechly selected as the top defensive player in 2013 and Suggs in 2011.
Kuechly's career was brief but impactful. The first-round pick by Carolina in 2012 was an All-Pro five times in his eight-year career with seven Pro Bowl nods and a Defensive Rookie of the Year award.
Over his eight-year career, Kuechly led all linebackers in the NFL in tackles (1,090), takeaways (26), interceptions (18) and passes defensed (66).
Suggs was one of the top pass rushers in the league over his 17-year career, with his 139 sacks ranking eighth best since they became an official stat in 1982.
Suggs had seven double-digit sack seasons in his 16 seasons with Baltimore, including 14 in 2011 when he was selected as the top defensive player in the league and led the NFL with seven forced fumbles.
He won Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2003 and helped the Ravens win the Super Bowl in the 2012 season. He finished his career in Kansas City where he helped the Chiefs win the Super Bowl in the 2019 season.
Vinatieri was one of the most clutch kickers in NFL history, making the game-winning field goals in the first two Super Bowl titles during New England's dynasty.
He helped launch the run with one of the game's greatest kicks — a 45-yarder in the snow to force overtime in the "Tuck Rule" game against the Raiders in the 2001 divisional round. He made the game-winning kick in OT to win that game and then hit a 48-yarder on the final play of a 20-17 win in the Super Bowl against the Rams.
He then made a 41-yarder two years later to give the Patriots a 32-29 win in the Super Bowl against Carolina. Vinatieri also won Super Bowls in 2004 with New England and in the 2006 season with Indianapolis.
Vinatieri is the NFL's all-time leader in points (2,673) and made field goals (599) over a 24-year career with New England and Indianapolis. He also leads all players with 56 field goals and 238 points in the postseason.
Yanda was a member of the 2010s all-decade team as a key of Baltimore's success. He also was selected second-team All-Pro five times and made the Pro Bowl in eight of his final seasons, missing in 2017 when he played only two games of an injury.

author: Bill Haufe
content:
Defending North Bayside champion Queen Anne’s County among teams trying to fill graduation holes in an attempt for another deep playoff

 September 17, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1620
 Words 

 Read News Document

 North Bayside boys soccer coaches have been busy this preseason — and during the early weeks of the regular season — mending holes in their lineups.Defending division champion Queen Anne's County High, which went 13-3-1 and reached the Class 2A state semifinals a year ago, graduated eight, including six starters.
"The guys that we lost were huge parts," Lions head coach Wade Hosler said.
North Caroline head coach John Austin can sympathize after graduating seven, including 2023 North Bayside Player of the Year Logan Harned.
"I feel as a conference we lost a lot of really good players," Austin said. "Last year's conference was very, very senior heavy."
A handful of those graduates are now playing in the collegiate ranks, with North Caroline's Harned at Neumann (Pa.) University and goalie Gavin O'Brien at Frostburg State, while Queen Anne's has Billy Schindler at Washington College.
The Class 1A ranks also felt graduation's sting. North Dorchester lost 10, while Cambridge-South Dorchester first-year head coach Josh Dohoney is trying to patch holes created by almost half of dozen losses.
In addition to the Vikings, Easton welcomes former standout Avery Brice as its new head coach, while Kent County begins the Dennis Hickman era.
Queen Anne's shared the conference title with James M. Bennett in 2021, but the last North team to win the Bayside championship outright was Kent Island in 2016, when the Bucs topped Stephen Decatur in penalty kicks. The Bucs and Lions look to be on another collision course to decide the North when they meet in Stevensville on Oct. 18, though North Caroline and Easton figure to also be atop the division ranks.
The South's dominance of the conference crown could be extended this year, as Bennett, which lost to eventual Class 3A state champion South River in last year's postseason, returns the bulk of its team from a season ago.
Here's a look at this year's North Bayside teams.
CAMBRIDGE-SD
Head Coach: Josh Dohoney.
Who's Where: Goalie: Nate Huber (Sr.); Backs: Osvaldo Hernandez (Jr.); Evan Kozak (Sr.); Colton Phillips (So.); Gibby Robinson (So.); Midfield: Lucas Harper (So.); Gavin Weber (So.); Ryan Harris (Sr.); Forwards: Will Banks (Jr.); Wyatt Abbott (So.); Marcos Hernandez (Fr.).
Outlook: After one year as an assistant, Dohoney begins his first head coaching job in soccer knowing he'll need to be patient.
"We're very young. Very much a rebuilding squad," said Dohoney, who played at Delmar, Del.
The Vikings graduated more than half a dozen from last year, including center midfielder Randall Johnson. The midfield looks technically sound, but with five sophomores and one freshman starting, Dohoney hopes this will be a season of growth.
COL. RICHARDSON
Head Coach: Dillon Shaheen.
Who's Where: Goalie: Cohen Carels (Sr.); Backs: Cameron Todd (Sr.); Jacklin Novembre (Jr.); Jackson Jean Jr. (Jr.); Caleb Rouser (So.); Midfield: John Beaven (So.); Jack Walls (Jr.); Preston Rickwood (Sr.); Ludver Vasquez (Jr.); Aydan Downie (Sr.); Forwards: Morgan Demir (Sr.); Angel Castro-Rios (Sr.); Skyler Endzel (Fr.); Brody Omohundro (Fr.).
Outlook: Shaheen begins his third year as head coach with his most experienced team he's had. That has translated into victories over Pocomoke and North Dorchester for starters.
"It's been pretty good so far," said Shaheen, who lost three seniors from last year. "Obviously we have a lot of seniors and juniors, and most have been playing at the varsity level for three or four years. I'm pretty confident in our squad this year."
EASTON
Head Coach: Avery Brice.
Who's Where: Goalie: Sam Hutchison (Jr.); Backs: Mario Medina (Sr.); Felix Valentine (Jr.); Brody Byrnes (Sr.); Kai Ferraris (Jr.); Landon Chaney (Sr.); Midfield: Clay Nagle (Sr.); Luke Stanco (Jr.); CJ Chaconas (Sr.); Blake Royer (So.); Ale Monroy (So.); Dominic Stanco (Sr.); Otto Perez-Arreaga (Fr.); Logan Sundt (Jr.); Liam Edgell (Sr.); Forwards: Kyle Ensminger (Jr.); Rodi Fresco Rubio (Jr.).
Outlook: Brice was a center midfielder on Easton's last two teams to win Bayside titles (2013, '14) and helped the Warriors reach the 2A state final in '14 before continuing his playing career at Wesley (Del.) College.
Now, he steps into his first head coaching job.
"Things are shaping up nicely," Brice said. "Could things be better? Yes. That's kind of one thing that we just hope to do every day in the season; just be better than the day before."
While the Warriors have been receptive to their new coach's ideas and style, Brice stressed they must strive for consistency.
"The mindset is you can be really good, but every game you've got to bring it," Brice said.
KENT COUNTY
Head Coach: Dennis Hickman.
Who's Where: Goalie: Leyder Cruz (Sr.); Backs: Noah Iacona (Jr.); Jayden Miller (So.); Stewart Hickman (Jr.); Bryce Jacobs (So.); Midfield: Nick Stead (Sr.); Colbyn Lopez (Jr.); Ethan Clark (Sr.); Forwards: Gabe Parr (So.); Dylan Peralta (Fr.); Sebastian Cousineau (So.).
Outlook: A 1993 graduate of Kent County, Hickman, who played soccer, baseball and wrestled for the Trojans, takes over as head coach after spending the last two years as an assistant.
In an attempt to build a program, Hickman has already achieved one goal in fielding a junior varsity for the first time since 2019.
"We think by having a jayvee, getting them out there on practice, getting them those reps and having some game-time situations and play, that we're only going to be able to build on that moving forward," Hickman said. "It's just the best thing for the program."
That coupled with a varsity roster that includes nine juniors and nine sophomores, could bode well for the future.
As for this year's team, there isn't a lot of experience, though Stewart Hickman has plenty of travel ball experience, as has recruited players over the summer to come out for the team.
KENT ISLAND
Head Coach: Lin Outten.
Who's Where: Goalie: Quinn Burns (Fr.); Backs: Davis Miller (Sr.); Noah Scopp (Sr.); Gavin Neboshynsky (Sr.); Mark Rees (Sr.); Spencer Chappell (Jr.); Elijah James (So.); Midfield: Simon Vujinovic (Sr.); Brendan Thomas (Jr.); Cooper Liebel (So.); Landon Pecor (Jr.); Forwards: AJ Miller (Jr.); Eric Hoffman (Sr.); Ethan Schriver (Sr.); Robert Simkins (Jr.).
Outlook: The Bucs have a lot of experience moving from the midfield into the attack, but are not as experienced in the back. Though seniors Davis Miller, Scopp and Rees return, Outten hopes shifting Neboshynsky and Chappell from midfield to the back bolsters his defense.
AJ Miller netted 10 goals a year ago, and Outten thinks that number will go up, especially with the return of Hoffman, who missed the bulk of last year with an early season injury.
"But really what makes the engine go is the three guys in the middle — Thomas, Vujinovic and Liebel," Outten said.
NORTH CAROLINE
Head Coach: John Austin.
Who's Where: Goalie: Mason Shilling (Jr.); Backs: Lewis Higgs (Jr.); Brayden Boarts (Sr.); Jimmy Cohoon (Jr.); Midfield: Ayden Russell (Jr.); Tyler Gutierrez (Jr.); Omar Marroquin (Sr.); Jonnathan Luna Feliciano (Jr.); Diego Castro (So.); Landyn Harned (So.); Kyle Reed (Jr.); Forwards: Heath Frantum (Jr.); Issac Bautista (Jr.); Luke Raga (So.).
Outlook: The Bulldogs graduated seven from a year ago, including Harned, O'Brien, and also lost leading scorer Kevin Godinez.
Austin thinks his team will be more defensive-minded this season. The defense is led by Shilling, who Austin thinks has college potential. Shilling and company figure to be tested early, as the Bulldogs open with defending conference champion James M. Bennett, Class 2A state semifinalist Queen Anne's, and perennial conference heavyweight Stephen Decatur.
"We have a lot of holes to fill," Austin said. "I think we are where we need to be right now. But the goal is can we just keep getting better as the year goes on, and then when October rolls around, play our best soccer?"
NORTH DORCHESTER
Head Coach: Gabe Guzman.
Who's Where: Goalie: Jayden Coleman (Jr.); Backs: Chris Sanchez (Jr.); Tahjere Pritchett (Jr.); Alex Fonseca-Gonzalez (So.); Martin Chirino Fernandez (Jr.); Midfield: Christian Chase (Jr.); Peyton Bleyer (So.); Daniel Mejia (Sr.); Kegan Henry (Jr.); Forwards: Volcy Nerat (Fr.); Dagoberto Chirino Fernandez.
Outlook: The Eagles graduated 10, including seven starters. Among Guzman's top priorities is getting his freshman to buy into his system and get acclimated to the high school varsity format.
"We're working on trust," Guzman said.
QUEEN ANNE'S
Head Coach: Wade Hosler.
Who's Where: Goalie: Ethan Keppler (Sr.); Backs: Christian Coppage (Sr.); Conner Cheezum (Sr.); Hayden Albright (Sr.); Brody Nordvik (Jr.); Midfield: James Rath (Jr.); Gage Jordan (Sr.); Nathan Kostka (Jr.); Mason Albright (Sr.); Boden Blodgett (So.); Josiah Hegarty (So.); Forwards: Ryan Lee (Sr.).
Outlook: "The preseason seemed awfully short this year, and our chemistry wasn't quite where I'd like it this time of year," Hosler said. "But I think it's coming, so I'm optimistic that we can do good things. We've had good moments and we've had mistakes. But I like the direction we're heading in."
Hosler has also liked his team's 3-0-1 start, which included Monday's 3-0 shutout of North Caroline.
Despite its big graduation losses, the Lions do have a solid core of returners. Outside backs Coppage and Cheezum return along with Keppler in goal. Jordan is back in the midfield while Lee returns at striker.
"We have some big pieces, but we still have some big holes to fill," said Hosler, who graduation losses included Schindler, center back William Nagle and leading scorer Nick Esper. "If we can have some guys step up I think we'll be OK."
ST. MICHAELS
Head Coach: Pat Hambleton.
Who's Where: Goalie: Will Sherwood (Sr.); Backs: Tyler Murphy (Jr.); Jack Brennan (Sr.); Sherwin Mendez (Sr.); Brennan Dean (Jr.); Midfield: Ethan Royer (Jr.); Gavin Bieber (Fr.); Johnny Mautz (Jr.); Abel Delgaudio (So.); Forwards: Connor Wheeler (Jr.); Miles Fox (Jr.); Haven Haddaway (Sr.).
Outlook: Having Sherwood — first-team all-North Bayside goalie the past two years — and an experienced returning defensive unit should make the Saints plenty tough.
While that provides Hambleton comfort, he also liked what he has seen on the offensive end.
"Finally creative," Hambleton said of his attack. "We're going to be an enjoyment to watch. Still have an older group to support our creative offensive style. I have players to make it a pretty game finally. And they get it."

title: Vikings rush past Knights

content:
Vikings rush past Knights

 September 13, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 603
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CAMBRIDGE — Rob Burnham is among the football coaching crowd who stresses the importance of the second half's first possession.The last possession of the first half proved pretty important as well for Burnham's Cambridge-South Dorchester High team Friday night.
Sterling Perkins hauled in a 14-yard touchdown pass just before the end of the first half, then scored on a 3-yard run to open the second half, to help give the Vikings separation on the way to a 49-21 victory over Century.
"I tell our kids all the time when we get in the locker room that the first possession of the second half is the biggest possession of the game," said Cambridge-SD's first-year head coach after his team improved to 2-0. "And I believe that. You open the game and score, that's OK because there's a lot of ballgame left. But when you open the second half (and score). ... And I thought it was big that we scored right before halftime and then we got the possession again. So that gives us the two-score lead. That's huge. Huge."
After a scoreless first quarter, Cambridge-SD senior quarterback Anthony Hughes scored on runs of 20 and 55 yards to help stake the Vikings to a 14-0 lead with 9 minutes, 18 seconds left in the second quarter. Collin Bair drilled both point-after kicks.
The Knights (0-2) rallied though. Jonathan Ferguson scored on a 1-yard run up the middle, but the point-after boot sailed wide left, leaving Century trailing 14-6.
Cambridge-SD drove from its 40 to the Knights' 20, where Dylan Vroom intercepted Vikings backup quarterback Nathan Twilley and raced 80 yards up the sideline for a touchdown. Ferguson's two-point conversion run tied the game at 14-all with 3:02 left before halftime.
The Vikings came right back, as Hughes lofted a pass toward the end zone that Perkins made a nice over-the-shoulder grab on for a 14-yard touchdown and a 20-14 lead with 7.6 remaining in the first half. Cambridge-SD bobbled the snap from center on the extra-point attempt, and settled for a six-point lead entering the break.
The Vikings needed just three plays to expand that lead on the first possession of the second half. Perkins ran for gains of 17 and 27 yards before he took a handoff and made a quick juke into the end zone for a 3-yard touchdown. Hughes hit Antonio Blueford with a two-point conversion pass for a 28-14 lead just 42 seconds into the third.
On its next possession, Century tried to convert a fourth-and-four from its own 31. But quarterback Jacob Dexter fired incomplete, turning the ball over to the Vikings. On the next play, William Jackson swept right and blazed into the end zone for a 31-yard touchdown. Bair added the PAT for a 35-14 lead with 9:08 to go in the third.
Century pulled within 35-21 with 4:50 left in the third, as Ferguson bulled his way into the end zone from 2 yards out, then booted the point-after.
The Knights though could not stop Cambridge-SD's big plays.
On its ensuing possession, Hughes broke free for his third touchdown run, this one covering 42 yards for a 41-21 cushion with 3:34 left in the third.
Cambridge-SD again stopped the Knights on fourth down, but penalties from the Vikings back to their own 6-yard line. It didn't matter, as Perkins took a handoff, found a seam up the middle, and bolted 94 yards for a touchdown. Blueford made a diving grab on Hughes' two-point pass for a 49-21 lead.
"We're going to get better," Burnham said. "The things we struggled with today we'll make improvements on. We have to be better than we were tonight that's for sure."

title: Webb's four goals pace Sabres in shutout of ESIAC newcomer Tome School
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Webb's four goals pace Sabres in shutout of ESIAC newcomer Tome School

 September 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 650
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — It could have easily been deemed a reenactment of David and Goliath."It's the equivalent of my son's rec team going up against a college team," Tome School head field hockey coach Jenn Waldron said after her team's visit to Saints Peter and Paul High.
Of course don't expect Sabres head coach Debbie McQuaid to ever call her team Goliath. The defending Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference champions? Yes. Goliath? No.
Yet McQuaid's bunch looked very much the part Wednesday, as Angie Webb scored four goals to lead seven different scorers during a 13-0 victory over the the Titans.
"I told one of the players, she's in my Spanish One class, I'm like, 'You're in Spanish One. Could you walk into Spanish Four and hold your own?'" said Waldron, whose team is in the ESIAC for the first time. 'Does it mean you're not as smart? No. You're just not there yet.' So they are a solid team. They've got the resources. They got the coaching staff. That's what showed on the field."
And it didn't take the Sabres (2-1 overall, 1-0 ESIAC) long to show their stuff.
The contest was all of 46 seconds old, when Webb converted a Caroline Corson feed into the game's first goal. Tome (1-2) and first-year goalie Steph Cingle held Sts. Peter & Paul scoreless for a stretch despite the Sabres racking up a slew of early penalty-corner opportunities.
But with just under 7 minutes left in the first quarter, Webb scored to spark a four-goal surge. Kate Sweeney (two goals) scored off a dish from Jules Stepp (two goals, two assists) with less than 5 minutes remaining in the opening quarter. Webb added her third goal with 2 minutes to go before Kat Murphy netted the first of her two goals for a 5-0 lead heading into the second quarter.
"I think we're jelling more than we did the first (scrimmage) because we played Stephen Decatur and we lost," Stepp said. "But after that we built together as a team. We practiced hard and we're jelling now. We're looking for our back passes. We're looking up for each other. And we're looking for our open teammates."
Claire Bieber, who transferred in from St. Michaels this season, touched on another Sabres' staple — speed.
"We have a very fast team," Bieber said. "We have a lot of speed, and we've been working on quick release and transfers."
The Sabres stretched the lead to 9-0 at halftime as Sweeney, Kiera Crossed, Webb and Corson each scored during a second quarter that was played with a running clock.
Bieber scored the lone goal of the third, then watched Stepp score twice and Murphy once in the fourth quarter.
"We are learning from what we are missing," Stepp said in reference to a graduated crowd that included Gennie Webb, Morgan Quade and Emmary Sweeney from last year's 14-2 team. "And we're trying to fill that void together and add more people in, and work together as a team."
McQuaid agreed, saying since preseason she has liked the influx of youth to this year's team.
"The younger kids' energy and enthusiasm, and how quickly they're picking up our system, has been very good," McQuaid said. "Bridget Gilman and Tara Foley in the back, they got good minutes and did what they were supposed to do; passed and share the ball. They don't always get into the tighter games, but today they were ready.
"Tried to play everybody," McQuaid added. "Had seven different people score. So that was good."
Corson finished with two assists and CC O'Connor had one assist. Sts. Peter & Paul finished with 13 corners to Tome's four.
KENT ISLAND 4, WASHINGTON 0
PRINCESS ANNE — Willow Yost scored a pair of goals and Ellie Burnside totaled three assists the lead the Buccaneers.
Sydney Riska and Lyla Bailey each had one goal for Kent Island (1-0) and Sadie Latchaw had an assist. Brynja Petursson finished with four saves. The Bucs had six corners.

title: Warriors use stops from Bowen, and goals from Knox, Motovidlak and Quicke in shootout to reach state final four
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors use stops from Bowen, and goals from Knox, Motovidlak and Quicke in shootout to reach state final four

 October 31, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 647
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Easton High head field hockey coach Kim Neff started coaching Taylor Bowen when she was five."I always knew she had the potential," Neff said of Bowen. "She's so athletic. And she's got such a high IQ of the game, that I knew she would be a good goalie. And I used to beg her all the time, 'When you get to high school, will you be my goalie?' And finally in seventh grade she turned to me at a rec game and said, 'I'm going to be your goalie in high school.' And I was like, 'Awesome.'"
That described Bowen's performance beautifully Thursday afternoon. Easton's freshman goalie stopped three of the four Hereford players she faced in the 1v1 shootout, and watched teammates Addie Knox, Myka Motovidlak and Ryann Quicke each score goals, propelling the Warriors to a 1-0 victory over the fifth-seeded Bulls in a Class 2A state quarterfinal.
Fourth-seeded Easton (12-3) advances to next Wednesday's 2A state semifinals, where it will meet top-seeded Manchester Valley (15-0) at Glen Burnie High School at a time yet to be determined.
"I don't have enough words to say about her," Neff said of Bowen. "I have believed in her from Day 1. And she believes in herself. She has confidence. And her skills are just growing and growing. She is determined to get better and better, and she has this year. She's just phenomenal."
On an unseasonably warm Halloween day that took a toll on several players, the Warriors and Bulls (11-4) were scoreless after 60 minutes of regulation and two 10-minute overtimes, pushing the duel into a shootout.
Hereford's Gracie Berquist went first in the shootout, but with Bowen moving toward her, fired a shot wide.
Knox went first for Easton, stepped to the right of Bulls goalie Julia Pfitzinger, and sent a shot into the far left corner for a 1-0 Warriors lead.
Caitlin Meeker beat Bowen on Hereford's second attempt to tie the shootout at 1-all. Motovidlak nudged Easton back in front, dodging left and scoring to make it 2-1.
Kayla Owings pushed the ball to the left post on the Bulls' third attempt, but was denied by a diving Bowen.
"Me and my other goalie Alli (Newnam) have trained all season for the shootouts," Bowen said. "And we both hate diving. So we just want to say thank you to (goalie) coach Claire (Spurry), who has been pushing us all season to dive and it worked out perfect. Couldn't ask for a better time."
Quicke was Easton's next shooter.
"I really was down on myself throughout the whole game," Quicke said. "I was getting really frustrated. And my team had told me that this is our only chance right here. 'Why not us?'"
Pfitzinger knocked the ball away from Quicke initially. But the sophomore quickly regained possession and drove the ball into the back of the goal for a 3-1 Easton edge.
"I got a little scared when she cleared it," Quicke said. "But I turned around, and I shot and hoped for it to go in."
Bowen then made a leg save on a shot by Hereford's last hope, Lauren Mathews, then watched the rebound roll out of bounds.
"That was very exciting," Bowen said of her final stop. "I was off my angle, but it all works out. So exciting. Final four."
But before the Warriors launched into a full-blown celebration, they waited for game officials to confirm the game was complete, with Hereford having shot four times and with no chance to tie. Once Easton players got the official stamp on their victory, they stampeded toward their goalie. Leading the charge was Motovidlak, who caught and embraced Bowen in midair. Bowen and Motovidlak were soon taken to ground by an avalanche of teammates.
"Definitely wasn't our best game," Neff said. "I was a little frustrated with them in the first couple quarters. We just weren't playing as a team. But somehow they pulled it off."

title: Warriors beat clock, Seahawks
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors beat clock, Seahawks

 October 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 675
 Words 

 Read News Document

 It's won on a penalty stroke in overtime.It's also won on penalty corners — once in overtime, once in double OT.
Tuesday evening, Easton High's field hockey team found yet another way to win — and fray their coaches nerves — scoring just before the clock ran dry.
Addie Knox scored on a corner with 11 seconds remaining in regulation, boosting the Warriors to a 2-1 victory over top-seeded Stephen Decatur in the Class 2A East Region II championship in Berlin.
Easton (11-3), which has won seven straight, is seeded fourth in the Class 2A state tournament and will host fifth-seeded Hereford (11-3) on Thursday at 3 p.m. in a quarterfinal match.
"They never give up," Easton head coach Kim Neff said of her team during a phone interview Wednesday. "They never come off the field thinking like, 'We're done.'"
Decatur (11-4) took a 1-0 lead in the second quarter on Jill Burton's goal, and carried that lead into halftime. But the Warriors didn't panic.
"I feel like this is our MO really," Neff said. "We're used to coming from behind. We don't stress too much about it. We knew we had plenty of time to get back in that game. And I told them, 'Just go put a goal in right now and score and tie it up.' And sure enough they went and tied it up."
Less than 2 minutes into the second half, Easton's Myka Motovidlak smacked a drive toward the goal that was knocked into the cage by Georgia Spies for a 1-1 tie.
"We have faced a lot of challenges this season," Neff said. "Not a lot of teams have. Some teams it comes a little easier to win. I feel running into the playoffs that's an advantage for us. We know we can come from behind. We know we can go to double overtime and win. We've experienced that. I feel like that's an advantage for us."
Play evened out through the rest of the third quarter. The Seahawks then got a string of corners in the fourth quarter, but could not get anything else past Easton's defense of Bis Johnson, Kadence McGuckin, Lea Boutte and freshman goalie Taylor Bowen (12 saves).
"Our goalie saved the day," Neff said of Bowen, whose only experience in goal prior to this season was in rec league play. "Taylor just did a phenomenal job. She's so coachable and she sees the field. And she's so athletic. She just impressed all of us."
Easton survived Decatur's flurry of corners and worked the ball back into the Seahawks end with about 2 minutes remaining. It was then that Neff turned to assistant Katie Spies and said they needed to start thinking about who they were going to put on the field for the first overtime period.
But with a little under a minute to play, Easton's Ryan Quicke drew a foul, setting up a corner.
"We got in a little huddle right before we got the corner and Stella (Kabler) was like, 'This is it guys,'" Knox said. "Then I looked up at the scoreboard and it said 50 seconds left. And when (Neff) called that Liv (Olivia Orrell) was taking the direct shot, I was like, 'This is it.' Because Liv always gets it in there."
Knox inserted the ball off the end line, then moved to the left post. Orrell sent a drive that was stopped by Decatur's goalie. But the ball bounced upward toward Knox, who batted the ball into the cage for a 2-1 Warriors lead.
"It was great," Knox said. "Everybody just jumped up. I couldn't even breath."
But while Easton's players were celebrating, Neff was pleading.
"Everybody was losing their mind except me who was saying, 'We still have 11 seconds left,'" Neff said. "'Do not let them go down and get in the circle.'"
Decatur rushed downfield and got close to the circle before Johnson swept the ball out of bounds, leaving the Seahawks not enough time to retrieve the ball and mount one last threat.
"They believe in themselves and they believe in their teammates," Neff said. "It's really an awesome group of girls."

title: One is enough for Queen Anne's
author: Bill Haufe
content:
One is enough for Queen Anne's

 October 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 711
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Neither one needed a lesson on the importance of scoring first."The first team that scores is more likely to win than the second," Kent Island High head field hockey coach Laura Harding said.
"Getting that early goal, it sets the tone," Queen Anne's County head coach Shana Corder said. "And I knew going into this game, I knew both teams were going to come out to win it in regulation."
Queen Anne's and Kent Island played to a scoreless, double-overtime tie Oct. 19 before each team scored twice in a shootout in their regular-season finale.
It didn't take that long Tuesday afternoon.
Haley Cole's goal on a corner just 7 minutes in proved enough, as the Lions blanked Kent Island, 1-0, for their second straight Class 2A East Region I championship.
Queen Anne's (12-1-1) is seeded third in the 2A state tournament and will host No. 6 seed Centenniel (11-3) on Thursday at 4 p.m. in a quarterfinal.
"We're successful on our corners because our defense is so amazing," said Corder, whose team has won back-to-back Bayside Conference and regional titles for the first time in the program's history. "And it pays off for us. And all you need is one to go in. And honestly going forward, this is how the state tournament's going to go. One goal is going to get it."
One goal was all that was needed on this beautiful autumn afternoon.
Queen Anne's earned two corners in the game's first 5 minutes, then got a third with 7:20 remaining in the first quarter. Jordan Bilbo sent an entry pass to Ellee McLean, who quickly sent the ball back Bilbo. Positioned to the right of the goal, Bilbo centered a pass to an unmarked Cole about five yards from the cage. Cole didn't hesitate, quickly sweeping shot under the lunge of Bucs goalie Brynja Petursson and into the left side of the cage for a 1-0 lead.
"We've been working really hard on corner execution, and every practice it's been getting better and better," Cole said. "And I got the perfect pass from Jordan and happened to be the one. It was really a team effort. We were all in there to get it done and earn the corner. I just happened to be the one lucky to tap it in."
That was plenty for Queen Anne's defense.
Since yielding a goal to Crisfield on Oct. 7, the Lions haven't surrendered a goal over their last six games — not counting the 1 vs. 1 against the Bucs in the regular-season finale. Corder again played Cassidy Alexander (four saves) and Caroline Kimball (two saves) two quarters each Tuesday. And even though Sydnie Harris — one of the new mainstays on a rebuilt defense — was not 100%, she played tough minutes along with linemates Sydnee Carr and Mel Gill. Corder dropped forward Aly Edwards back on defense when Harris needed a breather.
"I just knew if we scored first I knew we could do it because my defense is amazing, and they're peaking," Corder said of a unit that has now logged 10 shutouts this season. "They are peaking right now. They've done well all season.
"I had to put one of my forwards back to defense," Corder said of Edwards. "But the kids listen to what we tell them in practice and they know everybody's role. So we're just able to be successful even being sick. I'm super proud of the girls."
Harding was also proud of her defense, which limited an opponent to one goal or less for the 11th time this season. Petursson made seven saves, including a stop McLean's penalty stroke with 7:45 left in the second quarter, and made another save when the Bucs were down a man for 2 minutes in the third quarter.
"We made the save and we battled back on all the corners down here in the first half," said Harding, whose team stopped Queen Anne's on 10 of its 11 corners.
Kent Island (9-4-1) almost pulled even with 2:50 remaining, when a drive in the circle missed connecting with Ellie Burnside at the post.
"They have a good defense," Harding said of Queen Anne's. "And they've got a great goalie. It's going to be a big battle again next year, too. I think we'll be right back here again next year."

title: Lions serve up 3rd straight title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions serve up 3rd straight title

 October 29, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 630
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SALISBURY — Queen Anne's County High's volleyball team spent time during the first week of practice in August getting to know new head coach Jamie Leventry.But it was on the first day of practice that Leventry defined the importance of serving.
"We talked about it starting Day 1," Leventry said. "'We're going to serve tough. It's what we're going to do.'"
The Lions proved extremely tough from the serving line Monday night, as Emerson Stewart reeled off the team's longest service run of the season during a dominating 25-10, 25-9, 25-5 victory over Parkside that gave Queen Anne's its third consecutive Bayside Conference championship.
"There's a reason why their record is what it is," Parkside head coach Roy Geiser said after the Lions improved to 15-0. "Great serving team. Great passing team. And frankly we didn't play our best game. But they put a lot of pressure on us and we weren't prepared."
The Rams (14-4) got an idea of things to come in Game 1, when Sydney Pinder (eight kills) served four straight points, turning a 5-4 Lions lead into a 9-4 edge.
"I feel it gives us such an advantage and I think it helps build up our team's momentum," Pinder said of her team's service game. "It just keeps us up as a team."
Queen Anne's maintained that five-point edge before Kaisa Hickson started a five-point serving spree with one of the Lions' 22 aces, extending the lead to 19-9.
Parkside put down a winner to stop that run before Bianca Baker (team-high 13 kills) closed the first game with a six-point roll from the line to cap Game 1.
"It's just a matter of putting a lot of pressure on the other team, and kind of getting them out of system," Leventry said. "Whenever we're back there putting good, tough serves on them and they're struggling to pass those, then that puts us in a really good spot."
Jensen Nutley put the Lions in a really good spot, when she strung together eight service points for an 8-0 Queen Anne's lead to start Game 2.
"I think that was really important because when you're up by so much, I feel like you don't think about making mistakes so much," Nutley said. "When you're in a neck-to-neck game, like when we play a team like Kent Island, where it's serve and serve back and forth, that takes a lot of effort from us not to make mistakes and think about it a lot. When we're up by that much I feel like it lets us loose and play our game."
A Baker kill and three consecutive service points from Stewart pushed the Lions' lead to 11 at 12-1. Queen Anne's lead remained around 11 points until 20-9, when Stewart again stepped to the line and wedged two more aces into a game-sealing, five-point run.
"Climbing back on a team like that you just can't do," Geiser said. "We got to play at our very best and that's not what we did tonight."
Parkside's Brylie Geiser served to open Game 3, but Baker unloaded another kill for a 1-0 Lions lead. Stewart moved back to the service line and wouldn't leave until Queen Anne's lead was at 19-0.
"My main goal is to keep it in; keep a nice, clean flow at serve," said Stewart, whose previous best service run was 13. "I think it's definitely intimidating when there's a long serving streak, especially with a big game on the line."
Queen Anne's completed its 12th sweep of the season with a kill from Nutley and a Marylee Kline serve that was not returned.
"Feels great," Leventry said. "It's been a fun season so far. And like I said, we're not done yet. A state championship is our goal."
It was the first time Queen Anne's has won three straight conference titles in volleyball.

title: Rival clashes feature various degrees of confidence
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Rival clashes feature various degrees of confidence

 October 29, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 784
 Words 

 Read News Document

 They each come into rivalry week with varying degrees of confidence.After getting shutout by defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur on Oct. 11, Kent Island High's football team rides a two-game win streak into Friday's annual clash with county rival Queen Anne's.
The Lions come into Friday having won five of six, their latest, a 21-20 victory over Parkside eight days after losing a one-point heartbreaker to Easton.
Streaking Colonel Richardson readies for its annual duel with North Caroline having outscored its last four opponents, 203-20.
And though they are still searching for their first win of the season, the Bulldogs fell just two points shy of Kent Island but have senior star Zymear Smith back and running.
"I can see some progress that we've made," said Heath Wilkins, who became North Caroline's head coach just four weeks ago. "I wish I had the team for more time, but I don't, so this is what we've got."
For the second time in Wilkins' three games as head coach, the Bulldogs (0-8) held a halftime lead last Friday. Corey Bunce's 4-yard touchdown run and Caden Deavers' two-point conversion run gave North Caroline an 8-0 lead on Kent Island, which had a field-goal attempt blocked before the half.
But the Bucs (5-3) rebounded in the second half, as Nathan Green scored on runs of 14 and 38 yards to help push Kent Island to a 16-8 lead.
Caroline pulled within 16-14, when Bunce connected with tight end Declan Egan for a short touchdown pass in the fourth quarter. But the Bucs stopped North Caroline short on the two-point try, then picked up a couple of first downs over the final 4 minutes to melt the clock and seal the win.
"I think we've taken some steps," said Kent Island first-year head coach Zach Davis, who got a 16-carry, 123-yard rushing effort from Jaxson Hess against the Bulldogs. "We've been a streaky team; win three, lose three, and then we've won two.
"This team has been a work in progress, figuring out how do we have success because a lot of these guys are new starters," Davis added. "We bring back a ton of starters next year. But we're a young football team. Those growing pains showed in the middle of the season. We're getting better and that's what you want to see."
Queen Anne's head coach Brian Mooney has learned a lot about pain this season after losing a slew of starters to injuries, and then falling to Easton, 27-26, when Mikey O'Connor hit Chase Raab with a late touchdown pass on a fourth-and-five.
"The Easton game was a gut punch," Mooney said.
But it was the Lions delivering the gut punch last Friday by way of a 21-20 victory over Parkside.
Down 7-0, Queen Anne's (5-3) pulled even on John Connolly's 28-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. The Rams moved back in front in the third quarter, but again Connolly (season-high 27 carries, 156 yards rushing) answered, scoring on a 3-yard run. But Parkside maintained a slim lead when the Lions missed the point-after attempt.
Parkside extended its lead to 20-13 on a 70-yard touchdown pass. The Lions again looked poised to respond, only to fumble the ball away inside the Rams' 5-yard line. But Queen Anne's senior linebacker Parker Whiteford came through with one of the season's biggest plays when he made a tackle for a safety, drawing the Lions with 20-15.
Aided by Ja'Dereon Thompson's 33-yard completion to Jamison Woodward, Queen Anne's drove 60 yards, with Thompson scoring on a 4-yard run with a little over a minute to play giving the Lions a 21-20 victory.
"It was a nail-biter for sure," Mooney said. "It's huge. A confidence booster. Just again the resiliency. But we're going to scratch and claw just like we have all year."
Though is took a little while, Colonel Richardson appears to have found its groove.
Ja'Zir Dickerson carried 10 times for 175 yards and three touchdowns, and Derrick Mitchell had 100 yards on 11 touches during last Friday's 44-0 rout of Kent County, the Colonels' fourth straight win.
"We coach them each week to stay true to themselves and follow the system that we run," said Colonel head coach James Jackson, his team now 5-3. "Our backs I feel like are finally starting to follow our linemen, not trying to kick out too soon, or over-run the hole."
While the Colonel's running attack has impressed over the past four weeks, so has its defense, notching a pair of shutouts.
"Can we be better? Yes," Jackson said. "I think we need better play from our two d-tackles. Our d-ends have to contain a little better. Our linebackers, we've got to flow a little better. But the last four weeks they've been bent but they haven't been broken."

title: Easton's fast start too much for Bennett
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Easton's fast start too much for Bennett

 October 25, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 EASTON — It may have been the most efficient offensive performance produced by Easton High's football team this season.The Warriors scored on all six of their first-half possessions, then scored the first time they had the ball in the second half Friday night en route to a 49-31 victory over James M. Bennett.
Easton improved to 6-2, strengthening its hold on the No. 2 seed in the approaching Class 2A East playoffs behind undefeated and defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur (8-0).
"We did very well in the first half," Warrior head coach Matt Griffith said. "We came out and I thought we did well in the second half, too. I think we went down and scored pretty quickly. Senior night, try to get a lot of players in and do some different things. But no matter who's in the game, we've got to learn to finish."
Senior quarterback Mikey O'Connor's 6-yard touchdown run around left end and Dom Stanco's point-after kick moved Easton to a 49-10 lead with 9 minutes, 20 seconds remaining in the third quarter, setting the running clock in motion.
The Warriors carried that 39-point cushion into the fourth quarter before the Clippers (3-5) got a pair of touchdown passes from Liam Nelson as part of a 21-point closing surge. But Easton's opening onslaught proved too much for Bennett to overcome.
Dustin Blue carried 17 times for 115 yards and scored on touchdown runs of 1, 1 and 11 yards in the first quarter to help Easton build a 21-3 lead.
"Dustin ran great tonight," Griffith said. "Awesome. Dustin dictated the tempo and how we were going to play physical up front tonight."
Easton's passing game took over from there, as O'Connor connected with Colin Mooney down the center of the field for a 37-yard touchdown strike that extended the Warriors lead to 28-3 just 33 seconds into the second quarter.
O'Connor, who had 14 carries for a game-high 129 yards and a touchdown, completed 9 of 13 for 120 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.
"Just kind of taking what they gave us in how they tried to defend us," Griffith said.
Chase Raab hauled in a 17-yard touchdown pass with 8:44 still to go in the second quarter, widening Easton's lead to 35-3.
Bennett stopped Easton's scoring spree, when Zakai Smullen hit Jamareon Stevens for a 1-yard touchdown pass on fourth-and-goal with 4:25 left in the first half.
But Easton answered, as O'Connor hit Mooney for an 18-yard scoring play, pushing Easton's lead to 42-10 with 1:28 left in the first half.

title: Burnham has Vikings seemingly in all the right places
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Burnham has Vikings seemingly in all the right places

 October 25, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 467
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Rob Burnham deflects praise quite nicely."We got great kids. I'm not a good coach," Cambridge-South Dorchester High's first-year head football coach said. "All I've done is put people in places to be successful. I haven't done anything fancy."
Well, after Thursday night's 42-0 road victory at Washington, the Vikings have a fancy 8-0 record — the first time they've been unbeaten this deep into a season since 2000.
Despite his self evaluation, Burnham has proven to be a pretty good head coach, and has certainly put his personnel in the right spots offensively, as Cambridge-SD has outscored its last five opponents, 187-14.
Leading that charge has been junior running back Sterling Perkins, who has rushed for 902 yards and 10 touchdowns, and senior quarterback Anthony Hughes, who has 733 yards and a team-high 12 touchdowns on the ground, and has completed over 50% of his passes for 355 yards and seven touchdowns — two of those coming Thursday against the Jaguars.
But the Vikings have been equally, if not more impressive, on defense.
"The defense is definitely the strength of our team without question," Burnham said of a unit that has four players — KaMarii Stanley, Christen Dockins, Antonio Blueford and Tabrion Watts — with over 40 tackles apiece.
Hard to argue that considering Cambridge-SD has surrendered just one offensive touchdown over its last five games — that coming on an 8-yard run by Wicomico — and has shut out three of its last five opponents, including its last two.
"We've done pretty well defensively holding people," Burnham said. "Our kids play fast. We tackle well and drive the pile backwards. And we run fast to it."
That unit figures to face its stiffest test of the season next Friday when longtime rival Easton (5-2) comes to Cambridge for the regular-season finale for both teams.
"Easton brings a quality opponent to Cambridge next week," Burnham said. "They have some talent on offense that's pretty special and we have to be able to contain that. Our kids are going to be ready to play."
Burnham liked the way his team started for the most part against winless Washington. The Vikings scored on their first possession, committed a turnover, then scored the next three times they had the ball while building a 35-0 halftime lead.
Hughes was an efficient 4 of 5 passing for 65 yards and two touchdowns before being relieved by Nathan Twilley, who also had a scoring toss. Blueford, Ra'Quan Cornish and Tamyron Evans each had touchdown receptions, and William Jackson and Watts had one rushing touchdown apiece.
Still, Burnham said there's work to be done offensively.
"We have things we need to clean up offensively," Burnham said. "We're not anywhere near where I want to be offensively.
"Overall we blocked well. We finished well," Burnham said of Thursday's win. "But we have not played a complete game yet."

title: Boarders can now drop-in to new Terrapin Skate Park
author: ANDREA GRABENSTEIN agrabenstein@chespub.com
content:
Boarders can now drop-in to new Terrapin Skate Park

 October 25, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: ANDREA GRABENSTEIN agrabenstein@chespub.com | Section: Local News 
 
 380
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Giving skaters of all ages a local place to safely hone their skills, Queen Anne's County welcomed a ribbon cutting of Terrapin Skate Park in Stevensville Oct. 18.Complete with quarterpipes, ramps, rails, hubba ledges and more, Terrapin Skate Park is crafted to suit all level of skaters stands as the county's first permanent skatepark, according to Queen Anne's County Parks and Recreation Director Steve Chandlee.
Over two decades ago the parks department established a makeshift skating area but it was hidden away and not utilized well, he said.
Utilizing county owned property, an important aspect of the Terrapin Skate Park project was insuring it was in a visible location, Chandlee said.
In 2022, youths were instrumental in voicing a need to the commissioners and the Parks Advisory Board, including Kent Island High Schooler Dylan Cannon and Violet Baudean, who was a then seventh grader, created a petition highlighting the need for a skatepark.
"We knew upfront this was a great project," Chandlee said.
Now a Kent Island High School sophomore, Baudean is excited to share a love of skating with the community.
Public skateparks highlight a sense of community and offer an outlet for all ages, especially for those who don't drive, according to Baudean.
"There's something here for all skill levels, " she said.
Baudean credited county officials for their support of the project.
While skating is not a team sport, the skating community is very welcoming, always encouraging each other, Chandlee and Baudean said.
"It is a team of support for individuals," Chandlee said.
Funding for the park was made possible through a grant with the Department of Natural Resources Local Parks and Playground Infrastructure, he said.
Breaking ground in April, 12 weeks of construction opened the park to the public in June before stormwater management and tree planting completion officially welcomed the park, according to Chandlee.
More improvements are on the horizon for the park, including bleachers thanks to PRS Guitars and a restroom, he said.
The park has already become a welcome addition of the community with the hope to reach skaters far and wide.
"No matter what, try skateboarding," Baudean said.
Terrapin Skate Park is open sunrise to sunset and patrons are reminded to be respectful of the site and neighbors.
Cars are permitted in the designated parking area and should not be parked in the cul-de-sac or on the roadway.

title: Orrell nets equalizer, game-winner to lift Easton over Rams in double overtime
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Orrell nets equalizer, game-winner to lift Easton over Rams in double overtime

 October 24, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 614
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SALISBURY — It was a Warrior's cry."The story's not done," declared a member of Easton High's field hockey team before breaking the pregame huddle.
The Warriors did indeed extend their 2024 story Thursday afternoon. And as usual — at least when it comes to chapters with big games — they needed more than the usual amount of time to finish and deliver a happy ending.
Olivia Orrell scored the equalizer late in the fourth period, then knocked in the game-winner 1 minute, 52 seconds into the second overtime yesterday, lifting Easton to a 2-1 victory over No. 2 seed Parkside in a Class 2A East II semifinal.
Winners of six straight, the third-seeded Warriors (10-3) advance to Tuesday's 2A East II final at top-seeded Stephen Decatur (11-3).
"These girls never give up," said Easton head coach Kim Neff, whose team has played beyond regulation four times this season, losing a shootout to two-time Bayside champion Queen Anne's and beating perennial conference heavyweights Pocomoke and Kent Island in OT before yesterday's double-overtime thriller. "And as exhausted as they were, they never ever give up."
But Easton could have.
After a scoreless first half, the Warriors earned four penalty corners in the third period but couldn't beat Rams goalie Eden Hirsch. Easton continued applying pressure.
Then with 7:20 left in regulation, Parkside's Ava Holland converted a pass from Mady Bleile for a 1-0 Rams lead.
Neff immediately called time.
"I called time because I knew they were going to get in their own heads with that goal," Neff said of her team. "I knew I had to bring them back together as as unit and tell them we had seven minutes (in regulation). That's plenty of time to score and get ahead. And sure enough, they took that and within three minutes they were able to put one in the goal."
Easton surged into the circle and earned another corner. Hirsch made an initial save on the play. But Ryan Quicke gained possession and got the ball to Orrell, who tucked into the right corner of the cage with 3:52 remaining in regulation.
"When they scored the first goal, it put a drive in us to like dig deep," Orrell said. "Coach said we had it and she knew we had the energy. We just had the discipline. And the discipline I think as a team really got us through the game."
Easton's defense kept it a 1-1 tie through the first 10-minute overtime.
Freshman goalie Taylor Bowen (five saves) kicked away a sweeping backhand from Bleile 1:05 into the extra session. The Rams earned back-to-back corners but were denied, with Addie Knox making a clear on the second corner. Easton's Bis Johnson then swept away a ball inches from the goal line with 2 minutes remaining.
Hirsch answered, making a big save just 15 seconds later, forcing the game into a second OT.
The Warriors got two corners early, and capitalized on the second, as Orrell continuously hit at the ball before sneaking it into the back of the cage for the winner.
"Too many," Orrell answered when asked how many times she hit the ball before scoring. "We were really determined. We just got it in. It was great."
The Rams, who shut out Easton earlier in the season, finish 9-4.
"I think it was a great game from both sides," Parkside head coach Stephanie Cason said. "It just didn't fall in our favor."
KENT ISLAND 4 NORTH CAROLINE 0
STEVENSVILLE — Willow Yost scored two goals and set up a third as second-seeded Kent Island blanked the No. 3 seed Bulldogs.
The second-seeded Buccaneers (9-3-1) played at top-seed Queen Anne's (11-1-1) in the region final on Tuesday.
Ellie Burnside and Parker Tengwall each scored once for Kent Island. Goalie Brynja Petursson made seven saves.
